3.1.m: A sacred ford equal to this sacred ford has never been, nor will ever be.
This has been told to you, O brahmins: the grandeur of Lakṣmītīrtha,
which destroys bad dreams, is meritorious, and accomplishes all desired things.
Whatever man recites this chapter or hears it with devotion
shall become rich in wealth and grain; of this there is no doubt.
Having enjoyed all pleasures here, he shall obtain liberation at the end of the body.

3.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasyā saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe setumāhātmye lakṣmītīrthapraśaṃsāyāṃ dharmaputraniratiśayasaṃpadavāptivarṇanaṃnāmaikaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 21 ..
3.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्या संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतुमाहात्म्ये लक्ष्मीतीर्थप्रशंसायां धर्मपुत्रनिरतिशयसंपदवाप्तिवर्णनंनामैकविंशोऽध्यायः .. 21 ..
3.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, entitled 'Description of Dharmaputra's Attainment of Incomparable Wealth in the Praise of Lakṣmītīrtha', in the Setumāhātmya of the third Brahmakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Glorious Sūta said:
In the auspicious Lakṣmītīrtha, the sole cause of all sovereignty for men,
a man having bathed should then go to Agnitīrtha, O best of the twice-born.
Agnitīrtha is greatly meritorious, the destroyer of great sins,
the highest sacred ford among sacred fords, the sole instrument for fulfilling all desires.
There a man should bathe with devotion for the complete purification of his own sins.
The seers said:
How did it obtain renown as 'Agnitīrtha', O lord of sages?
Where is this Agnitīrtha, and what is its grandeur?
You ought to tell this in detail to us who are full of faith.
Glorious Sūta said:
Properly indeed have you asked; listen, O bulls among sages!

3.1.s: purā hi rāghavo hatvā rāvaṇaṃ saparicchadam .. 5 ..

3.1.m: Long ago, having slain Rāvaṇa along with his attendants,

3.1.m: and having installed Vibhīṣaṇa as lord in Laṅkā,
Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, accompanied by Sītā and the son of Sumitrā,
being praised by siddhas, cāraṇas, and gandharvas, by the gods and hosts of apsarases,
and by hosts of sages whose blessings are true, curious about sacred fords,
Rāma of irresistible prowess, effortlessly bearing his bow,
in order to establish his own purity and to test Jānakī,
along with the multitudes of gods led by Indra, with the sages and the ancestors,
accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa and by all the monkeys,
came by way of the causeway to Mount Gandhamādana.
Stationed on the shore of Lakṣmītīrtha to test Jānakī,
he invoked Agni in the presence of the celestial seers and the ancestors.
Then, [Agni] arose from the great ocean, not far from Lakṣmītīrtha.
while all the worlds looked on, the purifier [Agni] arose, licking the waters,
his eyes coppery-red, clad in yellow garments, and holding a bow. (12)
Licking the ten directions with his seven tongues,
and seeing the heroic lord of the Raghus, who had assumed a human form in sport, (13)
he spoke these pleasing words to attest the purity of Jānakī:
“O Rāma, Rāma, mighty-armed one, terror of the rākṣasas! (14)
You have slain Rāvaṇa through the chastity of Jānakī.

3.1.s: satyaṃsatyaṃ punaḥ satyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 15 ..
3.1.d: सत्यंसत्यं पुनः सत्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 15 ..
3.1.m: Truly, truly, and again truly, let there be no doubt on this matter. (15)
She is Kamalā, the mother of the universe, who has assumed a human form in sport.
When [you assume] divinity, she assumes a divine body; and in humanity, she is human. (16)
Indeed, she fashions her own body to conform with the body of Viṣṇu.
Whenever, O Lord of the universe, God of gods, Janārdana, (17)
you take descents, she is then your companion.
When you were Rāma the descendant of Bhṛgu, she was the Earth; (18)

3.1.s: adhunā jānakī jātā bhavitrī rukmiṇī tataḥ ..
3.1.d: अधुना जानकी जाता भवित्री रुक्मिणी ततः ..
3.1.m: now she is born as Jānakī, and next she will be Rukmiṇī.
In other descents too, she is the companion of Viṣṇu. (19)
Therefore, O Rāghava, accept her at my word.”

3.1.m: Having heard those words of the purifier [Agni], the gods, great seers, (20)
vidyādharas, gandharvas, men, and serpents,
and other hosts of beings, praised Rāma the son of Daśaratha, (21)
as well as Jānakī, the princess of Mithilā, again and again.
At Agni’s word, Rāma accepted the stainless Sītā. (22)
Thus, for the sake of Sītā’s purity, by Rāma of untiring deeds,
when the invocation was performed, the fire [rose] not far from Lakṣmītīrtha. (23)
O best of brahmins, from that place in the ocean where he rose up,
know that peerless place to be Agnitīrtha. (24)
Because Agni came forth from there, it is called Agnitīrtha.

3.1.s: atra snātvā naro bhaktyā vahnestīrthe vimuktide .. 25 ..

3.1.m: He should give them garments, wealth, land, and an adorned maiden. (26)
Freed from all sins, he attains union with Viṣṇu.
On this bank of Agnitīrtha, the gift of food is especially praised. (27)

3.1.m: There was never, nor will there ever be, a sacred ford equal to Agnitīrtha,
where even Duṣpaṇya, a great sinner, by bathing, cast off his dreadful ghosthood (28)
and attained a celestial form.
In ancient times, there lived in Pāṭaliputra a vaiśya named Paśumān. (29)

3.1.m: He was ever devoted to righteousness and intent on worshipping brahmins,

To that vaiśya three sons were born of the third [wife],
famed as Mahāpaṇya, Mahākośa, and Duṣpaṇya. (34)
Thus, O best of brahmins, to that vaiśya Paśumān
there were eight sons born from those three wives. (35)

3.1.m: Led by Supaṇya, all those sons grew up in due course.
Playing in the dust, they delighted their parents. (36)
In time, those sons of the vaiśya reached the age of five years.
Paśumān, the chief of vaiśyas, (37)
trained all those sons continuously from childhood in their own duties.
Trained gradually in the tasks of agriculture, cattle protection, and trade, (38)
the seven [sons], led by Supaṇya, obeyed their father's command.
Whatever duty Paśumān spoke of, they performed it immediately. (39)
They attained great skill even in goldsmith work.
Duṣpaṇya, however, the eighth son, continuously from his childhood (40)
became devoted to evil ways and did not heed his father's words.
Starting from the time of playing in the dust, he was devoted to evil ways. (41)
Even while a boy, that son harassed other boys.
Seeing him devoted to evil deeds, his father Paśumant likewise,
simply overlooked it, saying, “He is just an ignorant child.”
Then all eight sons of the merchant reached youth.
Among them, this eighth son, Duṣpaṇya, the foremost of the strong,
seized the boys living in the city by the hands and throats,

3.1.m: No one among the people knew of this evil conduct of his.
He threw them into the water until those boys died.
The fathers and mothers of those dead boys
searched for them everywhere through all the towns.
And seeing their sons dead, the people could only weep aloud.
Then, having seen the corpses in the waters, the people performed the proper rites.
Killing boys in the city in this manner every day,
Duṣpaṇya continued thus for a long time, unnoticed even by the people.
As boys were dying because of the merchant's son's deed,
the city became almost desolate due to the lack of growth among the citizens.
Then, having assembled, the citizens reported that matter to the king.
Hearing their words, the king summoned the village guardians
and commanded: “Let the cause of the boys' deaths be investigated!”
The village guardians agreed, saying, “So be it,” and, posted here and there,
they thoroughly searched for the cause of the slaughter of the boys.
Though searching, they did not discover the killer of the boys.
Approaching the king again, they spoke fearfully:
“O King, though we search, we do not discover
who it is that lives in the city and continually kills the boys.”

3.1.m: And again, all the citizens, distressed, approached the king;
choked with tears, they spoke again of the death of their children.
Not knowing the cause of it, the king remained silent, deep in thought.
Once this merchant's son, together with five little boys,
went near a pond under the pretext of gathering lotuses.
Seizing those boys by force while they cried out,
the cruel-hearted Duṣpaṇya submerged them in the neck-deep water of the lake.

3.1.m: Thinking them dead, Duṣpaṇya quickly went to his home.
The fathers of those five searched for their sons in the city.
While they were searching, the five very young boys thrown by him into the waters,
did not die, by stroke of chance.
Slowly reaching the shore, all five of them, their heads soaked,
were unable to go to the city and wandered right there out of childishness.
Hearing their names called from afar by their kinsmen,
all five boys called back in response.
Then their fathers, hearing them, came to the lake shore,
and seeing their sons alive, experienced incomparable joy.
When questioned by their fathers and elders, “What happened?”
the boys reported the wicked deed of Duṣpaṇya to their kinsmen.
Then the citizens, having learned the fact, approached the king
and reported the deed of Duṣpaṇya as told by the five [boys].
Then the king summoned Paśumant, the foremost merchant,
and spoke these words while the citizens were listening:
The king said:
“O Paśumant, see how this city of abundant folk
has been rendered nearly desolate by your wicked-minded son named Duṣpaṇya!
Just now, indeed, he plunged these innocent children into the water;
and by good fortune they have returned alive to the city.

Today I ask you yourself, since you are devoted to dharma.”
Thus addressed by the king, Paśumant, who knew dharma, spoke fitting words:
Paśumant said:
“He who has emptied the city deserves nothing less than death.

"For this is no son of mine, but a foe who commits dreadful sins;

3.1.m: Having heard the words of Paśumān, all the citizens
praised the excellent merchant and spoke thus to the king:
"Let not this wicked one be put to death; let him quietly be banished from the city."
Then the king summoned Duṣpaṇya and spoke thus:
"You wicked soul, depart swiftly from this country at once!
If you remain right here, I shall certainly punish you with death."
Having been thus reprimanded by the king and banished from the city by messengers,
Duṣpaṇya, abandoning that country in fear,
then went to a forest crowded with assemblies of sages.
Even there, he drowned a son of a sage in the water.
The sons of the sages, having come to play and seeing the dead child,
approached his father and told him, deeply grieved.

3.1.s: tata ugraśravāḥ śrutvā tebhyaḥ putraṃ jale mṛtam .. 78 ..

3.1.m: Then Ugraśravas, hearing from them that his son had died in the water,
perceived through the power of his austerity that it was the deed of Duṣpaṇya.
Ugraśravas cursed that Duṣpaṇya, the son of the vaiśya:
Ugraśravas said:
"Since you have thrown my son into the water and killed him,
may your death also come about by drowning in water!
And when you are dead, you shall become a piśāca for a very long time."

3.1.s: iti śāpe śrute sadyo duṣpaṇyaḥ khinnamānasaḥ .. 81 ..

3.1.m: When that curse was heard, Duṣpaṇya, dejected at heart,
at once abandoned that forest and went to another, dreadful forest,
abounding in fierce beasts such as lions. When he reached that other forest,
a great tempest wind blew, feeling like a thunderbolt's strike,
raining down a great shower of dust and constantly breaking down trees.
And there was an unbearable rain tearing at his limbs with its velocity.
Seeing that, Duṣpaṇya, reflecting and sorely distressed,
beheld a dead, dried-up elephant of enormous size.
Unable then to endure the great wind and the heavy downpour,
he entered the cavity of its belly through the opening of the elephant's mouth.
No sooner had he entered than the rain became exceedingly heavy.
Then, from all the rainwater, a tremendous flood arose;
that flood became a kind of river in that forest.
Then, with its belly filled by those rainwaters,
that elephant, floating in the great torrent, became swollen shut.
Then, from the belly of that elephant which had no opening left

3.1.s: gajasya jaṭharātso'yaṃ nirgaṃtu na śaśāka ha .. 89 ..
3.1.d: गजस्य जठरात्सोऽयं निर्गंतु न शशाक ह .. 89 ..
3.1.m: and whose belly was filled with water, he was indeed unable to come out.
And then the torrent of rainwater, possessed of terrifying velocity,
carried the elephant, with Duṣpaṇya inside its belly, to the ocean.
Duṣpaṇya, submerged in the water, was in an instant deprived of life.
As soon as he died, Duṣpaṇya attained the state of a piśāca.
Afflicted by hunger and thirst, he took refuge in an impassable forest,
crying out terrifyingly during the dreadful hot seasons.
He stayed in the dense wilderness, experiencing many sorrows,
for tens of millions of thousands of kalpas, and hundreds of tens of millions of kalpas.
That piśāca lived in the dreadful forest, suffering great misery,
running from one forest to another, and likewise from country to country.
Experiencing sorrow everywhere, he eventually came to the Daṇḍaka forest.
Wandering not far from the sacred hermitage of Agastya,
roaring a terrifying roar, he spoke aloud these words:
"O ascetics, listen all of you to my words!
For you are compassionate and devoted to the welfare of all beings;
look upon me with a gaze of compassion and favor me, who am exceedingly afflicted by sorrows!
Formerly I was a vaiśya named Duṣpaṇya in Pāṭaliputra,
the son of Paśumān, and I murdered many children.
Then, banished from that land by the king, I went to a forest.
There I killed the son of the sage Ugraśravas in the water.

3.1.s: sa munirdatta vāñchāpaṃ mamāpi maraṇaṃ jale ..
3.1.d: स मुनिर्दत्त वाञ्छापं ममापि मरणं जले ..
3.1.m: That sage pronounced a curse upon me that my death also should be in water.
And he inflicted on me the terrible state of a piśāca, full of immense suffering.
For thousands of millions of kalpas, and hundreds of millions of kalpas as well,
this state of a piśāca has been endured by me in desolate forest lands.

3.1.m: I am not able to endure this thirst and hunger.
Therefore, out of compassion, please protect me, who am suffering greatly.
O ascetics, act in such a way that I may be freed from this piśāca state!

3.1.m: Having heard this plea of the piśāca, those rich in austerity

The ascetics said:

3.1.m: For you alone are capable of saving such sinners.
Agastya, having heard them, was filled with supreme compassion.
Having summoned his dear disciple Sutīkṣṇa, he spoke these words:
Agastya said:
O Sutīkṣṇa, go swiftly to Mount Gandhamādana.
There is a great sacred ford named Agnitīrtha, which destroys sins.
O noble-minded one, bathe there for the purpose of liberating the piśāca.
When you have bathed there for the piśāca's sake, preceded by a formal vow (saṃkalpa),
he will cast off the state of a piśāca and attain divinity.
I see no expiation for him without resorting to that sacred ford.
Therefore, O Sutīkṣṇa, out of compassion save this piśāca!
Thus addressed by Agastya, Sutīkṣṇa, that ocean of compassion,
having reached Gandhamādana, made a formal vow at Agnitīrtha for the piśāca's sake,
and bathed there for the piśāca's sake according to rule for three days.
Having worshipped Rāmanātha and other deities, and having taken water of that sacred ford,
Sutīkṣṇa, the best of brahmins, then returned to his hermitage.
Immediately upon being sprinkled with [the water of] that sacred ford, [the spirit] was freed from the state of a piśāca,
and by the power of that sacred ford instantly attained divinity.
Mounting an excellent aerial chariot, surrounded by celestial women,
he bowed repeatedly to Sutīkṣṇa, Agastya, and the other ascetics,
and having taken leave of them, full of joy,
he swiftly ascended to heaven itself, worshipped even by the gods.
By the māhātmya of Agnitīrtha, Duṣpaṇya, the son of the vaiśya,
abandoned the piśāca state born of the curse and thus attained divinity.

3.1.s: evaṃ vaḥ kathitaṃ viprā agnitīrthasya vaibhavam .. 16 ..
3.1.d: एवं वः कथितं विप्रा अग्नितीर्थस्य वैभवम् .. 16 ..
3.1.m: Thus has the glory of Agnitīrtha been told to you, O brahmins.
Whoever recites this chapter or listens to it with devotion—
this narrative of the liberation of the piśāca—is freed from all sins.
Having enjoyed great delights in this world, he obtains happiness in the next world as well.

Glorious Sūta said:
Having performed a ritual ablution in the sacred ford named Agnitīrtha, which destroys all sins,

3.1.s: snānaṃ kṛtvā viśuddhātmā cakratīrthaṃ tato vrajet .. 1 ..
3.1.d: स्नानं कृत्वा विशुद्धात्मा चक्रतीर्थं ततो व्रजेत् .. 1 ..
3.1.m: one should then proceed, with a purified self, to Cakratīrtha.
Whatever desire a mortal aims for, O best of brahmins,
when performing a ritual ablution at Cakratīrtha, that very desire he attains.
Formerly, a great seer named Ahirbudhnya, strict in his vows,
an ascetic, worshipped Sudarśana on this Gandhamādana [mountain].
While the sage was performing austerities there, rākṣasas of terrible forms,
intent solely on obstructing austerities, constantly harassed him, O brahmins.
Then Sudarśana, having arrived there out of a desire to protect his devotee,
effortlessly struck down the tormenting demons of old.
From that time forward, O brahmins, that discus [Sudarśana], at the request of the devotee,
constantly established its presence in the sacred ford made by Ahirbudhnya.
From that time forward, that sacred ford is called Cakratīrtha.
By the grace of Sudarśana, through plunging into that sacred ford,
affliction caused by rakṣases, piśācas, and others never occurs at all.
Having bathed in this purifying sacred ford in ancient times, the sun god Ravi, whose hands had been cut off,
obtained two hands made of gold by the glory of this sacred ford.
The seers said:
How did Āditya's hands come to be cut off, O son of Sūta?

3.1.s: yathā ca labdhavānpāṇī sauvarṇau tadvadasva naḥ .. 9 ..
3.1.d: यथा च लब्धवान्पाणी सौवर्णौ तद्वदस्व नः .. 9 ..
3.1.m: And tell us how he obtained golden hands.
Glorious Sūta said:
Formerly, the gods, led by Indra, were continually afflicted by the Daityas.

3.1.m: Pondering, "What shall we do?", they assembled and deliberated together.
Placing Bṛhaspati at their head, having deliberated for a long time, the gods,
putting Turāṣāh at their forefront, went to the abode of the Self-born.

3.1.s: te brahmāṇaṃ samāsādya dṛṣṭvā stutvā ca bhaktitaḥ .. 12 ..

3.1.m: Having approached Brahmā, seen him, and praised him with devotion,
they then informed him of the purpose of their arrival.
The gods said:
"O Lord, husband of Bhāratī, the Daityas, exceedingly arrogant with might,

3.1.s: bādhaṃte satataṃ deva tatra brūhi pratikriyām ..
3.1.d: बाधंते सततं देव तत्र ब्रूहि प्रतिक्रियाम् ..
3.1.m: continually oppress us, O God! Tell us the remedy for this."

3.1.s: ityuktaḥ sa surairbrahmā tānāha kṛpayā vacaḥ .. 14 ..
3.1.d: इत्युक्तः स सुरैर्ब्रह्मा तानाह कृपया वचः .. 14 ..
3.1.m: Addressed thus by the gods, Brahmā spoke words to them with compassion:
Brahmā said:
"Do not fear, O gods! I will tell you the means in this matter.
A great sacrifice sacred to Maheśvara, which brings destruction to the asuras,
you, O gods, together with sages who see the truth, should begin.

3.1.s: ayaṃ ca daivataiḥ sarvairvidhilobhaṃ vinā kṛtaḥ .. 16 ..
3.1.d: अयं च दैवतैः सर्वैर्विधिलोभं विना कृतः .. 16 ..
3.1.m: And let this sacrifice sacred to Maheśvara, performed by all the deities without desire to curtail ritual rules,
be celebrated on Mount Gandhamādana.
For if they were to perform that sacrifice elsewhere, O best of gods,
then the wicked-minded enemies of the gods would cause obstacles to the sacrifice.
If this sacrifice is performed on Mount Gandhamādana,
then through the favor of Sudarśana, no obstacle will arise at all.
To grant favor to the great seer named Ahirbudhnya on Gandhamādana,
Sudarśana is present in that sacred ford.

3.1.s: ataḥ kurudhvaṃ bho yūyaṃ taṃ yajñaṃ gaṃdhamādane .. 3.1.23.20 ..
3.1.d: अतः कुरुध्वं भो यूयं तं यज्ञं गंधमादने .. 3.1.23.20 ..
3.1.m: Therefore, O gods, perform that sacrifice on Gandhamādana,
which destroys the asuras, not far from Cakratīrtha."
Then, at the word of Brahmā, they quickly went to Gandhamādana,
placing Bṛhaspati at their head, desirous of performing the sacrifice.
Having bowed to the great-souled Ahirbudhnya, lord of sages,
they prepared the sacrificial enclosure not far from his hermitage.
Together with those whose wealth is austerity, experts in sacrificial rites,
the gods commenced the sacrifice that destroys the asuras.
In that rite, Bṛhaspati himself was the hotṛ;
Jayanta, son of Pākaśāsana, was the maitrāvaruṇa;
the eighth Vasu of the Vasus was the acchāvāka;
Parāśara, son of Śakti, was the grāvastut;
Aṣṭāvakra of great fiery energy bore the yoke of the adhvaryu;
the great sage Viśvāmitra was the pratiprasthātṛ;

3.1.s: neṣṭā babhūva varuṇa unnetā ca dhaneśvaraḥ .. 27 ..
3.1.d: नेष्टा बभूव वरुण उन्नेता च धनेश्वरः .. 27 ..
3.1.m: Varuṇa was the neṣṭṛ, and the lord of wealth was the unnetṛ;
Savitṛ was the brahmā, bearing half the yoke of the sacrifice;
Vasiṣṭha, foremost of knowers of the Veda, was the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin;
Śunaḥśepa was the āgnīdhra, and the sacrificial fire was the potṛ;
Vāyu was the udgātṛ, and the king of the departed was the prastotṛ;
Agastya, jar-born, was the pratihartṛ;
the great Madhucchandas, son of Viśvāmitra, was the subrahmaṇya;
Purandara, king of the gods, was himself the patron of the sacrifice;
and the sage Śuka, son of Vyāsa, was the upadraṣṭṛ.
Then all those priests duly consecrated
Purandara, king of the gods, in that sacrifice sacred to Maheśvara.
Thus the great sacrifice proceeded indeed on Gandhamādana.
Greatly afflicted by the unbearable majesty of Sudarśana,
the asuras found no flaw there as the sacrifice proceeded.
Thus, free from hindrance, that great sacrifice went on.
And there the sacrificial fire, carrying the oblation, blazed, consuming the offerings.
Having duly performed the series of rites without agitation,
the adhvaryu poured the sacrificial cake, purified by mantras, into the fire.
Having reverently divided the remainder of the sacrificial cake offered in the fire,
the adhvaryu gave the sin-destroying portions to the priests, headed by the hotṛ.
And to Savitṛ, the brahmā, one portion of exceedingly fierce brilliance,
the share of the sacrificial cake named prāśitra, he gave there.
Then Savitṛ took the prāśitra with both hands.
As soon as it was touched by Savitṛ, that unapproachable prāśitra portion
severed his hands while all the officiating priests were watching.
Then, his hands severed by the prāśitra possessing terrible fiery energy,
he was terrified, saying, "What is this?", with a downcast face.
Calling together all the officiating priests, Savitṛ said this:
Savitṛ said:
"This portion of the puroḍāśa named prāśitra
was given to me, yet it severed my hands even while you were looking on.

3.1.s: ato bhavaṃtaḥ saṃbhūya sarva eva hi ṛtvijaḥ .. 42 ..
3.1.d: अतो भवंतः संभूय सर्व एव हि ऋत्विजः .. 42 ..
3.1.m: Therefore, all of you officiating priests coming together
must restore these two hands, or else I shall destroy this sacrifice."
Hearing Savitṛ's words, they all deliberated.

3.1.m: There in the midst of the foremost sages and all the gods,
Aṣṭāvakra, endowed with great fiery energy, spoke to those officiating priests.
Aṣṭāvakra said:
"Listen with collected minds to my word, all you officiating priests:

3.1.s: mayi jīvati vipreṃdrā viriṃcānāṃ śataṃ gatam .. 45 ..
3.1.d: मयि जीवति विप्रेंद्रा विरिंचानां शतं गतम् .. 45 ..
3.1.m: while I have lived, O foremost brahmins, a hundred Viriñcas have passed away.
Tens of millions of four-faced [Brahmās] are born and die,
and watching them all, I have maintained my life.
During the tenure of a Prajāpati named Lokeśvara,
a brahmin named Harihara was residing in Śyāmalāpura.
By a forest-dwelling hunter who was shooting at a target for sport,
his feet were cut off with arrows as he stepped into the middle of the target.
Having gone to Gandhamādana, impelled then by sages,
and having bathed in this Munitīrtha, he regained his feet in ancient times.
Then, this sacred ford was called Munitīrtha;
now it is known as Cakratīrtha, having acquired the name of the Discus.
Therefore, let a bath be taken here by him whose hands were severed by the prāśitra,
even by Savitṛ in Munitīrtha, if it pleases you."
Thus addressed by the great seer Aṣṭāvakra,
the officiating priests, all overjoyed, spoke to Savitṛ:

bathed there in order to regain his hands, [in that ford] which grants desired wishes.

3.1.m: Even as he was rising after bathing there with devotion,
he was seen endowed with two golden hands.
Seeing him golden-handed, all the officiating priests rejoiced.

3.1.m: Then, having completed that sacrifice and having conquered the hosts of Daityas,
all the gods headed by Indra happily returned to heaven.
Therefore, having arrived at this sacred ford, by all human beings
it should be resorted to with effort for the attainment of their respective desires:
by the blind, the crippled-handed, the mute, the deaf, the hunchbacked,
by the limping and the lame, and by others deprived of limbs,
those whose hands and feet are severed, and those who have lost other bodily parts,
by men and others as well, for the restoration of deficient limbs,
this sacred ford, granter of all desired things, should be resorted to.
Thus the majesty of Cakratīrtha has been told to you, O brahmins,

3.1.s: yatra snātvā purā chinnau pāṇī prāpa prabhākaraḥ .. 61 ..
3.1.d: यत्र स्नात्वा पुरा छिन्नौ पाणी प्राप प्रभाकरः .. 61 ..
3.1.m: where formerly, having bathed, the Light-maker regained his severed hands.
Whoever recites this chapter or listens to it attentively,
his deficient limbs will become whole, without doubt;
for a mortal desiring liberation, liberation will ensue—there is no doubt about this.

3.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe setumāhātmye cakratīrthapraśaṃsāyāmādityahiraṇmayapāṇyavāptivarṇanaṃnāma trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 23 .. .. cha ..

The venerable Sūta said:

3.1.s: cakratīrthe naraḥ snātvā śivatīrthaṃ tato vrajet ..
3.1.d: चक्रतीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा शिवतीर्थं ततो व्रजेत् ..
3.1.m: Having bathed at Cakratīrtha, a man should then proceed to Śivatīrtha,
where, by mere ritual ablution, tens of millions of heinous sins
and associations with them are destroyed that very moment, O ascetics.
Having bathed here, Kālabhairava was released from the sin of killing a brahmin.
The seers said:
How did the killing of a brahmin come upon Kālabhairava Rudra, O great sage?
For what reason did it occur, O Sūta? You ought to tell us that here.
Śrī Sūta said:
All sages, I will relate an ancient event that grants liberation,
By the mere hearing of which one is freed from all sins. // 4
Formerly, a dispute arose between Prajāpati [Brahmā] and Viṣṇu
Over a certain matter, in the presence of all beings: // 5
"I alone am the creator of the universe; there is no other creator whatsoever.
I am the bestower of restraint and grace upon all the manifold creations. // 6
There is no one superior to me, nor equal to me, even among the gods."

3.1.s: evaṃ sa manute brahmā devānāṃ sannidhau purā .. 7 ..
3.1.d: एवं स मनुते ब्रह्मा देवानां सन्निधौ पुरा .. 7 ..
3.1.m: Thus did Brahmā think in the presence of the gods in former times. // 7
Then Nārāyaṇa, laughing, spoke, O best of twice-born [sages]:
"Why do you speak thus now out of egoism? // 8

3.1.s: vākyamevaṃvidhaṃ bhūyo vaktuṃ nārhasi vai vidhe ..
3.1.d: वाक्यमेवंविधं भूयो वक्तुं नार्हसि वै विधे ..
3.1.m: You ought not to utter such words again, O Vidhi [Brahmā].
I alone am the creator of the world, sacrifice [itself], Nārāyaṇa, the omnipresent lord. // 9

3.1.s: māṃ vināsya prapañcasya jīvanaṃ durlabhaṃ bhavet ..
3.1.d: मां विनास्य प्रपञ्चस्य जीवनं दुर्लभं भवेत् ..
3.1.m: Without me, the existence of this universe would be impossible.
By my grace has this world, both motionless and moving, been created by you." // 10
While Brahmā and Viṣṇu, each seeking victory, were thus disputing,
The four Vedas came there before the gods
And spoke these true words, revealing the ultimate reality. // 11
The Vedas said:

3.1.s: tvaṃ viṣṇo na jagatkartā na tvaṃ brahmanprajāpate .. 12 ..
3.1.d: त्वं विष्णो न जगत्कर्ता न त्वं ब्रह्मन्प्रजापते .. 12 ..
3.1.m: "You, O Viṣṇu, are not the creator of the universe, nor are you, O Brahmā Prajāpati! // 12
Rather, Īśvara is the creator of the universe, higher than the highest, the all-pervading lord.
This world of moving and motionless things has been fashioned by his power of Māyā. // 13
Indeed, Sāmba, characterized by truth and other virtues, is worthy of reverence by all gods;

3.1.s: sraṣṭā ca pālako hartā sa eva jagatāṃ prabhuḥ ..14..
3.1.d: स्रष्टा च पालको हर्ता स एव जगतां प्रभुः ..14..
3.1.m: He alone is the creator, protector, and destroyer, the lord of the worlds." // 14

3.1.s: evaṃ samīritaṃ vedaiḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ śubhākṣaram..
3.1.d: एवं समीरितं वेदैः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं शुभाक्षरम्..
3.1.m: Having heard those words composed of auspicious syllables uttered by the Vedas,
Brahmā and Viṣṇu then said there, O best of twice-born [sages]: // 15
Brahmā and Viṣṇu said:
"Embraced by Pārvatī, embodied, the master of the Pramathas—
How can Śambhu be the supreme Brahman, free from all attachment?" // 16

3.1.s: tābhyāmitīrite tatra praṇavaḥ prāha tau tadā ..
3.1.d: ताभ्यामितीरिते तत्र प्रणवः प्राह तौ तदा ..
3.1.m: When this was spoken by the two, the Praṇava (Oṃkāra) then spoke to them,
Though formless, having assumed a form, with a mighty voice, O twice-born: // 17
The Praṇava said:
"This Śambhu, Mahādeva, never sports with a Pārvatī
Who is distinct from himself, but with one who is of his own essential nature. // 18
This Śambhu has no ruler above him (anīśāna), self-luminous, taintless;
Mahādeva transcends the universe; he is declared in scripture as 'transcending the universe.' // 19
He is the self of all, the maker of all, independent, the cause of the being of all.
O Brahmā, at the time of creation he appoints you by means of the quality of rajas. // 20
O Keśava, Śambhu sends you forth with the quality of sattva for the purpose of protection,
And he directs the one named Kālarudra with tamas at the time of dissolution. // 21
Therefore, O Viṣṇu, there is never independence for you two,

3.1.s: nāpi prajāpaterasti kiṃ tu śaṃbhoḥ svatantratā .. 22 ..
3.1.d: नापि प्रजापतेरस्ति किं तु शंभोः स्वतन्त्रता .. 22 ..
3.1.m: Nor is it Prajāpati's; rather, independence belongs to Śambhu alone. // 22

3.1.s: brahmanviṣṇo yuvābhyāṃ tu kimarthaṃ na maheśvaraḥ ..
3.1.d: ब्रह्मन्विष्णो युवाभ्यां तु किमर्थं न महेश्वरः ..
3.1.m: O Brahmā, O Viṣṇu, why indeed is Maheśvara not recognized
By you two as the creator of all worlds and likewise surpassing the universe? // 23
Even that power, the goddess Umā, is never separate from Śaṃkara;
The goddess consists of the bliss of Śambhu; she is not considered incidental. // 24
Therefore Rudra transcends the universe, independent, free from conceptual distinction;
This Śaṃkara is to be worshipped by all gods, and by both of you as well. // 25
There is no maker of this Rudra, nor is anyone found superior to him;
Nor is an equal to him found across hundreds of worlds. // 26

3.1.s: ato mohaṃ na kurutaṃ brahmaviṣṇo yuvāṃ vṛthā ..
3.1.d: अतो मोहं न कुरुतं ब्रह्मविष्णो युवां वृथा ..
3.1.m: Therefore, do not maintain delusion in vain, O Brahmā and Viṣṇu!"

3.1.s: ityuktaṃ praṇavenātha śrutvā brahmā ca keśavaḥ .. 27 ..
3.1.d: इत्युक्तं प्रणवेनाथ श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा च केशवः .. 27 ..
3.1.m: Having heard what was thus spoken by the Praṇava, Brahmā and Keśava, // 27
Deluded by the Māyā of Śambhu, did not cast off their ignorance at all.
In the meantime, Brahmā beheld a great wonder: // 28
Pervading the entire sky, resembling countless suns,
An orb of light standing in the midst of the atmosphere, facing in all directions. // 29
In order to examine it, Brahmā emitted an upward-facing head;
With that fifth head created by the power of his austerity, he, // 30
The lord, continuously examined that orb of light.
That face flared up with anger from gazing upon that light. // 31
Resembling endless suns, that fifth head was blazing;
it shone like the submarine fire desiring to burn the worlds at the cosmic dissolution. // 32
And from that splendour was seen a blue-and-red person.

3.1.s: dṛṣṭvā sraṣṭā tadā brahmā babhāṣe parameśvaram .. 33 ..
3.1.d: दृष्ट्वा स्रष्टा तदा ब्रह्मा बभाषे परमेश्वरम् .. 33 ..
3.1.m: Seeing [him], Brahmā the creator then spoke to Parameśvara: // 33

3.1.s: vedāhaṃ tvāṃ mahādeva lalāṭānme purā bhavān ..
3.1.d: वेदाहं त्वां महादेव ललाटान्मे पुरा भवान् ..
3.1.m: “I know you, Mahādeva. Formerly you
came forth from my forehead, O Śambhu, my son named Rudra.” // 34

3.1.s: iti garveṇa saṃyuktaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā maheśvaraḥ ..
3.1.d: इति गर्वेण संयुक्तं वचः श्रुत्वा महेश्वरः ..
3.1.m: Hearing this speech filled with arrogance, Maheśvara
then sent forth a person named Kālabhairava. // 35
Kālabhairava fought for a long time with Brahmā—
he who arose as a portion of Mahādeva, bearing a trident, a chisel, and a mace. // 36

3.1.s: yuddhvā tu suciraṃ kālaṃ brahmaṇā kālabhairavaḥ ..
3.1.d: युद्ध्वा तु सुचिरं कालं ब्रह्मणा कालभैरवः ..
3.1.m: Having fought for a very long time with Brahmā, Kālabhairava
looked upon the bright fifth face of Brahmā. // 37
Beholding the upward-facing fifth mouth of the husband of Bhāratī
filled with immense pride, he blazed forth, exceedingly enraged. // 38
Then Bhairava severed that fifth head in fury.
Thereupon that Brahmā died, slain by Kālabhairava. // 39
By the grace of Īśvara, he regained life once more.
Then he looked upon Śaṃkara, adorned with the moon, // 40
adorned with ornaments of the eight serpent kings, Vāsuki and the rest.

3.1.s: dṛṣṭvā vedhā mahādevaṃ pārvatyā saha śaṃkaram .. 41 ..
3.1.d: दृष्ट्वा वेधा महादेवं पार्वत्या सह शंकरम् .. 41 ..
3.1.m: Seeing Mahādeva, Śaṃkara together with Pārvatī, // 41
the creator attained knowledge pertaining to Maheśvara through the grace of Mahādeva.
Then he praised Giriśa, the choice boon-giver, Śiva: // 42
Brahmā said:
“Be gracious to me, O Giriśa, whose crest is fashioned of the moon!
Whatever wrong was done by me, O Śambhu, forgive it, O ocean of compassion! // 43

3.1.s: kṣamasva mama garvaṃ tvaṃ śaṃkareti punaḥpunaḥ ..
3.1.d: क्षमस्व मम गर्वं त्वं शंकरेति पुनःपुनः ..
3.1.m: Forgive my arrogance, O Śaṃkara!”—thus again and again
he bowed to Soma, to him whose crest is fashioned of the crescent moon. // 44

3.1.s: atha devaḥ prasanno'smai brahmaṇe svāṃśajāya tu ..
3.1.d: अथ देवः प्रसन्नोऽस्मै ब्रह्मणे स्वांशजाय तु ..
3.1.m: Then the god, pleased with this Brahmā born from his own portion,
said, “Do not fear,” and Śambhu addressed Bhairava: // 45
Īśvara said:

3.1.s: eṣa sarvasya jagataḥ pūjyo brahmā sanātanaḥ ..
3.1.d: एष सर्वस्य जगतः पूज्यो ब्रह्मा सनातनः ..
3.1.m: “This eternal Brahmā is worthy of worship by the entire universe.
Now carry the head of this Viriñci who has been slain. // 46
For purification from the slaying of a brahmin, desiring the maintenance of world order,
wander for alms with the skull, O Bhairava, by my command!” // 47
Having spoken thus, O brahmins, Śaṃkara vanished right there—
the blue-throated Mahādeva whose half-body is the daughter of the mountain. Then
he caused Bhairava to take the face of the creator, O twice-born ones:
“Wander for purification from sin, indeed for the maintenance of the world. // 49
Bearing the skull in hand, let Bhairava receive alms!”
Having said this, Giriśa [summoned] a certain terrifying maiden // 50
named Brahmin-Murder, cruel, resembling the submarine fire.
Directing her [to follow], Giriśa spoke again to Bhairava: // 51
Īśvara said:
“O Bhairava, observe this observance for a year for purification from the slaying of a brahmin.
Wander through all sacred fords; bathe for your own purification. // 52
Then go to Vārāṇasī for the pacification of the slaying of a brahmin.
By entering Vārāṇasī, this vile slaying of a brahmin of yours
will be destroyed except for a fourth part; the fourth portion is not destroyed. // 53

3.1.s: tasya nāśaṃ pravakṣyāmi tava bhairava tacchuṇu ..54..
3.1.d: तस्य नाशं प्रवक्ष्यामि तव भैरव तच्छुणु ..54..
3.1.m: I will tell you the destruction of that [portion], O Bhairava; listen to that! // 54
On the shore of the southern ocean, on Mount Gandhamādana,
an auspicious sacred ford was made by me for the benefit of all living beings, // 55
named Śiva, of great merit; go there with reverence.
By the mere entrance into it, this inauspicious slaying of a brahmin of yours // 56
will surely be destroyed without remainder by the māhātmya of the Śivatīrtha.”

3.1.s: uktvaivaṃ bhairavaṃ rudraḥ kailāsaṃ prayayau kṣaṇāt .. 57 ..
3.1.d: उक्त्वैवं भैरवं रुद्रः कैलासं प्रययौ क्षणात् .. 57 ..
3.1.m: Having spoken thus to Bhairava, Rudra went to Kailāsa in an instant. // 57
Then, skull in hand, Bhairava, urged by Śiva,
wandered through the worlds of gods, dānavas, yakṣas, and others. // 58
As he went, the exceedingly terrifying Brahmin-Murder followed him.
Having visited all the sacred fords and holy abodes // 59
in sport, the god Bhairava then went to Vārāṇasī.
When Bhairava, born of Śaṃkara's portion, entered Vārāṇasī,
the exceedingly vile killing of a brahmin was destroyed except for a fourth part.
With that fourth part, it pursued Bhairava born of Śaṃkara's portion.

3.1.s: tataḥ sa bhairavo devaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ kapāladhṛk ..
3.1.d: ततः स भैरवो देवः शूलपाणिः कपालधृक् ..
3.1.m: Then that god Bhairava, holding a trident and carrying a skull,
went later by Śiva's command to Mount Gandhamādana.
Having gone there to Śivatīrtha, O twice-born ones, Bhairava bathed.
By mere ablution there, in that most great Śivatīrtha,
the exceedingly terrifying killing of a brahmin was completely dissolved.
At this juncture, Śambhu appeared before him.
Having manifested, Mahādeva spoke [these] words to Bhairava:
Īśvara said:
"Your [sin of] killing a brahmin has been completely destroyed by plunging into Śivatīrtha;
there is no doubt about this, O Bhairava of noble vows.

3.1.s: idaṃ kapālaṃ kāśyāṃ tvaṃ sthāpayasva kvacitsthale .. 66 ..
3.1.d: इदं कपालं काश्यां त्वं स्थापयस्व क्वचित्स्थले .. 66 ..
3.1.m: Place this skull in some spot in Kāśī."
Having spoken thus, the blessed Śambhu vanished right there.
Then, O brahmins, Bhairava also, freed from the killing of a brahmin
by the majesty of Śivatīrtha, went to the city of Vārāṇasī.
He set down the skull in a certain spot, O twice-born ones;
then that place obtained the name Kapālatīrtha.
Śrī Sūta said:
Such is the power of that holy Śivatīrtha which grants liberation,
which relieves great suffering, which destroys great sins,
which allays the afflictions of hell, and which bestows heaven and liberation.
The majesty of Śivatīrtha, which bestows liberation, has been told by me.
A mortal who constantly recites this is freed from the multitude of sorrows.

3.1.m:
Śrī Sūta said:
Having bathed in Śivatīrtha, which frees from the killing of a brahmin,
a man should then go to Śaṅkhatīrtha to quell the web of his sins,
where by mere plunging even an ungrateful person is freed.
Deluded people who do not revere mothers, fathers, and teachers,
and whatever other wicked, ungrateful, shameless people there may be,
they all become purified in this Śaṅkhatīrtha merely by bathing.
Formerly, a sage named Śaṅkha lived on Mount Gandhamādana,
performing austerity, meditating on Viṣṇu with a concentrated mind.
There he fashioned an excellent sacred ford for the purpose of bathing;
the sacred ford created by Śaṅkha is called Śaṅkhatīrtha.
Having bathed there even once, a mortal—even an ungrateful one—is liberated.
Here I shall relate an ancient tale that destroys sin,
merely by hearing which a man attains liberation.
Formerly there was a foremost brahmin, the great sage Vatsanābha,
truthful, virtuous, eloquent, devoted to compassion for all beings,
equal toward enemy and friend, restrained, ascetic, with conquered senses,
versed in the Supreme Brahman, taking refuge solely in Brahman the Reality.
Endowed with such power, that sage performed austerity in his own hermitage.
Standing motionless in all his limbs on the ground right there,
he did not move from his place even by the distance of an atom.
As he remained in one place performing austerity for many hundreds of years,
an anthill crept over him and covered his limbs.
Even though his body was covered by an anthill, that great sage Vatsanābha
performed austerity alone, and did not notice the anthill at all.
While he was performing austerity, O foremost sages, Vāsava,

having released masses of clouds, swiftly caused it to rain.
In this way he rained unceasingly for seven days.
Even while being rained upon with an immense torrential downpour, the sage
received that rain with his eyes closed.
With a great roar instantly deafening the ears then,
a mighty thunderbolt fell upon the anthill.
While the cloud was raining, unbearable with cold wind,
the top of the anthill was destroyed, struck by the thunderbolt.
When the summit of that anthill had shattered, struck by the thunderbolt,
Vatsanābha, meditating, endured the unbearable rain.
As the great seer was afflicted day and night by streams of rain,
exceedingly great compassion arose in the heart of Dharma.
That Dharma reflected, while Vatsanābha was performing austerity:
"Even though an excessive rain is falling, he does not turn back from austerity.
Oh, how Vatsanābha's mind is devoted solely to righteousness!"
As he was thinking thus, such a thought arose in him:

3.1.m:
"Taking on the form of a buffalo, very great and charming,
with a tough skin capable of bearing the fall of downpours of rain,
having assumed the buffalo form, I will stand above the yogin.
The rain, even accompanied by great force, will certainly not trouble [him]."
Having decided thus, Dharma, bearing the streams [of rain] on his back,
stood above Vatsanābha, covering him with his body.
Then, at the end of seven days, that rain indeed ceased.
Then Dharma, in the form of a buffalo, filled with immense compassion,
departed from that anthill and stayed not far away.
Then, when the rain had stopped, the great sage Vatsanābha,
turning away quickly from his austerity, looked around in all directions:
"I stood amidst the downpour of rain, performing great austerity today.
The earth is seen drenched with water in all directions;
the peaks of the mountains, the forests, and the groves,
and the hermitages of the great seers are flooded with fresh water."
Having seen all these things, he became delighted;

3.1.m:
the righteous-minded great sage Vatsanābha thought:
"I have surely been protected by someone in this great deluge of rain.
For while such a great deluge of rain fell, how else could there be life?"
Having reflected thus, the best of sages looked in all directions.
Then, standing not far ahead, he saw a huge-bodied,
dark-colored buffalo; and Vatsanābha, rich in tapas,
reflected in his mind concerning that buffalo:
"How is a righteous disposition seen even among animals born of brute wombs?
For I have indeed been thoroughly protected from the great rain by a buffalo.
May long life be his, since he protected me here!"
Having reflected thus and so forth, he set out again for tapas.
Seeing him practicing tapas once more, the one bearing the form of a buffalo,
with all his limbs covered in horripilation, felt exceedingly great joy.
Yet, as the sage Vatsanābha was practicing tapas once again,
his mind did not become focused on the supreme Brahman as before.

3.1.m:
Becoming dejected in mind, Vatsanābha thought:
"If there is no purity, then the mind must be unsteady.
And when there is an abundance of sin, the mind does not at all become pure.
Yet I have not even a trace of sin; why then does my mind waver?"
Vatsanābha pondered again and again the cause of the fault.
Having reflected and determined [it], he straightway condemned himself:
"Fie on me, an evil-minded one today! Oh, how exceedingly foolish I am!
The great fault of ingratitude has come upon me today.
Because, towards the excellent buffalo who saved me from such a great rain,
I remain without even worshipping [him]; therefore, ingratitude has arisen in me.
Ingratitude is a great fault; there is no expiation for the ungrateful.
For the ungrateful there are no worlds, nor does the ungrateful have kinsmen.
By the power of the fault of ingratitude, my mind is defiled.
The ungrateful go to hell, as do those who betray the trusting.
I see no expiation whatsoever for the ungrateful,

Failing to maintain one's parents, not giving the teacher's fee,
and contracting ingratitude—for these the expiation ends only with death.
Therefore, renouncing my life, I shall perform an expiation."
Having resolved thus in his mind, the great sage Vatsanābha,
holding his own life as straw, with an inner self detached,
climbed the peak of Meru, wishing to perform the expiation.
The sage wished to throw himself down from that peak of Sumeru.
As he began to jump, saying, "Do not act in haste!",
Dharma himself, abandoning the form of a buffalo, restrained him.
Dharma said:
"O Vatsanābha of great wisdom, live for many years!
I am well pleased with your desire to renounce your body; may you prosper!
Indeed, in the world there is no one equal to your standard of righteousness.
Although the abandonment of life is the expiation for an ungrateful person,
nonetheless, because of your righteous character, I shall tell you another expiation.

3.1.m:
There is a sacred ford named Śaṅkhatīrtha on Gandhamādana.
For the pacification of this sin, bathe there with a concentrated mind.
You will attain purity of mind, and will thereby be freed from stain.
And then, having attained wisdom, you will reach the eternal abode.
I am Dharma, O lord of yogins; I speak truth to you."
Having heard these words of Dharma, the great sage Vatsanābha,
wishing to bathe in Śaṅkhatīrtha, went towards Gandhamādana.
Reaching Śaṅkhatīrtha, the great sage bathed there.
Then, his sin departed, his mind attained purity.
Then, before long, the sage attained oneness with Brahman.
"Thus has the power of Śaṅkhatīrtha been told to you, O brahmins,
where merely by bathing, even an ungrateful person is liberated.
One who injures his mother, one who injures his father, likewise one who injures his teacher,
and other hosts of ungrateful people are freed by immersing here.
Therefore, this [ford] should always be frequented by ungrateful men."

3.1.m:
Ah, the māhātmya of the sacred ford, by which even the ungrateful person is freed!
Failing to maintain one's parents, failing to give the fee to the guru,
and falling into ungratefulness—the expiation [for these] indeed ends only in death.
Here, however, by mere ritual ablution there is expiation even for the ungrateful person;
even ungratefulness is destroyed in that sacred ford merely by ritual ablution.
What need be said now of all other trifling sins?
Even an ungrateful mortal who recites this chapter with devotion is freed from sin;
with an inner self purified, having gone to Satyaloka, he would quickly attain liberation together with Brahmā.

3.1.m: And that Raikva Sayugvan, out of compassion,
imparted to Jānaśruti that knowledge which is difficult to attain even for lords of sages.
As soon as the experiential knowledge, identical with brahman, was taught by him,
the best of kings came to possess uncontradicted direct experience.
When he had attained the nature of brahman through the grace of the yogin Raikva,
the phenomenal world, consisting of pots, walls, and granaries, no longer appeared to him.
Suddenly rending illusion, he became Brahman alone.
In this way, from bathing in the triad of sacred fords, King Jānaśruti—how wonderful!—
attained the state of being Brahman, which is hard even for hosts of yogins to attain.
Thus has the glory of that triad of sacred fords been related to you, O brahmins.
Whoever recites this chapter on the glory of the triad of sacred fords,
rending the darkness of ignorance, becomes fit to attain the state of being Brahman.

Therefore, taking this [wood] which is fire by nature, having gone to the city,
and properly making churning-sticks (araṇīs), I shall with reverence worship the fire produced from it.”
Having so resolved, the king went to his own city.
He made a charming fire-churning stick measured by his own finger-breadths.
At the time of its making, O brahmins, the king chanted the Gāyatrī.
Indeed, as many syllables as there are in the Gāyatrī being recited,
to that exact measure in finger-breadths the king made the churning-stick.
Having produced the three fires there by churning,
aiming for the desired fruit of attaining Urvaśī's realm,
the king, adhering to the Vedas, joyfully made offerings into the three fires.
And by that very procedure of fire, he then performed many sacrifices.
Having thereby attained the Gandharva realms, the lord of the earth,
sported for a long time together with Urvaśī in the world of the gods, O best of brahmins.
Then once, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, accompanied by all the immortals,
watched the dance of the celestial maidens in the assembly.
King Purūravas also came at that time to the assembly of the lord of the gods,
in order to watch the captivating dance of the celestial maidens of the sky-dwellers.
One by one, those maidens danced before Śakra.
Then Urvaśī came and danced before Hari [Indra].
Then Urvaśī, filled with pride in her skill of dancing and dramatic expression,
saw that Purūravas and laughed most delightfully.

3.1.s: jahāsa tatra rājāpi tāṃ vilokya tadorvaśīm ..
3.1.d: जहास तत्र राजापि तां विलोक्य तदोर्वशीम् ..
3.1.m: The king too laughed there, beholding Urvaśī at that moment.
Then Tumburu, the master of dramatic arts, enraged by their laughter,
in anger cursed both of them—Urvaśī and the best of kings.
Tumburu said:
“Since here, in an assembly filled with many gods,
laughter was indulged in by you two in the midst of the dance without reason and in vain,
therefore, O best of kings, quickly, in an instant,
let there be separation between you two!” Thus he cursed him in the presence of all the deities.
Then the king, cursed there by the master of dramatic arts, was sorrowful.
He took refuge with the wielder of the thunderbolt [Indra], crying, “Protect me, protect me!”
With a plaintive voice Purūravas spoke to Puruhūta [Indra]:
“I performed sacrifices for the sake of attaining residence in the same world with Urvaśī;
hence, separation from her would be unbearable to me, O chastiser of Pāka!”
To him who spoke thus, the thousand-eyed husband of Śacī said:
“I will tell you the release from the curse; do not fear, O best of kings.
In the southern ocean, on the holy Gandhamādana mountain,
there is a supreme sacred ford known as Sādhyāmṛta,
served by all the gods, Siddhas, Cāraṇas, and Kinnaras,
and frequented by the host of great yogic sages such as Sanaka and others.
Bestowing enjoyment and liberation upon men, granting release from all curses,

3.1.m: such a sacred ford exists; go there in haste, O king.
Since by ritual ablution here nectar (amṛta) is to be attained (sādhya) by all,
it is therefore renowned as Sādhyāmṛta, celebrated in all the worlds.
By ritual ablution there, your reunion with Urvaśī will occur,

3.1.m: and your dwelling in my world shall take place; there is no doubt.”
Instructed thus in return, the king, with a delighted mind,
instantly set out, heading toward the great sacred ford Sādhyāmṛta.
He bathed there in Sādhyāmṛta, which destroys great sins.

3.1.m: From the ritual ablution there, O brahmins, the king was instantly freed from the curse.
Immediately after the ritual ablution, he was reunited with Urvaśī.
Seated in an aerial chariot with her, he set out for Amarāvatī.
Like a god, he sported again with her in the abode of the gods.
Such is the power of that unequalled sacred ford, Sādhyāmṛta,
where Purūravas was reunited with Urvaśī by means of a ritual ablution.
Therefore, whoever bathes in this sacred ford, which destroys great sins,
attains desired wishes and will go to the highest heaven;

3.1.m:
The glorious Sūta said:
Having bathed in the Sādhyāmṛta sacred ford, which releases the king from his curse, / a person observing vows should then go to Sarvatīrtha. (1)
Sarvatīrtha is of great merit, the destroyer of grave sins; / whether one is tainted with grave sins or tainted with all sins, (2)
one is purified that very moment from plunging into Sarvatīrtha. / All sins remain in the body, O you of noble vows, (3)
only as long as a sinful person does not plunge into this Sarvatīrtha.
Seeing a man going to this Sarvatīrtha for a ritual ablution, O twice-born,
all his sins tremble, thinking, ‘Our destruction will occur!’
A man on earth experiences sufferings such as dwelling in the womb only so long (5)
as he does not bathe in this Sarvatīrtha, O foremost of brahmins.
Whatever fruit a mortal obtains by performing great sacrifices and attending upon sacred fords, (6)
by reciting great mantras such as the Gāyatrī according to rule,
by repeating all four Vedas a hundred times, (7)
by worshiping the deities headed by Śiva and Viṣṇu with devotion,
and likewise by fasting on lunar days such as the eleventh,

The seers said:
How did this obtain the fame of being called ‘Sarvatīrtha’, O Sūta?
Tell this merit to us, O sage, as we listen at length. (9)
The glorious Sūta said:
Formerly there was a sage named Sucarita, endowed with vows, (10)
born in the lineage of Bhṛgu, blind from birth, and afflicted with old age.
Incapable of pilgrimage to sacred fords because of his lack of eyes, O twice-born, (11)
that great sage, desiring to bathe in all sacred fords,
went to the holy mountain Gandhamādana at the southern ocean, (12)
and performed exceedingly difficult austerity dedicated to Śaṃkara.
Worshiping Śambhu at the three junctures of the day, fasting, with senses subdued, (13)
and performing ritual ablution at the three ritual times, and likewise honoring guests,
standing in water in the cold season, standing amidst the five fires in the summer, (14)
enduring torrential downpours in the rainy season, subsisting on water, feeding on air,
always wearing the dusting of ashes and the three-striped mark made with ash, (15)
and wearing rudrākṣa beads according to the rule of the Jābāla Upaniṣad,

the twice-born performed fierce austerity thus for ten years. (16)
Pleased by his austerity, Śaṃkara, who bears the crescent moon upon his crest,
manifested before that sage Sucarita, O twice-born, (17)
mounted upon a great bull, served by a host of spirits,
half of his body the daughter of the mountain, wielding a trident, equal in radiance to ten million suns, (18)
illuminating all quarters with his own luster, dispelling the darkness,
all his limbs pale white with ash, adorned with a mass of matted hair, (19)
bedecked with ornaments of great serpents such as Ananta.
Śambhu, having then manifested, gave him two eyes (20)
so that he might behold him, Śaṃkara, the lord of the mountain’s daughter.
Then, O brahmins, Sucarita, given a pair of eyes by Śambhu,
beheld the supreme lord, and with a serene mind praised him: (21)
Sucarita said:
Hail, O god, supreme lord! Hail, O Śaṃkara, O you with matted hair! (22)
Hail, you who are worshiped by Brahmā and the rest, destroyer of Tripura, ender of Yama!
Hail, lord of Umā, great god, slayer of Kāma, hail, spotless one! (23)

.. महादेव उवाच .. ..
मुने सुचरिताद्य त्वं वरं वरय कांक्षितम् ..
वरं दातुं तवायातः पुण्येस्मिन्नाश्रमे शुभे ..
इतीरितो मुनिः प्राह महादेवं दयानिधिम् .. 3.1.29.30 .. ..
.. सुचरित उवाच .. ..
3.1.m:
Hail, physician of worldly existence, protector of beings, benevolent and imperishable!
Homage to you, three-eyed one, dedicated to protecting devotees! (24)
Homage to you, whose hair is the sky! Hail, embodiment of compassion!
Homage to you, blue-throated one! Hail, liberator from worldly existence! (25)
Homage to you, supreme lord, embodiment of supreme bliss!
Homage to you, bearer of the Gaṅgā, lord of the universe, Mṛḍa, imperishable one! (26)
Homage to you, the Lord, to Vāsudeva, to Śambhu,
to Śarva, to the fierce one, to the source, homage to the lord of Kailāsa! (27)
Protect me, ocean of compassion, through the glance of your merciful gaze!
Without examining my conduct, save me through mercy, O Hara! (28)
The glorious Sūta said:
Puffed with praise in this manner, Mahādeva said this to him,
to the sage Sucarita, O brahmins—[Mahādeva,] the lord of Umā, an ocean of compassion: / 29
Mahādeva said:
“O sage Sucarita, choose today the boon you desire.
I have come to this meritorious, auspicious hermitage to grant you a boon.”
Addressed thus, the sage spoke to Mahādeva, the treasure of compassion: / 3.1.29.30
Sucarita said:

3.1.s:
bhagavaṃstvaṃ prasanno me yadi syāścaṃdraśekhara .. 31 ..
tarhi tvāṃ pravṛṇomyaddhā varaṃ madabhikāṃkṣitam ..
jarāpalitadehohaṃ kutracidgaṃtumakṣamaḥ .. 32 ..
sarvatīrtheṣu ca snātumākāṃkṣā mama vidyate ..
tasmātsarveṣu tīrtheṣu snānena manujo hi yat ..
phalaṃ prāpnoti me brūhi tatphalā vāptisādhanam.. 33 ..
.. mahādeva uvāca .. ..
ahamāvāhayiṣyāmi tīrthānyatraiva kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 34 ..
rāmasya setunā pūte nage'smingaṃdhamādane ..
ityuktvā sa mahādevaḥ parvate gandhamādane .. 35 ..
tīrthānyāvāhayāmāsa muniprītyarthamuttamaḥ ..
tatassucaritaṃ prāha śaṃkaraḥ karuṇānidhiḥ .. 36 ..
mune sucaritedaṃ tu mahāpātakanāśanam ..
sāṃnidhyātsarvatīrthānāṃ sarvatīrthābhidhaṃ smṛtam .. 37 ..
mayātra sarvatīrthānāṃ manasākarṣaṇādidam ..
mānasaṃ tīrthamityākhyāṃ lapsyate bhuktimuktidam .. 38 ..
3.1.d:
भगवंस्त्वं प्रसन्नो मे यदि स्याश्चंद्रशेखर .. 31 ..
तर्हि त्वां प्रवृणोम्यद्धा वरं मदभिकांक्षितम् ..
जरापलितदेहोहं कुत्रचिद्गंतुमक्षमः .. 32 ..
सर्वतीर्थेषु च स्नातुमाकांक्षा मम विद्यते ..
तस्मात्सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु स्नानेन मनुजो हि यत् ..
फलं प्राप्नोति मे ब्रूहि तत्फला वाप्तिसाधनम्.. 33 ..
.. महादेव उवाच .. ..
अहमावाहयिष्यामि तीर्थान्यत्रैव कृत्स्नशः .. 34 ..
रामस्य सेतुना पूते नगेऽस्मिन्गंधमादने ..
इत्युक्त्वा स महादेवः पर्वते गन्धमादने .. 35 ..
तीर्थान्यावाहयामास मुनिप्रीत्यर्थमुत्तमः ..
ततस्सुचरितं प्राह शंकरः करुणानिधिः .. 36 ..
मुने सुचरितेदं तु महापातकनाशनम् ..
सांनिध्यात्सर्वतीर्थानां सर्वतीर्थाभिधं स्मृतम् .. 37 ..
मयात्र सर्वतीर्थानां मनसाकर्षणादिदम् ..
मानसं तीर्थमित्याख्यां लप्स्यते भुक्तिमुक्तिदम् .. 38 ..
3.1.m:
“O Lord, if you are pleased with me, O crescent-crested one, / 31
then I truly choose from you the boon desired by me:
My body is worn out by old age and gray hair; I am unable to go anywhere, / 32
and yet my desire is to bathe in all sacred fords.
Therefore, tell me the means of obtaining that fruit
which a mortal attains by bathing in all sacred fords.” / 33
Mahādeva said:
“I shall summon all the sacred fords right here in their entirety, / 34
on this mountain Gandhamādana, purified by Rāma's causeway.”
Having spoken thus on Mount Gandhamādana, that Mahādeva, / 35
the supreme one, summoned the sacred fords for the pleasure of the sage.
Then Śaṃkara, the treasure of compassion, spoke to Sucarita: / 36
“O sage Sucarita, this [pool] indeed destroys great sins.
Because of the presence of all the sacred fords, it is known by the name Sarvatīrtha. / 37
Since all the sacred fords were drawn here by me mentally,
it shall obtain the name Mānasa sacred ford, bestowing enjoyment and liberation. / 38

3.1.s:
ataḥ sucaritātra tvaṃ snāhi sadyo vimuktaye ..
mahāpātakasaṃghānāṃ dāvānalasamadyutau .. .. 39 ..
kāmamohabhayakrodhalobharogādināśane ..
vinā vedāṃtavijñānaṃ sadyonirvāṇakāraṇe .. 3.1.29.40 ..
janmamṛtyvādinakraughasaṃsārārṇavatāraṇe ..
kumbhīpākādisakalanarakāgnivināśane .. 41 ..
itīritaḥ sucaritaḥ śambhunā madanāriṇā ..
sasnau viprāḥ sarvatīrthe mahādevasya saṃnidhau .. 42 ..
snātvotthitaḥ sucarito dadṛśe'khilamānavaiḥ ..
jarāpalitanirmuktastaruṇo'tīva sundaraḥ .. 43 ..
dṛṣṭvā svadehasauṃdaryaṃ tataḥ sucarito muniḥ ..
ślāghayāmāsa tattīrthaṃ bahudhā'nye ca tāpasāḥ .. 44 ..
mahādevaḥ sucaritaṃ babhāṣe tadanaṃtaram ..
asya tīrthasya tīre tvaṃ vasansucarita dvija .. .. 45 ..
snānaṃ kuruṣva satataṃ smaranmāṃ muktidāyakam ..
deśāṃtarīyatīrtheṣu mā vraja brāhmaṇottama .. 46 ..
3.1.d:
अतः सुचरितात्र त्वं स्नाहि सद्यो विमुक्तये ..
महापातकसंघानां दावानलसमद्युतौ .. .. 39 ..
काममोहभयक्रोधलोभरोगादिनाशने ..
विना वेदांतविज्ञानं सद्योनिर्वाणकारणे .. 3.1.29.40 ..
जन्ममृत्य्वादिनक्रौघसंसारार्णवतारणे ..
कुम्भीपाकादिसकलनरकाग्निविनाशने .. 41 ..
इतीरितः सुचरितः शम्भुना मदनारिणा ..
सस्नौ विप्राः सर्वतीर्थे महादेवस्य संनिधौ .. 42 ..
स्नात्वोत्थितः सुचरितो ददृशेऽखिलमानवैः ..
जरापलितनिर्मुक्तस्तरुणोऽतीव सुन्दरः .. 43 ..
दृष्ट्वा स्वदेहसौंदर्यं ततः सुचरितो मुनिः ..
श्लाघयामास तत्तीर्थं बहुधाऽन्ये च तापसाः .. 44 ..
महादेवः सुचरितं बभाषे तदनंतरम् ..
अस्य तीर्थस्य तीरे त्वं वसन्सुचरित द्विज .. .. 45 ..
स्नानं कुरुष्व सततं स्मरन्मां मुक्तिदायकम् ..
देशांतरीयतीर्थेषु मा व्रज ब्राह्मणोत्तम .. 46 ..
3.1.m:
Therefore, Sucarita, bathe here immediately for liberation—
in this [ford] possessing a splendour like a forest fire to the masses of great sins, / 39
in that which destroys lust, delusion, fear, anger, greed, disease, and the rest,
in that which causes immediate emancipation without the knowledge of Vedānta, / 3.1.29.40
in that which carries one across the ocean of worldly existence filled with crocodiles such as birth and death,
in that which extinguishes the fire of all hells such as Kumbhīpāka.” / 41
Thus addressed by Śambhu, the enemy of Madana,
Sucarita bathed in Sarvatīrtha, O brahmins, in the presence of Mahādeva. / 42
Emerging after his ritual ablution, Sucarita was beheld by all people
freed from old age and gray hair, young and exceedingly handsome. / 43
Then, seeing the beauty of his own body, the sage Sucarita
praised that sacred ford in many ways, as did the other ascetics. / 44
After that, Mahādeva spoke to Sucarita:
“Dwelling on the bank of this sacred ford, O Sucarita, O twice-born, / 45
perform your ritual ablution constantly, remembering me, the giver of liberation.
Do not wander to sacred fords in other regions, O best of brahmins! / 46

3.1.s:
asya tīrthasya māhātmyānmāmaṃte prāpsyasi dhruvam..
anye'pi ye'tra snāsyaṃti te'pi māṃ prāpnuyurdvija .. 47 ..
ityuktvā bhagavānīśastatraivāṃtaradhīyata ..
tasminnaṃtarhite rudre tataḥ sucarito muniḥ .. 48 ..
anekakālaṃ nivasansarvatīrthasya tīrataḥ ..
snānaṃ samācaraṃstīrthe mānase niyamānvitaḥ .. 49 ..
dehāṃte śaṃkaraṃ prāpa sarvabandhavimocitaḥ ..
sāyujyaṃ cāpi saṃprāpa sarvatīrthasya vaibhavāt .. 3.1.29.50 ..
evaṃ vaḥ kathitaṃ viprāḥ sarvatīrthasya vaibhavam ..
etatpaṭhanvā śṛṇvanvā mucyate sarva pātakaiḥ .. 51 ..
Comments on Koti/Dhanushkoti
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe setumāhātmye sarvatīrthapraśaṃsāyāṃ sarvatīrthasvarūpa kathanaṃnāmaikonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 29 .. .
3.1.d:
अस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यान्मामंते प्राप्स्यसि ध्रुवम्..
अन्येऽपि येऽत्र स्नास्यंति तेऽपि मां प्राप्नुयुर्द्विज .. 47 ..
इत्युक्त्वा भगवानीशस्तत्रैवांतरधीयत ..
तस्मिन्नंतर्हिते रुद्रे ततः सुचरितो मुनिः .. 48 ..
अनेककालं निवसन्सर्वतीर्थस्य तीरतः ..
स्नानं समाचरंस्तीर्थे मानसे नियमान्वितः .. 49 ..
देहांते शंकरं प्राप सर्वबन्धविमोचितः ..
सायुज्यं चापि संप्राप सर्वतीर्थस्य वैभवात् .. 3.1.29.50 ..
एवं वः कथितं विप्राः सर्वतीर्थस्य वैभवम् ..
एतत्पठन्वा शृण्वन्वा मुच्यते सर्व पातकैः .. 51 ..
चोम्मेन्त्स् ओन् कोति/धनुस्ह्कोति
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतुमाहात्म्ये सर्वतीर्थप्रशंसायां सर्वतीर्थस्वरूप कथनंनामैकोनत्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 29 .. .
3.1.m:
Through the māhātmya of this sacred ford, you will surely reach me at the end.
Others too who will bathe here shall also attain me, O twice-born.” / 47
Having said this, the Lord, the Ruler, vanished right there.
When Rudra had disappeared, the sage Sucarita, / 48
dwelling for a long time on the bank of Sarvatīrtha,
performing his ritual ablution in the Mānasa sacred ford with vows observed, / 49
at the end of his physical existence attained Śaṃkara, freed from all fetters,
and attained intimate union by virtue of the power of Sarvatīrtha. / 3.1.29.50
Thus the power of Sarvatīrtha has been told to you, O brahmins.
One who recites or hears this is freed from all sins. / 51
Comments on Koṭi/Dhanuṣkoṭi
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, entitled “Description of the Nature of Sarvatīrtha” in the Praise of Sarvatīrtha, in the Setumāhātmya of the third section, Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. // 29
Śrī Sūta said:
A mortal who has performed ritual ablution in the exceedingly purifying Sarvatīrtha
should then proceed to Dhanuṣkoṭi, which destroys sins such as killing a brahmin. / 1
Merely by remembering it, a human being on earth becomes liberated.

3.1.s: dhanuṣkoṭiṃ prapaśyaṃti snāṃti vā kathayaṃti ye .. 2 ..
3.1.d: धनुष्कोटिं प्रपश्यंति स्नांति वा कथयंति ये .. 2 ..
3.1.m: Those who look upon Dhanuṣkoṭi, or bathe [there], or speak of it, / 2
do not experience the twenty-eight varieties of hells:
Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Mahāraurava, Raurava, / 3
Kumbhīpāka, Kālasūtra, Asipatravana likewise,
Kṛmibhakṣa, Andhakūpa, Saṃdaṃśa, and Śālmalī; / 4
Sūrmi, Vaitaraṇī, Prāṇarodha, and likewise Viśasana,
Lālābhakṣa, also Avīci, and likewise Sārameyādana,
and also Vajrakaṇaka, Kṣārakardamapātana,
Rakṣogaṇāśana, Śūlaprota, Vitodana,
Daṃdaśūkāśana, and the one named Paryāvartana,
the one named Tirodhāna, O brahmins, and the one called Sūcīmukha,
Pūyaśoṇitabhakṣa, and Viṣāgniparipīḍana.
Into this collection of hells numbering twenty-eight,

3.1.s: na yāti manujo viprā dhanuṣkoṭau nimajjanāt ..
3.1.d: न याति मनुजो विप्रा धनुष्कोटौ निमज्जनात् ..
3.1.m: a person does not go, O brahmins, by taking a plunge at Dhanuṣkoṭi.
He who plunders the wealth, offspring, and wives of others,
bound by the noose of Time by the terrifying messengers of Yama,
is cast into the dread hell of Tāmisra for many years.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.

3.1.s: yo nihatya tu bhartāraṃ bhuṃkte tasya dhanādikān .. 11 ..
3.1.d: यो निहत्य तु भर्तारं भुंक्ते तस्य धनादिकान् .. 11 ..
3.1.m: He who, having killed a master, enjoys his wealth and the like,
is thrown into Andhatāmisra, which is filled with immense suffering.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
A mortal who maintains his own family by malice toward living beings,

3.1.s: sa tāniha vihāyāśu raurave pātyate dhruvam .. 13 ..
3.1.d: स तानिह विहायाशु रौरवे पात्यते ध्रुवम् .. 13 ..
3.1.m: leaving them here, is quickly and surely cast into Raurava,
which is filled with great snakes violent with poison, by Yama's men.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
A mortal who feeds only his own body without wife, son, and the like,
is cast into dread Mahāraurava, eating his own flesh.

3.1.s: snāti ceddhanuṣaḥ koṭau tasmi nnāsau nipātyate ..
3.1.d: स्नाति चेद्धनुषः कोटौ तस्मि न्नासौ निपात्यते ..
3.1.m: If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
He who traps animals or birds while they are alive,
deprived of any trace of pity, condemned even by carnivorous demons,
Yama's attendants cast him into boiling oil in Kumbhīpāka.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
The vile man who hates mother, father, or brahmins,
he, in the hell of Kālasūtra, ten thousand yojanas wide,
tormented by fire below and by the sun's rays above,
is cast, afflicted by hunger, on a floor made of copper, O brahmins.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
The man who transgresses the Vedic path and walks on an evil road,
is cast into the dread Asipatravana by the servants of Yama.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.

3.1.s: yo rājā rājabhṛtyo vā hyadaṃḍye daṃḍamācaret .. 22 ..
3.1.d: यो राजा राजभृत्यो वा ह्यदंड्ये दंडमाचरेत् .. 22 ..
3.1.m: A king or a servant of a king who inflicts punishment on the unpunishable,

3.1.s: śarīradaṃḍaṃ vipre vā sa śūkaramukhe dvijāḥ ..
3.1.d: शरीरदंडं विप्रे वा स शूकरमुखे द्विजाः ..
3.1.m: or corporal punishment on a brahmin, he, O twice-born,
is cast into the dread hell of Śūkaramukha, crushed in a press like sugarcane.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
He who slaughters living beings whose livelihoods depend on God,
being tormented by those very creatures who were tormented by him,
is cast into the deeply terrifying Andhakūpa by Yama's servants.
There, heavy with darkness, sleepless, he must wander without rest.
[If he bathes] at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into it.
A man who eats grain, soup, and the like while making row-distinctions,

3.1.s: akṛtvā paṃcayajñaṃ vā bhuṃkte mohena sa dvijāḥ .. 27 ..
3.1.d: अकृत्वा पंचयज्ञं वा भुंक्ते मोहेन स द्विजाः .. 27 ..
3.1.m: or who, out of delusion, eats without having offered the five sacrifices, O twice-born,
is thrown down by Yama's warriors into the hell of Kṛmibhojana,
being eaten by hundreds of worms while eating masses of worms,
and, having himself become a worm, he remains there until the exhaustion of his sin.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
He who steals the wealth of a brahmin by theft or by force,
or the wealth of others, whether a king or his official,
tormented intensely with tongs in fiery pits made of iron,
is cast into the dread hell of Saṃdaṃśa by Yama's men.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not thrown into it.
A vile man who has intercourse with a forbidden woman,
or a woman who has intercourse with a forbidden man, O twice-born,
both of them, [embracing] an iron woman and an iron man,
standing embracing them red-hot as long as the moon and sun endure,
are cast into the dread hell named Sūrmi, full of many thorns.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into that [hell].
Whoever afflicts all creatures through various means and harassments,
is cast into the terrible hell Śālmalī, which is full of thorns.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into that [hell].

3.1.s: rājā vā rājabhṛtyo vā yaḥ pāṣaṃḍamanuvrataḥ ..
3.1.d: राजा वा राजभृत्यो वा यः पाषंडमनुव्रतः ..
3.1.m: A king or a king's servant who follows heresy,
and breaches the embankments of dharma, is cast into the Vaitaraṇī.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into that [hell].
He who is defiled by association with an outcaste woman, destitute of purification and proper conduct,
who has abandoned shame, abandoned the Veda, and engages in the conduct of beasts—
he, into [a place] filled with pus, feces, urine, blood, phlegm, bile, and the like,
into an exceedingly loathsome hell, is cast by the servants of Yama.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into that [hell].
A hunter who kills with stones or afflicts deer with arrows—
pierced by a flood of arrows by the servants of Yama in the other world,
he is cast by the servants of Yama into the hell named Prāṇarodha.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into that [hell].
A hypocrite who slaughters animals in a sacrifice without following the prescribed rites,
O twice-born ones, in the other worlds, into the hell Vaiśasa,
hacked to pieces by Yama's soldiers, is cast, overwhelmed with pain.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into that [hell].

3.1.s: ātmabhāryāṃ savarṇāṃ yo retaḥ pāyayate tu saḥ ..
3.1.d: आत्मभार्यां सवर्णां यो रेतः पाययते तु सः ..
3.1.m: He who makes his own wife of the same caste swallow semen,
becomes a semen-drinker in the other world and is cast into the semen-pit.
If he bathes at Dhanuṣkoṭi, he is not cast into that [hell].
He who, adopting the ways of a bandit, gives poison or burns down villages,
and robs merchants of their goods, in the other world, O best of the twice-born,
is cast for a long time into the hell named Vajradaṃṣṭrāhika.

all the kings, O brahmins, hastened to make camp.
Those kings who survived went with joyful minds,
Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Śikhaṇḍin and the others, and indeed all the Sṛñjayas.
And other rulers of the earth also departed to their own camps.
Then the heroic sons of Pṛthā, accompanied by Kṛṣṇa and Sātyaki,
entered Duryodhana's deserted camp, O twice-born.
By the elderly ministers present there, and by the eunuchs guarding the women,
who had their hands folded in reverence, bowing low, clad in ochre and soiled garments,
the sons of Pṛthā were saluted in the palace of the Kuru king.
Taking possession of the various wealth situated there, those mighty ones
dwelt happily in the camp of Suyodhana.
Then glorious Kṛṣṇa, as if pleasing them, spoke to those sons of Pṛthā:
"For the sake of auspiciousness, we should stay outside the camp."
Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, saying "So be it," the Pāṇḍavas,
accompanied by Kṛṣṇa and Sātyaki, went outside the camp.
Together with Vāsudeva, indeed for the sake of auspiciousness, the Pāṇḍavas,
those best of men, having reached the bank of the Oghavatī river,
spent that night there pleasantly, having slain the hosts of their enemies.
Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, and the son of Droṇa [went] into the presence of Duryodhana;
they arrived in the late afternoon before the setting of the sun.
Then, seeing Suyodhana smeared with the dust of battle,
with his thigh-bones shattered by Bhīmasena's terrible mace,
his entire body drenched in blood, writhing on the surface of the earth,
the three, Droṇa's son and the others, grieved there at that time.

He danced before Śambhu, overflowing with tears of joy.
Then the pleased Lord manifested before him.
Seeing Mahādeva there, he praised the Supreme Lord.
The son of Droṇa said:

Whose lotus-feet act as a boat for those drowned in the ocean of misfortune!
O Mahādeva, embodiment of mercy, Dhūrjaṭi, blue-and-red one,
Beloved of Umā, odd-eyed one, moon-crested one, homage to you!

3.1.m: Grant this very boon to me, O Śambhu! Homage be to you!

Aśvatthāman too, O chief of brahmins, had his sins cleansed away and became stainless
at that very moment, merely by ritual ablution at Rāmacandra's Dhanuṣkoṭi.
With his sins washed away, all the great seers then welcomed
this son of Droṇa as pure and stainless from that time forward.

merely through the majesty of ritual ablution at Rāmacandra's Dhanuṣkoṭi.
Whoever recites this chapter or listens to it attentively,
shaking off sins here in this world, is honored in the world of Śiva.

His officiating priest was Raibhya, learned and supremely righteous.

knowers of the Vedas with their six limbs, skilled in Vedic and traditional rites,

There was no error by the two brothers in the rites with their auxiliary elements at the sacrificial session.
While this sacrificial session of King Bṛhaddyumna was being performed,

Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Atri, Jābāli, then Kaśyapa,
Kratu, Dakṣa, Pulastya, Pulaha, the sage Nārada,

Bhṛgu, Kutsa, then Vālmīki, Vyāsa, Dhaumya, and others,
accompanied by numerous, innumerable disciples and grand-disciples.
Seeing them arrived, King Bṛhaddyumna
respectfully honored all the sages with water offerings and other gifts.
Arrived from various quarters, accompanied by fourfold armies,
kings, bringing presents, [came] out of respect to view the sacrificial session.
Vaiśyas and Śūdras, thus all four classes, came together.
Religious students, householders, forest-dwellers, and mendicants
also came to see that sacrificial session of Bṛhaddyumna.
The best of kings honored all of them according to their worth,
and gave food to everyone, with clarified butter, soup, and other dishes,
and garments, gold, necklaces, and countless jewels.
In this way, the king extended hospitality to those who had gathered at the sacrificial session.
Then, O brahmins, the two sons of Raibhya, Arvāvasu and Parāvasu,
performed the rituals of the sacrifice and other rites without any error.
Seeing that skill of the two sons of Raibhya,
all the sages, headed by Vasiṣṭha, praised them while nodding their heads.
Having caused certain rites to be performed there, Parāvasu,
at the end of the third pressing, in order to attend to household matters,

"From the slaying of his father, a brahmin, Parāvasu has incurred a great sin.
For indeed, regarding a sin committed by another, through an expiation performed by someone else // 58

Moreover, for the killer of a father and a brahmin, there is by no means an expiation. // 59

Arvāvasu spoke again to the gods headed by Indra: // 61
"Nevertheless, through your greatness, and likewise through your favor,
O best among the thirty gods, for my brother, the slayer of his father and a brahmin, // 62
tell how there may be expiation, filled with compassion as you are."
Having thus heard the words of Arvāvasu, those dwellers of the thirty-fold realm, // 63
after meditating for a very long time and having determined [it], said this:
"We shall tell you a means that removes that sin. // 64
In the sacred southern ocean, at the liberating Rāmasetu,
there is a liberating sacred ford renowned as Dhanuṣkoṭi. // 65
It destroys the slaying of a brahmin, the drinking of liquor, and the theft of gold;
it also destroys the sins of violating the guru's bed and association [with such sinners]. // 66
Even if one bathes without desire, it grants the fruit of liberation;
it destroys bad dreams, brings good fortune, and removes the suffering of hell. // 67
It is the cause of attaining the realm of Kailāsa and others, granting the highest truth;
it fulfills all desires of men and destroys debts and poverty. // 68
From the mere utterance, 'Dhanuṣkoṭi, Dhanuṣkoṭi, Dhanuṣkoṭi,'
it grants heaven and liberation to men, bestowing the fruit of great merit. // 69

That Yajñadeva indeed had a son named Sumati.
Abandoning both his parents and also his devoted wife,
he went off to the Utkala country, dedicated to the company of rakes.
A certain Kirāta woman lived in that country, charming to young men;
alluring young men, she took away all their wealth for a long time.
Sumati, the lowest of brahmins, went to her house.

3.1.m: you must worship, O dear one, once, twice, or thrice a day.
Mixed with tulasī leaves and sprinkled with water that washed the feet [of the deity],
always eat the food of the divine offering before Śambhu and Nārāyaṇa.
Offer the oblation called Vaiśvadeva for the purification of food.
Satisfy with food the lords of ascetics established in Brahman who come to your house,
as well as the aged, others who are helpless, the sick, and religious students.
Render service to your mother, and remain devoted to the domestic fire.
The great five-syllable mantra combined with the praṇava,
likewise the eight-syllable mantra, and other mantras as well, O twice-born,
recite with self-restraint, meditating upon the presiding deities of the mantras.
Always practice other such duties taught in the Smṛtis as well.
Having observed your vows in this manner, liberation at the end of the body shall surely be yours."
Thus addressed by the sage Vyāsa, Durvinīta bowed to him,
performed all that was spoken by him, and attained liberation at the end of the body.
His mother too, having died in due time from bathing at Dhanuṣkoṭi,
attained supreme liberation, which grants freedom from rebirth.
Durvāsas said:
"Thus the deliverance of Durvinīta and his mother
by ablution at Dhanuṣkoṭi has been narrated to you by me, O Yajñadeva.
To purify [him] from the murder of a brahmin, you too quickly
take this son, O brahmin, and go to Dhanuṣkoṭi, which bestows liberation."

Sindhudvīpa said:

the deliverance of Sumati, this son of Yajñadeva,
from great sins through immersion in Dhanuṣkoṭi.
Therefore, go to Dhanuṣkoṭi for the purification of your sins;
there can be no purification of sin otherwise, even by tens of thousands of expiations."
Glorious Sūta said:
Having heard these words of Sindhudvīpa, O best of brahmins,
