3.1.m: Or how was he freed from sin through immersion in Dhanuṣkoṭi?
Tell this in detail to us who are eager to hear, O sage!"
Glorious Sūta said:
"O sages, let the sin of that Durācāra be heard,

3.1.s: snānena dhanuṣaḥ koṭau yathā muktaśca pātakāt .. 4 ..
3.1.d: स्नानेन धनुषः कोटौ यथा मुक्तश्च पातकात् .. 4 ..
3.1.m: and how he was freed from sin by a ritual ablution at the point of the bow (Dhanuṣkoṭi).
There was a certain brahmin named Durācāra residing on the bank of the Gautamī,
a sinner, O brahmins, constantly devoted to cruel deeds.
Corrupted by association with killers of brahmins, drinkers of liquor,
thieves, and violators of the guru's bed, he lived with them, O brahmins.
Because of the fault of associating with great sinners, of this twice-born,
all brahminhood was lost completely, O best of brahmins.

3.1.s: mahāpātakibhiḥ sārddhaṃ dinamekaṃ tu yo dvijaḥ ..
3.1.d: महापातकिभिः सार्द्धं दिनमेकं तु यो द्विजः ..
3.1.m: The twice-born who respectfully lives with great sinners
for even a single day—from that very moment, of that twice-born
brahmin, a fourth part is destroyed indeed; of this there is no doubt.
From two days of serving, touching, seeing, sleeping with,
and dining in the same row with great sinners, O brahmins,
the second portion of a brahmin is destroyed; of this there is no doubt.
From three days, the third part is destroyed indeed; of this there is no doubt.
From four days, the fourth part certainly dissolves.

3.1.s: ataḥ paraṃ tu taiḥ sākaṃ śayanāsanabhojanaiḥ ..
3.1.d: अतः परं तु तैः साकं शयनासनभोजनैः ..
3.1.m: Beyond this, however, by sleeping, sitting, and dining with them,
he becomes an equal sinner to them, owing to the emergence of a great sin.
Because of that, this man named Durācāra was stripped of his brahminhood, O brahmins.
[he] was seized by a fearsome, mighty vetāla.
He, helpless and terribly tormented by that vetāla,
wandered from country to country, O brahmins, and from one forest to another.
Through the ripening of former merit and through the working of destiny, that twice-born man,
pursued and possessed by that piśāca, O brahmins,
went to Rāmacandra’s Dhanuṣkoṭi, which destroys great sins.
That vetāla submerged him into the waters of Dhanuṣkoṭi.
Having been made to enter the waters of Dhanuṣkoṭi by the vetāla,
he emerged in an instant, freed by the vetāla.
Having risen then from the waters of Dhanuṣkoṭi, O brahmins,
that twice-born man, restored to health, reflected: “What region is this on the seashore?
How have I, a dweller on the banks of the Gautamī, arrived here?”
Thus perplexed with anxiety, he approached the great-souled Dattātreya,
the foremost and highest of yogins, who resided at Dhanuṣkoṭi;
bowing down to him, that Durācāra spoke:
“I do not know, O Lord, what country this is. Tell me now!
I am indeed Durācāra by name, residing on the bank of the Gautamī.
Out of compassion, tell me, O holy one: how did I come here?”
Thus asked by that Durācāra, the sage of noble vows,
a treasury of compassion, meditated for a moment and said to Durācāra:
“O Durācāra, when contact with a great sinner was made formerly,
[your] brahminhood was lost, and then a vetāla seized you.
Possessed by him, helpless and bewildered in mind, you arrived here.
The vetāla plunged you into the waters of Dhanuṣkoṭi here;
and by the mere immersion there, you were freed from sin.

3.1.s: dhanuṣkoṭau tu ye snānaṃ puṇye kurvaṃti mānavāḥ ..
3.1.d: धनुष्कोटौ तु ये स्नानं पुण्ये कुर्वंति मानवाः ..
3.1.m: Those men who take a ritual ablution at sacred Dhanuṣkoṭi—
truly, their accumulations of the five great sins are destroyed.
By the mere immersion here at Rāmacandra’s Dhanuṣkoṭi,
the fault of contact with a great sinner has gone to dissolution.
Through that very destruction, the vetāla released you and vanished.
The vetāla who seized you was formerly a brahmin.
In the month of Bhādrapada, during the dark fortnight, he did not perform
the Mahālaya rite for the ancestors with joy, according to the rule of the Pārvaṇa rites.
Therefore, cursed by his ancestors, he became a vetāla.
Yet even he, by merely beholding this Dhanuṣkoṭi,
abandoned his vetāla state here and attained the world of Viṣṇu.
Therefore, in the month of Bhādrapada, during the dark fortnight,
those who, out of excessive greed, do not perform the Mahālaya rite intended for their ancestors—
filled with immense greed, they will certainly become vetālas; there is no doubt.
Therefore, in the month of Bhādrapada, during the dark fortnight,
those who, according to their ability, feed brahmins who have mastered the Vedas
with abundant food for the sake of the ancestors, do not suffer an evil state.
And in the month of Bhādrapada, during the dark fortnight,
even a destitute man who feeds one, two, or three brahmins according to his ability
for the Mahālaya, shall never suffer misfortune.
This brahmin who seized you, a sinner, went to the state of a vetāla

Never does what he desires come to pass on the earth;
he falls into the hell named Vaitaraṇī as long as the moon and stars endure.
The man who with faith performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the eighth [tithi]—
his ancestors are indeed satisfied for eighty thousand kalpas.
They prosper him with blessings, and his obstacles are dispelled;
the hosts of ancestors always grant him unbroken lineage.

3.1.s: navamyāṃ tu tithau martyaḥ śrāddhaṃ kuryānmahālayam ..
3.1.d: नवम्यां तु तिथौ मर्त्यः श्राद्धं कुर्यान्महालयम् ..
3.1.m: And if a mortal performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the ninth tithi,
the venerable Goddess Durgā, the consort of Śambhu, is pleased with him.
Consumption, epilepsy, leprosy, and the like, as well as petty spirits and piśācas—
Durgā, the slayer of Mahiṣa, destroys them for him when she is pleased.

3.1.s: navamyāṃ tu tithau martyo yo na kuryānmahālayam ..
3.1.d: नवम्यां तु तिथौ मर्त्यो यो न कुर्यान्महालयम् ..
3.1.m: The mortal who does not perform the Mahālaya [śrāddha] on the ninth tithi
will be afflicted with epilepsy as well as by a brahmarakṣasa,
and will be continually tormented by malignant spirits invoked through sorcery.
The mortal who performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the ninth tithi—
his ancestors are indeed satisfied for ninety thousand kalpas,
and the hosts of ancestors always grant him unbroken lineage.

3.1.s: daśamyāṃ tu tithau martyaḥ śrāddhaṃ kuryānmahālayam ..
3.1.d: दशम्यां तु तिथौ मर्त्यः श्राद्धं कुर्यान्महालयम् ..
3.1.m: If a mortal performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the tenth tithi,
the sixteen-fold Moon, whose rays are nectar, is pleased with him.
When this lord of medicinal plants is satisfied by this śrāddha,
the plants always bestow paddy and other grains.
He who does not perform the unsurpassed Mahālaya [śrāddha] on the tenth,
his medicinal plants are fruitless, and his agriculture too is fruitless.
The mortal who performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the tenth tithi—
his ancestors are indeed satisfied for a hundred thousand kalpas,
and the hosts of ancestors always grant him unbroken lineage.
If a man with devotion performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the eleventh [tithi],
Rudra, the destroyer of all the worlds, is pleased with him.
By the grace of Rudra, the destroyer of all, the lord of the universe,
this performer of the śrāddha constantly defeats his enemies,
and even ten thousand sins of killing a brahmin are destroyed in an instant.
He attains the full fruit of sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma.

3.1.s: ekādaśyāṃ naro bhaktyā yo na kuryānmahālayam .. 91 ..
3.1.d: एकादश्यां नरो भक्त्या यो न कुर्यान्महालयम् .. 91 ..
3.1.m: The man who does not devotedly perform the Mahālaya [śrāddha] on the eleventh [tithi]—

3.1.s: tasya vai vimukho rudro na prasīdati karhicit ..
3.1.d: तस्य वै विमुखो रुद्रो न प्रसीदति कर्हिचित् ..
3.1.m: to him Rudra is turned away and is never pleased.
Enemies increasing on all sides afflict him indeed.
Sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma performed with generous priestly fees
would be entirely fruitless for him, like an oblation poured into ashes.
He would become equal to a slayer of a brahmin from the fault of not performing the śrāddha.
He who performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the eleventh tithi—
his ancestors are indeed satisfied for two hundred thousand kalpas,

3.1.s: saṃtatiṃ cāpyavicchinnāṃ dadyuḥ pitṛ gaṇāḥ sadā .. 95 ..
3.1.d: संततिं चाप्यविच्छिन्नां दद्युः पितृ गणाः सदा .. 95 ..
3.1.m: and the hosts of ancestors always grant him unbroken lineage.

3.1.s:
dvādaśyāṃ tu tithau martyaḥ kuryācchrāddhaṃ mahālayam .
tasya lakṣmīpatiḥ sākṣātprasīdati janārdanaḥ .. 96 ..
3.1.d:
द्वादश्यां तु तिथौ मर्त्यः कुर्याच्छ्राद्धं महालयम् .
तस्य लक्ष्मीपतिः साक्षात्प्रसीदति जनार्दनः .. 96 ..
3.1.m:
If a mortal performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the twelfth tithi,
Janārdana, the Lord of Lakṣmī, is directly pleased with him.
When the Lord of the gods, the God of gods, Janārdana, is pleased,
the entire world, moving and unmoving, is pleased beyond doubt.
The Earth, beloved of Hari, also makes his crops flourish,
and Lakṣmī, the beloved of Hari, increases in his house.
The mace named Kaumodakī, held in Nārāyaṇa's hand,
always destroys spirits that cause epilepsy and the like.
Likewise, the sharp-edged discus burns up his enemies,
and His conch dispels yātudhānas, piśācas, and the like.
In this way, Keśava wards off his distress in every manner.

3.1.s: mahālayaṃ na kuryādyo dvādaśyāṃ manujā dhama .. 1 ..
3.1.d: महालयं न कुर्याद्यो द्वादश्यां मनुजा धम .. 1 ..
3.1.m: The lowest of men who does not perform the Mahālaya [śrāddha] on the twelfth,

3.1.s: tasya kṣetrāṇi saṃpacca vinaśyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ ..
3.1.d: तस्य क्षेत्राणि संपच्च विनश्यंति न संशयः ..
3.1.m: his fields and wealth are destroyed beyond doubt.
Spirits causing epilepsy and the like, very powerful enemies,
and yātudhānas torment him who has turned away from Viṣṇu.
And he is cast into the hell named Asthibhedana.
He who, filled with devotion, performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the twelfth lunar day,
his ancestors indeed remain pleased for six hundred thousand kalpas;
and the ancestors grant him an unbroken lineage.
If a man performs the Mahālaya śrāddha with devotion on the thirteenth lunar day,
the blessed Kāmadeva, lord of Rati, is pleased with him.
Pleasures such as garlands and sandalwood, and charming women—
all are forever accomplished for him by the grace of Kāmadeva,
and from birth until death he experiences only happiness.

3.1.s: yo na kuryāttrayodaśyāṃ na ca śrāddhaṃ mahālayam ..
3.1.d: यो न कुर्यात्त्रयोदश्यां न च श्राद्धं महालयम् ..
3.1.m: He who does not perform the Mahālaya śrāddha on the thirteenth lunar day,
Kāmadeva turns away from him and destroys his women and pleasures;
he causes him to fall into the hell called Rolling on a Bed of Coals.
He who performs the Mahālaya on the thirteenth lunar day on behalf of his ancestors,
his ancestors indeed remain pleased for a thousand thousand kalpas,
and the hosts of ancestors then bestow an unbroken lineage.
If a man performs the Mahālaya śrāddha with devotion on the fourteenth lunar day,
the blessed Śiva remains vigilant to grant his desired wish;
having taught knowledge of Śiva, he also grants union [with himself].
Ten thousand acts of drinking alcohol and ten thousand acts of stealing gold,
perish that very instant by virtue of the Mahālaya on the fourteenth;
even the guilt of associating with Caṇḍāla and Śūdra women is destroyed.
The abundant attainment of the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and ten thousand Pauṇḍarīka sacrifices
comes from the Mahālaya on the fourteenth lunar day.
He who does not perform this Mahālaya śrāddha on the fourteenth lunar day,
for ten million thousand kalpas and a hundred crore kalpas,
falls into the great blind well of saṃsāra, without any expiation.
Without having stolen gold and without having drunk alcohol,
that foolish-minded man is tainted by the sins of drinking alcohol and the like,
and sacrifices, even if performed according to rule, become fruitless.
But he who performs the Mahālaya śrāddha on the fourteenth lunar day,
for a hundred thousand crore thousand and a hundred thousand crore hundred
kalpas his ancestors are truly satisfied, without a doubt;
and the ancestors residing in hell go to heaven, greatly delighted;
and the hosts of ancestors then grant an unbroken lineage.

3.1.s: amāyāṃ tu naro bhaktyā śrāddhaṃ kuryānmahālayam .. 3.1.36.120 ..
3.1.d: अमायां तु नरो भक्त्या श्राद्धं कुर्यान्महालयम् .. 3.1.36.120 ..
3.1.m: If a man performs the Mahālaya śrāddha with devotion on the new moon day,

3.1.s: pitṝṇāṃ tasya tṛptiḥ syādanaṃtā nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
3.1.d: पितॄणां तस्य तृप्तिः स्यादनंता नात्र संशयः ..
3.1.m: the satisfaction of his ancestors will be endless, of this there is no doubt.

3.1.s: sudhāmāsvādya yā tṛptirdevānāṃ divi vai bhavet .. 21 ..
3.1.d: सुधामास्वाद्य या तृप्तिर्देवानां दिवि वै भवेत् .. 21 ..
3.1.m: Whatever satisfaction the gods in heaven obtain from tasting nectar,
such endless satisfaction comes from the Mahālaya on the new moon day.
The new moon day is very meritorious, saluted by ancestors and gods,

3.1.s: śāṃtā hyeṣā tu paramā śivasya ca mahāpriyā ..
3.1.d: शांता ह्येषा तु परमा शिवस्य च महाप्रिया ..
3.1.m: truly peaceful, supreme, and very dear to Śiva.
On it, during the Mahālaya śrāddha, one should feed those most learned in the Veda.

3.1.s: tena tṛptiḥ pitṝṇāṃ syādanaṃtā tuṣyate śivaḥ ..
3.1.d: तेन तृप्तिः पितॄणां स्यादनंता तुष्यते शिवः ..
3.1.m: By this, the satisfaction of the ancestors becomes endless, and Śiva is pleased;
the five great sins, beginning with killing a brahmin, perish.
All sacrifices with their priestly fees become properly performed,
and all eternal duties become carried out according to rule.
He by whom the Mahālaya śrāddha is performed on the new moon day,
knowing oneness with the inner Brahman, attains union [with it], without a doubt.
He who, senseless, does not perform the Mahālaya on the new moon day,
even if his ancestors have gone to the world of Brahmā, they go to hell,
and the lineage of that fool is severed at that very moment.

3.1.s: sa eva hi mahānartho yadamāyāṃ tithau naraiḥ .. 28 ..
3.1.d: स एव हि महानर्थो यदमायां तिथौ नरैः .. 28 ..
3.1.m: Indeed, that is a great disaster when, on the new moon day, by men
for the purpose of the Mahālaya, the foremost brahmins are not fed according to rule.
When the month of Bhādrapada arrives, the ancestral deities dance, [thinking:]
“May my sons feed the best of the twice-born on our behalf!

3.1.s: tena no narakakleśo na bhaviṣyati dāruṇaḥ .. 3.1.36.130 ..
3.1.d: तेन नो नरकक्लेशो न भविष्यति दारुणः .. 3.1.36.130 ..
3.1.m: Thereby no dreadful suffering of hell will befall us,
and our dwelling will be in the world of heaven as long as the moon and stars endure.”
When the month of Bhādrapada arrives, which brings satisfaction to the ancestors,
one should feed one brahmin daily with devotion;
the ancestors born in the paternal and maternal lines obtain satisfaction.
The wise man should especially feed brahmins during the dark fortnight,
preceded by anointing with oil, with ghee, lentil soup, and grains.
his ancestors, highly delighted, will drink nectar until the end of the kalpa.
Beginning from the seventh day of the dark fortnight, every day men
should feed brahmins, three at a time, having worshipped them, until the new moon.
Beginning from the twelfth day, one must without fail feed three brahmins;
otherwise there would be a loss of wealth, and one would become possessed of severe poverty.
Abandoning stinginess with money, [one should feed] brahmins with broth, clarified butter, and the like,
with milk, rice cooked in milk, curd, sweet cakes, and so forth,
and with various kinds of drinks, foods to be licked, sucked, and chewed,
one should feed the foremost knowers of the Veda so that they become satisfied.

3.1.s: tena brahmā hariḥ śaṃbhustṛptāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ..38..
3.1.d: तेन ब्रह्मा हरिः शंभुस्तृप्ताः स्युर्नात्र संशयः..38..
3.1.m: By this, Brahmā, Hari, and Śambhu will be satisfied; of this there is no doubt.
So too the ancestors such as the Agniṣvāttas, and the deities headed by Indra;
what is the use of saying much here? By this, the three worlds are pleased.
According to the rule of the Pārvaṇa [rite], one should perform the Mahālaya during the śrāddha.
A man in the Mahālaya-śrāddha [should feed] ancestors of the father's lineage, like the fathers,
and with joy he should also feed ancestors of the mother's lineage for the sake of welfare;
and he should give a sacrificial fee according to his capacity, in accordance with his means.
In that Mahālaya-śrāddha, one must not practice deception regarding money.
The sacrificial fee, indeed, is declared to be the leader of sacrifices;
just as a cart devoid of leaders [to draw it] will fail on the road,
so too this ancestral sacrifice devoid of a fee is ruined.
Therefore, even a small fee should be given in sacrifices by one who knows.
Even by widowed women without sons, the Mahālaya [rite]
must be performed for the sake of their husbands by means of lavish feeding;
otherwise there would be a loss of dharma, and a great hell would be [their lot].

3.1.s: māsi bhādrapade prāpte yo na kuryānmahālayam ..
3.1.d: मासि भाद्रपदे प्राप्ते यो न कुर्यान्महालयम् ..
3.1.m: When the month of Bhādrapada has arrived, whoever does not perform the Mahālaya,
his family meets destruction, and he incurs the sin of killing a brahmin.
Those possessed of faith who perform the Mahālaya for the ancestors,
their lineage will not be broken, and their prosperity will be imperishable.
"Ālaya" is indeed declared to mean an abode; "maha" is said to mean auspiciousness;
because it is the abode of auspicious things, it is called "Mahālaya".
Therefore, a mortal should perform the Mahālaya for the attainment of auspiciousness;
inauspiciousness would befall him if he should not perform the Mahālaya.
Even if one did not perform the śrāddha on the day of death of his father and mother,
an intelligent man, even without remembering [the date], should perform the Mahālaya-śrāddha.
If there is no capacity to perform the Mahālaya-śrāddha,
a man should perform that Mahālaya for the ancestors even by begging.
He should beg wealth and grain from distinguished brahmins;
he should never take wealth or grain from fallen persons.
If grain, wealth, and the like are not obtained from brahmins,
he should beg from noble kṣatriyas, with the desire to perform the Mahālaya.
If kings are not givers, he should beg even from vaiśyas;

3.1.s: vaiśyā api hi dātāro yadi loke na saṃti vai .. 54 ..
3.1.d: वैश्या अपि हि दातारो यदि लोके न संति वै .. 54 ..
3.1.m: if even vaiśyas are indeed not givers in the world,
in the month of Bhādrapada he should give a mouthful of grass to a cow for the satisfaction of the ancestors;
or, going outside into the forest, he should weep.
Beating his own belly with both hands, shedding tears,
a man in those forest regions should loudly speak thus:

3.1.s: śṛṇvaṃtu pitaraḥ sarve matkulīnā vaco mama ..
3.1.d: शृण्वंतु पितरः सर्वे मत्कुलीना वचो मम ..
3.1.m: "May all the ancestors of my family listen to my word!
I am poor, miserable, shameless, and a doer of cruel deeds.
The month of Bhādrapada, increasing the delight of the ancestors, has arrived,

3.1.s: karttuṃ mahālayaśrāddhaṃ na ca me śaktirasti vai .. 58 ..
3.1.d: कर्त्तुं महालयश्राद्धं न च मे शक्तिरस्ति वै .. 58 ..
3.1.m: and indeed I have no ability to perform the Mahālaya-śrāddha.

3.1.s: bhramitvāpi mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ na me kiṃcana labhyate ..
3.1.d: भ्रमित्वापि महीं कृत्स्नां न मे किंचन लभ्यते ..
3.1.m: Even having wandered over the entire earth, nothing is obtained by me;
therefore, I do not perform the Mahālaya-śrāddha for you.

3.1.s: kṣamadhvaṃ mama tadyūyaṃ bhavaṃto hi dayāparāḥ ..
3.1.d: क्षमध्वं मम तद्यूयं भवंतो हि दयापराः ..
3.1.m: Pardon this of mine, for you are supreme in compassion!"
Thus the poor man should weep in the forest lands.
Hearing his weeping, the ancestors born of that family,
delighted, surely attain satisfaction, just as the gods do upon drinking nectar.
Just as there would be satisfaction when a crowd of brahmins is fed for the sake of the Mahālaya,
in the same way the satisfaction of the ancestors comes about through a mouthful given to a cow and through weeping in the forest.
If in the month of Bhādrapada there should be an obstacle due to birth- or death-impurity and the like,
when the days of impurity have passed, he should perform it until the sun enters Scorpio.
For the Mahālaya, a wise man should invite nine brahmins:
he should invite one for the father, and likewise [one] for the paternal grandfather;
the twice-born should likewise invite one for the paternal great-grandfather,

3.1.s: tathā mātāmahārthaṃ tu ekaṃ vai vṛṇuyāddvijam .. 65 ..
3.1.d: तथा मातामहार्थं तु एकं वै वृणुयाद्द्विजम् .. 65 ..
3.1.m: and he should indeed invite one twice-born for the maternal grandfather;
and he should invite a single twice-born for the maternal great-grandfather,
and he should invite one for the maternal great-great-grandfather;
likewise, he should invite two excellent twice-born for the Viśvedevas,
and he should invite one brahmin best versed in the Veda for Viṣṇu.
Thus he should invite nine brahmins in the Mahālaya śrāddha.
Or, he may choose a single brahmin for the paternal ancestral line,
or choose a single brahmin for the maternal grandfathers and others,
and one for the Viśvedevas, and likewise another for Viṣṇu.
Thus indeed, the intelligent man should choose four brahmins in the Mahālaya;
he should choose brahmins endowed with the Veda and of good character.
One who chooses those of bad character is indeed a destroyer of the śrāddha.
When the month of Bhādrapada has arrived, especially in the dark fortnight,

3.1.s: kuryā nmahālayaśrāddhaṃ yo naraḥ śraddhayā saha ..
3.1.d: कुर्या न्महालयश्राद्धं यो नरः श्रद्धया सह ..
3.1.m: the man who performs the Mahālaya śrāddha with faith,
has bathed in all the sacred fords, O Durācāra of great intellect!
Even a hundred sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma have been performed by him,
and gifts chief among which is the Tulāpuruṣa have indeed been given;
penances such as the Cāndrāyaṇa have certainly been performed, without doubt.
He obtains the fruit of reciting the four Vedas with their auxiliary limbs;
likewise he obtains the merit of chanting the great mantras beginning with the Gāyatrī;
he obtains the fruit of reciting the Itihāsas and Purāṇas.
There is no meritorious conduct equal to the Mahālaya on the surface of the earth.
Attainment of the worlds of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśāna comes from the Mahālaya.
A śrāddha such as the Mahālaya is regarded as both obligatory and optional.
Therefore, if it is not performed, a great sin of omission will arise;
and from its performance, the attainment of desires will come to be, without doubt.
By the performance of the Mahālaya, spirits, vetālas, and the like,
seizing spirits of epilepsy, and hosts of śākinīs and ḍākinīs,
yātudhānas, piśācas, and terrifying vetālas,
and likewise other spirits, perish at that very moment.
By the performance of the Mahālaya, one enjoys abundant prosperity.
In ancient times, King Daśaratha, by the instruction of Vasiṣṭha,

3.1.s: māsi bhādrapade prāpte kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ mahālayam .. 81 ..
3.1.d: मासि भाद्रपदे प्राप्ते कृत्वा श्राद्धं महालयम् .. 81 ..
3.1.m: having performed the Mahālaya śrāddha when the month of Bhādrapada arrived,
obtained four sons beginning with Rāma, approved by the world;
he attained fortune surpassing the world and supreme fame.
By the performance of the Mahālaya, Yayāti, best of kings,
obtained noble sons headed by Yadu, who increased the dynasty;
through the merit of the śrāddha he attained heaven, which is hard for others to attain.
Duṣyanta obtained Bharata by the ritual procedure of the Mahālaya.
By the ritual procedure of the Mahālaya, Nala, the husband of Damayantī,
crossed over an exceedingly great hardship and regained this earth;
he subdued terrible Kali and his enemy Puṣkara,
and obtained an exceedingly righteous son named Indrasena.
Great King Hariścandra, by the ritual procedure of the Mahālaya,
the best of the truthful, was freed from the sorrow caused by Viśvāmitra;

3.1.s: lebhe caṃdravatīṃ bhāryāṃ lohitāśvaṃ sutaṃ punaḥ ..
3.1.d: लेभे चंद्रवतीं भार्यां लोहिताश्वं सुतं पुनः ..
3.1.m: he regained his wife Candravatī and his son Rohitāśva.
By the ritual procedure of the Mahālaya, the mighty son of Kṛtavīrya
attained sovereignty over the eighteen continents.
Even Rāma in the Daṇḍaka forest, by the ritual procedure of the Mahālaya,

3.1.s: hatvā tu rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye sītāṃ punaravāptavān ..
3.1.d: हत्वा तु रावणं संख्ये सीतां पुनरवाप्तवान् ..
3.1.m: having slain Rāvaṇa in battle, regained Sītā.
By the performance of the Mahālaya, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma,
having crossed over the ocean of sorrow, slew the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
By the performance of the Mahālaya, Vasiṣṭha, best of sages,
Atri, Bhṛgu, Kutsa, Gautama, and Aṅgiras,
Kaśyapa, Bharadvāja, Viśvāmitra, the jar-born [Agastya],
Parāśara, Mṛkaṇḍa, and other foremost sages,
having duly performed the incomparable Mahālaya śrāddha, [attained their desires]
became the dwelling places of the eight perfections such as minuteness, / and likewise of vows and austerities;
and thus surpassed the universe.
Indeed, all those best among sages became liberated while living.
Therefore, the Mahālaya śrāddha must be performed by one who desires prosperity.
Therefore, even today, O Durācāra, whoever does not perform the Mahālaya [rite]
will face great fear from spirits, vetālas, and the like.
From not performing the Mahālaya [rite], one would become a vetāla.
This spirit that possessed you was a brahmin in a previous birth,
holy, named Vedanidhi, born in the lineage of Bharadvāja;
and living in the village named Kuśasthalī, that noble-minded man
did not perform this Mahālaya śrāddha according to rule.
Then, because of a curse from his ancestors, he became a vetāla.
Therefore, O Durācāra, in the month of Bhādrapada, for the ancestors,
feed the brahmins with devotion, with food possessing the six tastes.

3.1.s: dāridryaṃ tena te na syātsukhīcaiva bhavānbhavet ..
3.1.d: दारिद्र्यं तेन ते न स्यात्सुखीचैव भवान्भवेत् ..
3.1.m: Thereby you will not have poverty, and you will certainly be happy.

3.1.s: mahāpātaki saṃsargaṃ mā kuru tvamitaḥ param .. 1 ..
3.1.d: महापातकि संसर्गं मा कुरु त्वमितः परम् .. 1 ..
3.1.m: Henceforth, do not keep company with great sinners.
[Now that] you have experienced the suffering that arose from being seized by a vetāla,

3.1.d: गच्छ त्वमनुजानामि स्वदेशं प्रति मा चिरम् .. 2 ..
3.1.m: go to your own country; I give you leave; do not delay.”
Thus addressed by the sage, the yogin Dattātreya,
having bowed to him, he departed to his country, his inner self fulfilled.

3.1.s: gatvā ca svagṛhaṃ vipro durācāro dvijottamāḥ ..
3.1.d: गत्वा च स्वगृहं विप्रो दुराचारो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
3.1.m: And having gone to his own home, the brahmin Durācāra, O best among brahmins,
freed from the fear of the vetāla, cast off the armor of sin.
Following the path taught by Dattātreya, with a delighted mind,
having abandoned the company of sinners, he was dedicated to the conduct of his own stage of life.
By the greatness of bathing at the sacred ford of Rāmacandra’s Dhanuṣkoṭi,

3.1.s: dehāṃte paramāṃ muktiṃ durācāro yayau tadā .. 6 ..
3.1.d: देहांते परमां मुक्तिं दुराचारो ययौ तदा .. 6 ..
3.1.m: at the end of his body Durācāra then attained supreme liberation.
The venerable Sūta said:
Thus the sacred liberation of Durācāra has been related to you.
This is that sacred Dhanuṣkoṭi, destroyer of great sins,
where merely by a bath Durācāra was completely liberated.

3.1.s: athavā dhanuṣaḥ koṭeriyattā kiṃ hi vai bhavet .. 8 ..
3.1.d: अथवा धनुषः कोटेरियत्ता किं हि वै भवेत् .. 8 ..
3.1.m: Indeed, what limit could there be to [the power of] Dhanuṣkoṭi,
which can destroy even sins that have no expiation?
Whatever sins there are that are devoid of atonement,
even those perish here from plunging into Dhanuṣkoṭi.

3.1.s: śūdreṇa pūjitaṃ liṃgaṃ viṣṇuṃ vā yo nameddvijaḥ .. 3.1.36.210 ..
3.1.m: If a twice-born bows to a liṅga or Viṣṇu worshipped by a Śūdra,
no expiation for him has been stated by the Smṛtis or the supreme seers;
even that sin of his would perish from plunging into Dhanuṣkoṭi.
For men who revile brahmins, no expiation exists;
and for betrayers of trust and the ungrateful, there is no redemption.
For those devoted to a brother’s wife, no expiation exists;
nor for those devoted to Śūdra food, nor for those whose minds delight in reviling the Veda.
For sellers of daughters, O brahmins, and likewise sellers of horses,
sellers of deities, those whose minds are intent on selling the Veda,
for men who sell dharma, and likewise sellers of vows,
and for men who sell sacred fords, no expiation exists.

3.1.s: teṣāṃ pāpāni naśyaṃti dhanuṣkoṭau nima jjanāt ..
3.1.d: तेषां पापानि नश्यंति धनुष्कोटौ निम ज्जनात् ..
3.1.m: Their sins perish from plunging into Dhanuṣkoṭi.
For those whose minds are bent on harming mothers, harming fathers, or harming ascetics,
and those devoted to reviling the guru, those whose minds delight in reviling Śiva,
those intent on reviling Viṣṇu, and those whose minds delight in reviling ascetics,
and for those who disparage virtuous narratives, no expiation exists.
Yet for them, purification will take place here through bathing in Dhanuṣkoṭi.

3.1.s: evaṃ vaḥ kathitaṃ viprā dhanuṣkoṭestu vaibhavam ..
3.1.d: एवं वः कथितं विप्रा धनुष्कोटेस्तु वैभवम् ..
3.1.m: Thus, O brahmins, the majesty of Dhanuṣkoṭi has been narrated to you,
hearing which a mortal on earth is liberated from all sins.

3.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतु माहात्म्ये धनुष्कोटिप्रशंसायां दुराचारसंसर्गदोषशांतिवर्णनंनाम षट्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 36 ..
3.1.m: Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Pacification of the Fault of Association with Durācāra in the Praise of Dhanuṣkoṭi,' in the Setumāhātmya of the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the third [part of] the venerable Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

3.1.m: Śrī Sūta said: / “O, all you whose wealth is austerity, dwellers of Naimiṣāraṇya! / All the twenty-four tīrthas, beginning with Rāmadhanuṣkoṭi and Cakratīrtha, / have now been narrated to you by me. / Beyond this, what further marvel do you wish to hear?” / The sages said: / “We wish to hear the māhātmya of Kṣīrakuṇḍa, O sage, / near which you previously mentioned Cakratīrtha was located. / Where is that Kṣīrakuṇḍa, what is its grandeur, / and how did its renown as ‘Kṣīrakuṇḍa’ come about? / You ought to speak of this in detail to us who are full of faith.” / Śrī Sūta said: / “I shall tell you, O all sages; listen with attentive minds. / Not far to the west of the highly sacred Devīpura, / there is a most great place known as Phullagrāma, / starting from which the bridge was built across the great ocean by Rāma. / That city named Phullagrāma is indeed a most sacred field. / And right there is Kṣīrakuṇḍa, destroyer of the greatest sins, / which bestows liberation even by darśana, touch, meditation, and recitation of its praise. / The renown of that sacred tīrtha as ‘Kṣīrakuṇḍa’ / I shall reverently tell you; listen with faith. / Long ago, indeed, a sage named Mudgala, who followed the path taught in the Veda, / performed an excellent sacrifice on the shore of the southern ocean in most sacred Phullagrāma, / bringing delight to Nārāyaṇa. / With a gracious mind, Viṣṇu was well pleased by his sacrifice, / and appeared before him in the sacrificial enclosure, O best of brahmins! / Seeing that Viṣṇu whose body was adorned by Lakṣmī, / whose bodily luster was like a dark cloud, adorned with yellow garments, / mounted on the son of Vinatā, his chest adorned with the Kaustubha gem, / his four arms shining with conch, discus, mace, and lotus, / overcome by devotion and adorned with bristling hair, / Mudgala praised him with words pleasing to the ear. / Mudgala said: / ‘To the creator of the world first, then next to its protector, / and then thereafter to its destroyer, reverence to you, Nārāyaṇa! / Reverence to him in the form of a fish, to the tortoise, the conscious Self! / Reverence to him whose body is a boar! Reverence to him who has the form of a lion! / Reverence to you, the dwarf; reverence to you, the son of Jamadagni! / Reverence to you, the descendant of Raghu! Reverence to you, Balabhadra! / To Kṛṣṇa, to Kalkin, reverence to you whose form is knowledge! / Protect me, ocean of compassion, Nārāyaṇa, Lord of the world! / Shameless, wretched, cruel, malicious, deceitful, emaciated, / greedy only for the wives, wealth, and fields of others, / with a mind beset by envy—protect me, O Hari, through compassion!’ / Thus praised in person by Mudgala, O best of brahmins, / Hari addressed that sage Mudgala with a voice deep as a cloud.”

3.1.m:
Śrī Hari said:
“I am pleased with this hymn of praise, Mudgala, and with your sacrifice.
I have come to your sacrifice in visible form to consume the oblation.”
Thus addressed by Hari there, Mudgala, with a joyful mind,
spoke to Adhokṣaja, filled with supreme devotion.
Mudgala said:
“I have attained my goal, Hṛṣīkeśa! My wife has achieved blessedness!
Today my birth has borne fruit; indeed, today my austerity has borne fruit!
Today my lineage has borne fruit; indeed, today my sons have borne fruit!
My hermitage has borne fruit this very day; everything of mine has borne fruit today,
since you have come here to my sacrificial enclosure to consume the oblation!
Whom the yogins, devoted to yoga, seek in their hearts,
that very you I see today face-to-face; this sacrifice of mine has borne fruit!”
Having said this, worshiping that Viṣṇu with a seat and other offerings,
with sandalpastes and other flowers, and offering arghya to Viṣṇu,
he gladly presented to Viṣṇu the oblation consisting of puroḍāśa cake and other offerings.

When that oblation was consumed by the all-powerful Viṣṇu,
all the thirty [gods] along with Agni were satisfied, O brahmins.
The officiating priests, the patron of the sacrifice, and likewise the brahmins present there,
and whatever living beings there were in this world, whether moving or stationary—
the entire world was satisfied when the oblation was consumed by Viṣṇu.
Then Hari, with a gracious mind, addressed Mudgala:
“I am pleased. Here I am as a granter of boons; choose a boon, O you of good vows.” / When Keśava had spoken thus, the great seer addressed him.
When this was said by Keśava, the great seer then spoke to him:
Mudgala said:
“Since my oblation in the sacrifice was consumed by you in visible form,
by that alone I have attained my goal; what boon could be greater than this?
Even so, Lord Viṣṇu, may my devotion to you be ever steadfast
and free of deceit; this is my first boon.

Saying “Om,” Surabhi, thus addressed by Nārāyaṇa, [filled the lake].
Then Lord Nārāyaṇa said to Mudgala:
“Constantly with the milk of Surabhi remaining in this lake,
every day, evening and morning, to the fire here for my pleasure,
offer oblations, O fortunate one! By that I shall be pleased with you.
Through my pleasure, all accomplishment shall be yours, O Mudgala!
This sacred ford shall become famous under the name Kṣīrasaras.
For those who have bathed in this sacred ford of Kṣīrasaras, the five great sins
and other sins as well shall perish in an instant.
And you, Mudgala, free from bondage, come to me at the end of your body.”
Having spoken thus and embraced that Mudgala, Lord Viṣṇu,
saluted by him, vanished right there.

Śrī Sūta said:
Thus, O best of brahmins, has this been told to you by me,
how this sacred ford came to be named Kṣīrasaras in ancient times.
This holy Kṣīrasaras is renowned in all the worlds,
where Kadru, the wife of sage Kaśyapa, O best of brahmins,
having bathed at the word of her husband, endowed with vows,
was immediately freed from the fault of deceitfully conquering her co-wife.
Therefore, the people of pure minds who bathe in this sacred ford,
freed from bondage, liberated, performers of meritorious deeds—
what need have they of sacrifices, or of the Vedas, or of resorting to sacred fords,
or of prayers and vows, for those who behold Kṣīrakuṇḍa?
A man whose body is touched by the breeze of Kṣīrakuṇḍa, O brahmins,
reaches the world of Brahmā and is fully liberated right there.
Those plunged in this Kṣīrakuṇḍa, even despising Yama,

For those plunged in this Kṣīrakuṇḍa, the Vaitaraṇī river becomes cool,
and all the hells become utterly useless.
Ah, while that Kṣīrakuṇḍa, equal to the wish-granting cow, exists,
the man who wanders elsewhere to bathe, O best of brahmins,
goes after the milk of the calotropis plant even when cow's milk is at hand!
Indeed, for those who have bathed in this Kṣīrakuṇḍa, nothing is unobtainable.
Liberation is placed right in their hand; what is the use of other long speeches?
Raising my arm, I tell you—truly, truly I tell you:
He who reads this chapter, or hears it with concentrated mind,
he attains the highest fruit of bathing in Kṣīrakuṇḍa.
Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, named “Description of the Nature of Kṣīrakuṇḍa,” in the praise of Kṣīrakuṇḍa within the Setumāhātmya in the third [section], the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
The seers said:
“O Sūta, how was Kadru freed by plunging into Kṣīrakuṇḍa?
How did she, whose resolve was sinful, act deceitfully toward her co-wife?

3.1.m: Then Vinatā and Kadrū, both having made a wager on servitude,
went with eager haste to see the horse of the king of gods.
Passing over the ocean, the lord of rivers, the source of the moon, / the conch, ruby, pearl, and Airāvata,
which is the couch of Hari at the dissolution of an age / when he adopts yogic sleep,
Kadrū and Vinatā crossed over the ocean, the lord of rivers,
and going there, they saw the horse, the mount of the king of gods.
Seeing the horse with a black tail, Vinatā became distressed.
Kadrū assigned the distressed Vinatā to the work of a slave.
In the meantime, Tārkṣya, breaking open the egg like fire,
appeared, O chiefs of brahmins, his body as large as a mountain.
Seeing the majesty of his body, the three worlds became terrified.
Then the gods praised Garuḍa, the best of birds.
Thinking: “Seeing the majesty of this body, the three worlds would be terrified,”
he withdrew his exceedingly terrifying form,
placed Aruṇa on his back, and approached his mother.
Then Kadrū said to Vinatā, who was bowed down and deeply distressed:
“Slave woman, I intend to go to the abode of the serpents;
let your son Garuḍa carry me and my sons!”
Then Vinatā spoke to her son Garuḍa:

Vinatā carried Kadrū, and Garuḍa carried all of them.
Then the serpents, coming close to the sun, were struck by its rays.
Kadrū praised the wielder of the thunderbolt to appease the burning heat of her sons.
The king of gods quenched all their burning heat with downpours of water.
Then the serpents being carried by the mighty Garuḍa,
having soon reached that region, said to the son of Vinatā:

3.1.m: “We are all eager to go and see another island;
carry us there at once, Garuḍa, you son of a slave woman!”
Then Garuḍa asked his mother Vinatā, O brahmins:
“Why do I carry these, and why do you always carry her?
Why do these crawling creatures call me ‘son of a slave woman’?
Tell me all this in truth, mother, as I ask you.”
Thus questioned by him, the mother spoke to her son Garuḍa:
“By my cruel sister, my son, I was defeated through deceit.
I am now her slave woman, and therefore you are the son of a slave woman.
Therefore you carry the serpents, and I always carry her.”
She related to him the whole account from the beginning.
Then Garuḍa, the son of Vinatā, said to his mother:
“What must I do now for the sake of your release from this servitude?”
Thus questioned by her son, Vinatā then spoke to him:
"Ask the serpents, Garuḍa, concerning my release from bondage:

3.1.d: युष्माकं मातुः किं कार्यं मयेति वदताधुना .. 39 ..
3.1.m: 'Tell [me] now: what task must I perform for you, my mother's [masters]?'"
Addressed in this way by his mother, Garuḍa went to the serpents
and asked, O best of brahmins; they too then said to him:
"When you quickly bring nectar from the abode of the immortals,
then indeed, O Vainateya, shall your mother be freed today from bondage."
Then, having returned to his mother, Garuḍa bowed and said:
"O Mother, provide me food as I depart to bring the nectar."

May the gods, led by the Maruts, protect your wings and other limbs!"
Strengthened thus by his mother's blessings, Garuḍa went forth.
Approaching the home of the Śabaras, as he ate, into his open mouth

Then that brahmin also entered his throat, O best of sages.
To that vipra who was burning his throat, the son of Vinatā said:

3.1.m: "O vipra, even if sinful, you must not be killed; come out of here!"
Thus addressed, the vipra then replied to Garuḍa:

3.1.d: किराती मम भार्यापि निर्गंतव्या मया सह .. 49 ..
3.1.m: "My wife, a Kirāta woman, must also come out along with me."
"So be it," the lord of birds said to that vipra.
Then Garuḍa spat out the vipra together with his wife.
The vipra too departed with the Niṣāda woman to regions of his choosing.
Then, having devoured the Śabaras, Garuḍa, the best of birds,
swiftly approached his father Kaśyapa.
Asked by him, "Where are you going?", Garuḍa replied to him:
"I have come to fetch the nectar to release my mother from bondage.
Even after consuming many Kirātas, I feel no satisfaction.
A boundless hunger afflicts me day and night, O holy one.
Bestow on me food that will relieve it, O rich in austerity,
so that I may be able, Father, to fetch the nectar with my strength."
Addressed in this way, Kaśyapa spoke to his son born of Vinatā.
Kaśyapa said:
"Formerly there was a sage named Vibhāvasu; he had a younger brother,
a brother named Supratīka. Both of them became bitter enemies over family property.
Overcome with great fury, the two twice-born cursed each other:
Supratīka became an elephant, and Vibhāvasu became a tortoise.
Thus, due to a dispute over wealth, the two brothers cursed each other.
The elephant is six yojanas in height and twice as long in length.
The tortoise is three yojanas in height and ten yojanas in breadth.
These two, having formed mutual enmity, [dwell] in this lake, O bird.
Remembering their past enmity, they fight with the desire to conquer.

Thus instructed by his father, the bird went to that elephant and tortoise.
Lifting up those two of gigantic body and immense strength and prowess,

Seeing the king of birds arrived there, O equals of the twice-born,
a very tall, great tree growing on its bank, named Rohiṇa,
said this to Vainateya of immense strength and prowess:
"Alight on this branch of mine, a hundred yojanas long;
perched here, devour the elephant and tortoise, O best of birds."
Thus addressed by the tree, that bird swift as thought settled there.
Under his weight, that branch of the tree broke, O best of brahmins.
Seeing the Vālakhilya sages hanging head-downward on it,
fearing they might fall, Garuḍa seized that branch.

Now at that moment, an evil omen appeared in heaven.
Seeing the portent, the enemy of Bala asked his own priest,
again and again: "O Jīva, what is the cause of this portent here?"
Then, O best of brahmins, Bṛhaspati spoke to Śakra:
Bṛhaspati said:
"Formerly, O Hari, the sage Kāśyapa performed a sacrificial rite;
all the seers, gods, siddhas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and kinnaras
he dispatched, O brahmins, to secure the sacrificial provisions.
Seeing the Vālakhilyas, carrying their provisions, short [and] only thumb-sized,
sinking in the water of a cow's footprint, you laughed.
Insulted by you, the Vālakhilyas, enraged then, O Hari,
offered oblations into the sacrificial fire, their faces blazing with anger:
'May there be an enemy of the lord of the gods, causing fear to him, born as a son to Kaśyapa!'
Today his son Garuḍa, eager to carry off the nectar,
is approaching. Due to that, this portent has appeared."
Thus addressed, Indra spoke to the gods headed by Agni:
"A bird is coming to steal the nectar; let it be guarded!"
Thus urged by Indra, the gods, bearing weapons, guarded the nectar.
The king of birds then approached the gods who bore weapons;

Bhauvana, the guardian of the nectar, was torn to pieces by the beak of the bird.
Then the gods repeatedly struck Garuḍa with various weapons;

Garuḍa hurled the gods headed by Agni far away with his two wings.
Cast off by his wings, the gods then became exceedingly enraged,

Then, with swift speed, the son of Vinatā raised dust
with his wings that obstructed the gods' sight; / the best of the thirty [gods] quelled that dust with wind.
The Rudras, the Vasus, likewise the Ādityas, the Maruts, and the other gods,
Garuḍa distressed with his wings and beak, O brahmins.
When the gods had fled, he beheld a fire before him;
and he set out to extinguish the fire that was blazing all around.

All those serpents then departed to bathe in order to consume the nectar. / 3.1.38.110

And through contact with the nectar, the darbha grasses attained purity. / 13

3.1.m: did not accept that Kadrū at all, remembering the sin committed by her.
Then Vinatā bowed down and spoke these words to Kaśyapa:
“O lord, accept this sister of mine, O treasure of mercy!
The sin that has now been committed out of ignorance by the bewildered Kadrū—
you ought to forgive all of it, for virtuous people are compassionate by nature.”
Addressed thus by the mother of Garuḍa, the sage Kaśyapa

3.1.s: uvāca vinate naināṃ vinā pāpasya niṣkṛtim .. 31 ..
3.1.d: उवाच विनते नैनां विना पापस्य निष्कृतिम् .. 31 ..
3.1.m: said: “O Vinatā, without atonement for her sin,
I will not accept this woman of evil conduct; three times I swear this to you.”
Having heard Kaśyapa's words, Vinatā spoke again:

3.1.s: bhaginyā mama pāpasya brahmaṃstvaṃ brūhi niṣkṛtim ..
3.1.d: भगिन्या मम पापस्य ब्रह्मंस्त्वं ब्रूहि निष्कृतिम् ..
3.1.m: “O brahmin, tell the atonement for my sister's sin,
by which she may become fit to attend upon you.”
Addressed in this manner by her, O brahmins, Kaśyapa the son of Marīci then,
having meditated for a moment in his mind, afterward spoke as follows:
“On the shore of the southern ocean, in Phullagrāma that bestows liberation,
there is a sacred ford named Kṣīrasaras that destroys sin.
By mere ritual ablution in that sacred ford, her fault will perish.
Even with ten thousand penances, without plunging into that sacred ford,

3.1.d: न नश्यत्येष दोषो ऽस्यास्तदेषा यातु तत्सरः ..
3.1.m: this fault of hers will not perish; therefore let her go to that lake.”
When her husband had spoken thus, Kadrū bowed to that best of brahmins,
and immediately set out for Kṣīrasaras, accompanied by her sons.

3.1.s: sā kadrūḥ putra sahitā gatvā katipayairdinaiḥ .. 38 ..
3.1.d: सा कद्रूः पुत्र सहिता गत्वा कतिपयैर्दिनैः .. 38 ..
3.1.m: Going together with her sons, that Kadrū, after some days,
reached the holy Kṣīrasaras, restrained and with senses subdued.
Making her resolve according to the rules, she bathed in Kṣīrakuṇḍa.
Fasting for three days, she bathed in the water of that Kṣīrasaras.
On the fourth day, as she was devoutly performing her ritual ablution,
a bodiless voice traveling through the sky arose, O best of brahmins.
The bodiless voice said:
“O Kadrū, by plunging in here, from the fault of winning by deceit
you are freed, and fit to serve your husband without doubt.
Even the curse pronounced by Garuḍa has been dissolved here by your bath.

3.1.s: gaccha bhartṛsakāśaṃ tvaṃ so'pi tvāṃ svīkariṣyati ..
3.1.d: गच्छ भर्तृसकाशं त्वं सोऽपि त्वां स्वीकरिष्यति ..
3.1.m: Go to the presence of your husband; he too will accept you.”
Having spoken thus, the bodiless voice from the sky fell silent.

3.1.s: tasyai vāce namaskṛtya kadrūḥ sā prītamānasā ..
3.1.d: तस्यै वाचे नमस्कृत्य कद्रूः सा प्रीतमानसा ..
3.1.m: Having bowed to that voice, Kadrū, with a delighted mind,
circumambulated the sacred ford, bowed down, and together with her sons
went near her husband out of eagerness to attend upon him.
Seeing her arrived, bathed in the water of Kṣīrasaras,

3.1.s: jñātvā vidhūtapāpāṃ ca kaśyapaḥ sa samādhinā ..
3.1.d: ज्ञात्वा विधूतपापां च कश्यपः स समाधिना ..
3.1.m: and knowing through meditation that her sins were wiped away, Kaśyapa
accepted that wife who was fit to serve him.
Thus has been recounted to you, O brahmins, the release from sin of Kadrū,
which bestows liberation on mortals by bathing in the holy water of Kṣīrasaras.
Whatever person hears or reads this chapter,
obtains the supreme fruit of a ritual ablution in Kṣīrakuṇḍa.
He enjoys the complete fruit of horse sacrifices and other rituals;
he certainly becomes [as if] bathed in all sacred fords beginning with the Gaṅgā.
Whoever reads this chapter praising Kṣīrakuṇḍa
attains the unbroken fruit of those who give a thousand cows.

3.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe setumāhātmye kṣīrakuṃḍapraśasāyāṃ kadrūkṛtacchaladoṣaśāṃtikathāvarṇanaṃ-nāmāṣṭatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 38 ..
3.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतुमाहात्म्ये क्षीरकुंडप्रशसायां कद्रूकृतच्छलदोषशांतिकथावर्णनं-नामाष्टत्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 38 ..
3.1.m: Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter named 'Description of the pacification of the fault of deceit committed by Kadrū, in the praise of Kṣīrakuṇḍa,' in the Setumāhātmya, in the Brahmakhaṇḍa, the third [part], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
The glorious Sūta said:
“Now, therefore, I will describe the majesty of Kapitīrtha.
That sacred ford was formerly, on Mount Gandhamādana,
created by all the monkeys for the benefit of all beings, O brahmins.
After Rāvaṇa and the other demons had been slain,

3.1.s: tīrthaṃ nirmāya tatraiva sasnuste kapayo mudā ..
3.1.d: तीर्थं निर्माय तत्रैव सस्नुस्ते कपयो मुदा ..
3.1.m: having created the sacred ford right there, those monkeys bathed with joy.

3.1.s: tīrthāya ca varaṃ prāduḥ kapayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ .. .. 3..
3.1.d: तीर्थाय च वरं प्रादुः कपयः कामरूपिणः .. .. 3..
3.1.m: And the monkeys, who could assume any form at will, granted a boon to the sacred ford:
‘Those who plunge into this sacred ford with minds intent on devotion
shall all partake of liberation, released from great sins.

3.1.s: atra tīrthe nimagnānāṃ na syānnarakajaṃ bhayam ..
3.1.d: अत्र तीर्थे निमग्नानां न स्यान्नरकजं भयम् ..
3.1.m: For those who plunge into this sacred ford there shall be no fear born of hell.

3.1.s: atra snātā narāḥ sarve dāridrayaṃ nāpnuvaṃti hi .. 5 ..
3.1.d: अत्र स्नाता नराः सर्वे दारिद्रयं नाप्नुवंति हि .. 5 ..
3.1.m: All men who have bathed here indeed never incur poverty.

3.1.s: atra tīrthe nimagnānāṃ yamapīḍāpi no bhavet ..
3.1.d: अत्र तीर्थे निमग्नानां यमपीडापि नो भवेत् ..
3.1.m: For those who plunge into this sacred ford there shall not even be torment inflicted by Yama.’
He who constantly says, "I will go to Kapitīrtha,"
and walks a hundred paces, O brahmins, shall go to the supreme abode.

3.1.s: etattīrthasamaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati .. 7 ..
3.1.d: एतत्तीर्थसमं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति .. 7 ..
3.1.m: A sacred ford equal to this sacred ford has never been, nor will ever be. // 7

3.1.s: evaṃ varaṃ tu te dattvā tīrthāyāsmai kapīśvarāḥ ..
3.1.d: एवं वरं तु ते दत्त्वा तीर्थायास्मै कपीश्वराः ..
3.1.m: Having thus granted a boon to this sacred ford, the monkey lords,
all bowing down to Rāma, son of Daśaratha, then made a request: // 8
"O Lord, let a wonderful boon be granted by you to this sacred ford!"
Beseeched by the monkeys, O brahmins, Rāmacandra, exceedingly delighted, // 9
granted a boon to that sacred ford for the sake of pleasing the monkeys:
"Those who bathe in this sacred ford shall obtain the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, // 10
the merit born of bathing at Prayāga, and likewise the fruit of all sacred fords;
may the unequalled fruit of sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma be theirs! // 11
So too, let there be the merit of chanting great mantras such as the Gāyatrī;
one obtains the full fruit of those men who bestow a thousand cows. // 12
One shall obtain the fruit of reciting the four Vedas completely;
one shall obtain the fruit of worshiping deities such as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa." // 13
Thus, O twice-born ones, this Rāma granted a boon to Kapitīrtha.

3.1.s: evaṃ rāmeṇa datte tu vare tatra kutūhalāt ..14..
3.1.d: एवं रामेण दत्ते तु वरे तत्र कुतूहलात् ..14..
3.1.m: When the boon was thus granted by Rāma there, out of curiosity, // 14
the three-eyed one [Śiva], Brahmā, the thousand-eyed one [Indra], and Yama;
Varuṇa, Agni, and Vāyu, Kubera, and the Moon as well; // 15
the Sun and Nirṛti, and the Sādhyas, and the Vasus;
and all the other gods, the Viśvedevas and the rest; // 16
Atri, Bhṛgu, and Kutsa, Gautama and Parāśara,
Kaṇva, Agastya, and Sutīkṣṇa, Viśvāmitra, and other sages; // 17
yogins such as Sanaka and others, and divine seers such as Nārada and others—
all then praised the sacred ford blessed with Rāma's boon in many ways. // 18
And they bathed in that sacred ford, which grants all desired things.
"Because this unsurpassed sacred ford was made by monkeys, // 19
it shall therefore go by the renown of 'Kapitīrtha' in the world!"
Thus spoke all those gods and sages. // 20
Therefore, Kapitīrtha must certainly be visited by seekers of liberation.
In ancient times, O twice-born ones, Rambhā, having turned into a stone through Kauśika's curse, // 21

3.1.s: tatra snātvā nijaṃ rūpaṃ prapede ca divaṃ yayau ..
3.1.d: तत्र स्नात्वा निजं रूपं प्रपेदे च दिवं ययौ ..
3.1.m: bathed there, regained her own form, and went to heaven.

3.1.s: asya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ mayā vaktuṃ na śakyate .. 22 ..
3.1.d: अस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं मया वक्तुं न शक्यते .. 22 ..
3.1.m: The greatness of this sacred ford cannot be fully told by me. // 22
The sages said:
Why did Kauśika curse Rambhā, O son of Sūta?
How did the celestial damsel, turned into stone, go to Kapitīrtha?
Explain all of this to us in full detail, O best of sages! // 23
The auspicious Sūta said:
Long ago, in the lineage of Kuśika, there was a king named Viśvāmitra. // 24
Once that mighty monarch, surrounded by his army,
traversed the earth, eager to inspect his kingdom. // 25
Having wandered through many lands, he went to the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha.
He was invited to receive hospitality by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha. // 26
"So be it," said the king, bowing prostrate like a staff.
By the power of the wish-fulfilling cow, to King Viśvāmitra // 27
Vasiṣṭha, son of Brahmā, offered hospitality, O brahmins.
Having realized the power of the wish-fulfilling cow, the descendant of Kuśika // 28
begged Vasiṣṭha for the wish-fulfilling cow that grants all desires.

3.1.s: pratyākhyāto vasiṣṭhena pracakarṣa ca tāṃ balāt .. 29 ..
3.1.d: प्रत्याख्यातो वसिष्ठेन प्रचकर्ष च तां बलात् .. 29 ..
3.1.m: Refused by Vasiṣṭha, he dragged her away by force. // 29
Defeated by Mlecchas and others brought forth by the wish-fulfilling cow,
he propitiated Mahādeva and obtained divine weapons from him. // 30
Having gone to Vasiṣṭha's hermitage, he unleashed showers of arrows;
the best of kings discharged all the divine weapons, including the Brahmā-weapon. // 31
All those weapons, Vasiṣṭha, son of Brahmā,
struck down with a single staff of Brahmā, by the power of his own austerity. // 32
Then, being defeated, O brahmins, Viśvāmitra was greatly ashamed;

3.1.s: brāhmaṇyāvāptaye svasya tapaḥ kartuṃ vanaṃ yayau .. 33 ..
3.1.d: ब्राह्मण्यावाप्तये स्वस्य तपः कर्तुं वनं ययौ .. 33 ..
3.1.m: to attain brahminhood for himself, he went to the forest to perform austerity. // 33
He performed austerity in three directions, ending in the east and the west;
in each of those directions, great obstacles arose for that Kauśika. // 34

3.1.s:
uttarāṃ diśamāsādya himavatparvate'male
kauśikyāssaritastīre puṇye pāpavināśini .. 35 ..
3.1.d:
उत्तरां दिशमासाद्य हिमवत्पर्वतेऽमले
कौशिक्यास्सरितस्तीरे पुण्ये पापविनाशिनि .. 35 ..
3.1.m: Reaching the northern direction on the pure Himavat mountain, / on the sacred, sin-destroying bank of the river Kauśikī, // 35
For a divine thousand years, without food, his senses mastered,
without looking about, his breath controlled, his anger overcome, completely motionless,
standing in the midst of five fires in summer, staying in the water during the cold season,
standing in the open air during the rains, his arms raised always, without any support,
he performed very severe, great tapas to attain the status of a brahmin.
Their minds agitated [because of] him, the thirty [gods] dwelling in heaven,

3.1.s: jaṃbhāriṇā ca sahitā raṃbhāṃ procuridaṃ vacaḥ .. 39 ..
3.1.d: जंभारिणा च सहिता रंभां प्रोचुरिदं वचः .. 39 ..
3.1.m: along with the foe of Jambha, addressed this speech to Rambhā:
The gods said:
“O Rambhā, to the sage on the mountain Himavat, on the bank of the Kauśikī,
to Viśvāmitra practicing tapas, entice him with your gestures;

3.1.s: yathā tattapaso vighno bhaviṣyati tathā kuru .. 3.1.39.40 ..
3.1.d: यथा तत्तपसो विघ्नो भविष्यति तथा कुरु .. 3.1.39.40 ..
3.1.m: act in such a way that there will be an obstacle to his tapas.”
Thus addressed then by the gods headed by Indra,
Rambhā then replied to all the gods with folded hands, bowing down.
Rambhā said:
“The great sage Viśvāmitra is extremely fierce and greatly wrathful;

3.1.s: sa śapsyate māṃ krodhena bibhemyasmādahaṃ surāḥ .. 42 ..
3.1.d: स शप्स्यते मां क्रोधेन बिभेम्यस्मादहं सुराः .. 42 ..
3.1.m: he will curse me in anger. O gods, I am afraid of him.
Out of compassion protect me, your servant!”
Thus addressed there by Rambhā, the foe of Jambha spoke to her:
Indra said:

3.1.s: raṃbhe tvayā na bhīḥ kāryā viśvāmitrāttapodhanāt ..
3.1.d: रंभे त्वया न भीः कार्या विश्वामित्रात्तपोधनात् ..
3.1.m: “O Rambhā, you should have no fear of Viśvāmitra, whose wealth is tapas.
I too will come as your ally, accompanied by Manmatha.
Spring, sweet with the calls of the cuckoo, will also arrive.
You of exceedingly beautiful form, entice the great sage!”
Thus told by Indra, Rambhā went to Viśvāmitra's hermitage.
Standing within range of his sight, having assumed a charming form,
she enticed the sage with captivating gestures,
and at that moment a cuckoo also cooed, delighting the mind.

3.1.s: śrutvā pikasvaraṃ raṃbhāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca munipuṃgavaḥ ..
3.1.d: श्रुत्वा पिकस्वरं रंभां दृष्ट्वा च मुनिपुंगवः ..
3.1.m: Hearing the voice of the cuckoo and seeing Rambhā, the eminent sage,
his heart seized with doubt, understood that it was the deed of Śakra.
Viśvāmitra, whose wealth is tapas, cursed Rambhā in anger.
Viśvāmitra said:
“Because you provoke anger in me, O Rambhā, who wish to conquer anger,
therefore, O Rambhā, become a stone here for ten thousand years.
At the end of that [time], protected by a brahmin, you will attain release.”
By the curse of Viśvāmitra, she instantly became a stone.
Turned into a stone, O twice-born, she remained in his hermitage for a long time.
Viśvāmitra too, of righteous soul, having performed great tapas once again,
obtained, by the word of Vasiṣṭha, the brahminhood difficult for kings to attain.
Turned into a stone, Rambhā also remained for a long time in that hermitage.
In that very holy hermitage, the esteemed disciple of Agastya,
a sage named Śveta, seeking liberation, performed supreme tapas.
As that great sage was performing tapas for a long time,
a certain rākṣasī known as Aṅgārakā arrived
at his hermitage, exceedingly cruel, roaring with a sound like clouds.
The terrifying creature polluted [the hermitage] with urine, blood, feces, and the like,
and afflicted that sage with other disturbances as well.

3.1.s: atha kruddho muniḥ śveto vāyavyāstreṇa yojayan ..
3.1.d: अथ क्रुद्धो मुनिः श्वेतो वायव्यास्त्रेण योजयन् ..
3.1.m: Then the enraged sage Śveta, employing the wind-weapon,
hurled at the rākṣasī the stone cursed by the son of Kuśika.
Assailed by the wind-weapon, that rākṣasī fled away;
and pursued by the rock propelled by the wind-weapon,
she ran afflicted with fear to the shore of the southern ocean.
Pursuing her as she ran, that stone hurled by the weapon
fell upon the rākṣasī as she was plunging into Kapitīrtha.
The rākṣasī died there from the impact of the stone on her head.
She who had been cursed by Viśvāmitra, through plunging into Kapitīrtha,
cast off the form of a stone and returned to the form of Rambhā.
Showered with torrents of flowers by the gods, the charming woman,
mounting a celestial vimāna, resplendent in celestial garments,
adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and nose-ornaments,
was surrounded by her friends, apsarases headed by Urvaśī.
Praising the māhātmya of Kapitīrtha again and again,
and having worshipped Rāmanātha, Śaṃkara, who is adorned with the moon,
she went to Amarāvatī, the delightful city of Indra.
That rākṣasī too, through the curse of the mighty Agastya, born of a jar,
—for Ghṛtācī, the courtesan of the gods, had assumed the form of a rākṣasī—
she too, by bathing here in the waters of Kapitīrtha, regained her own form.
Thus Rambhā and Ghṛtācī, by plunging into Kapitīrtha,
through the grace of Śveta, the disciple of Agastya, O best of brahmins,

3.1.s: rākṣasītvaṃ śilātvaṃ ca hitvā svaṃ rūpamāgate ..
3.1.d: राक्षसीत्वं शिलात्वं च हित्वा स्वं रूपमागते ..
3.1.m: abandoned their states of being a rākṣasī and a rock, and attained their own form.
Therefore, one should bathe in Kapitīrtha with every effort.
Whatever person hears or reads this chapter,
obtains the excellent fruit born of bathing in Kapitīrtha.

3.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe setumāhātmye kapitīrthapraśaṃsāyāṃ raṃbhāghṛtācīśāpavimokṣaṇavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..39..
3.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतुमाहात्म्ये कपितीर्थप्रशंसायां रंभाघृताचीशापविमोक्षणवर्णनं नामैकोनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ..39..
3.1.m: Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled 'The Description of the Release of Rambhā and Ghṛtācī from the Curse' in the praise of Kapitīrtha, in the Setumāhātmya, in the third Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of Skanda consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

3.1.s: 3.1.39.55 aṃgāraketi vikhyātā rākṣasī kācidāgatā . tasyāśramamatikrūrā meghasvanamahāsvanā .. 55 ..
3.1.d: 3.1.39.55 अंगारकेति विख्याता राक्षसी काचिदागता . तस्याश्रममतिक्रूरा मेघस्वनमहास्वना .. 55 ..
3.1.m: 3.1.39.55 A certain rākṣasī known as Aṅgārakā came to his hermitage, extremely cruel, with a mighty roar like the rumble of clouds. 55.
Note on Aṅgārakā.
Śrī Sūta said:
Now, therefore, O sages, I will proclaim that which purifies the world,

3.1.s: gāyatryā ca sarasvatyā māhātmyaṃ muktidaṃ nṛṇām .. 1 ..
3.1.d: गायत्र्या च सरस्वत्या माहात्म्यं मुक्तिदं नृणाम् .. 1 ..
3.1.m: the māhātmya of Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī, which grants liberation to mortals;
which destroys great sins for those who hear and recite it,
bestowing great merit upon men and destroying the torments of hell.

3.1.s: gāyatryāṃ ca sarasvatyāṃ ye snāṃti manujā mudā ..
3.1.d: गायत्र्यां च सरस्वत्यां ये स्नांति मनुजा मुदा ..
3.1.m: Those men who gladly bathe in Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī

3.1.s: na teṣāṃ garbhavāsaḥ syātkiṃ tu muktirbhaveddhruvam .. 3 ..
3.1.d: न तेषां गर्भवासः स्यात्किं तु मुक्तिर्भवेद्ध्रुवम् .. 3 ..
3.1.m: shall have no dwelling in a womb, but shall surely attain liberation.
On Mount Gandhamādana, of Sarasvatī and Gāyatrī,
because of the presence of the two wives of Brahmā, these two [tīrthas] are named after them.
The seers said:
On Mount Gandhamādana, of Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī,
for what reason did their presence come to be, O Sūta? Tell us that.
Sūta said:

3.1.s: prajāpatiḥ purā viprāḥ svāṃ vai duhitaraṃ mudā ..
3.1.d: प्रजापतिः पुरा विप्राः स्वां वै दुहितरं मुदा ..
3.1.m: Formerly, O brahmins, Prajāpati gladly lusted after his own daughter
named Vāc; having become filled with desire, infatuated, he longed for her.

3.1.s: atha prajāpateḥ putrī svasminvai tasya kāmitām..
3.1.d: अथ प्रजापतेः पुत्री स्वस्मिन्वै तस्य कामिताम्..
3.1.m: Then, perceiving his desire towards herself,

3.1.s: vilokya lajjitā bhūtvā rohidrūpa dadhāra sā .. 7 ..
3.1.d: विलोक्य लज्जिता भूत्वा रोहिद्रूप दधार सा .. 7 ..
3.1.m: the daughter of Prajāpati felt ashamed and assumed the form of a doe.
Brahmā also became a buck, wishing then to sport with her;
he pursued her as she fled, bearing the form of a female deer.
Seeing him intent upon cohabiting with his daughter, all the deities [cried]:
"This Brahmā is doing a forbidden deed in the form of incest with his daughter!"

3.1.s: iti nindaṃti taṃ viprāḥ sraṣṭāraṃ jagatāṃ patim ..
3.1.d: इति निन्दंति तं विप्राः स्रष्टारं जगतां पतिम् ..
3.1.m: Thus the brahmins censured that creator, the lord of the worlds.
Seeing Parameṣṭhin devoted to a forbidden act,
the lord Hara took his Pināka and assumed the form of a hunter.
With the Pināka bow drawn fully to his ear,

3.1.s: saṃyojya vedhasaṃ tena vivyādha niśitena saḥ ..
3.1.d: संयोज्य वेधसं तेन विव्याध निशितेन सः ..
3.1.m: having fitted a sharp arrow, he pierced the Creator with it.
Pierced by the arrow of the destroyer of Tripura, he fell to the earth.
Then, rising from his body, a great light of immense splendour
became the constellation named Mṛgaśīrṣa in the sky at that time.
Taking the form of the constellation Ārdrā, Hara too pursued it,
harassing the constellation named Mṛgaśīrṣa that had the form of Brahmā.
Even today, in the form of a deer-hunter, the destroyer of Tripura
is clearly seen in the sky near Mṛgaśīrṣa, O brahmins.
When that Parameṣṭhin was thus slain by Śambhu,
thereupon Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī were stricken with grief.
Bereft of their husband, O best of sages, longing for the revival of their husband,
they consulted each other: "What shall the two of us do?"
For the sake of bringing about the life of their husband, Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī,
intent on performing austerity on Mount Gandhamādana,
the most supreme abode of Śiva which bestows all desires upon men,
went [there] bound by vows to perform austerity dedicated to Śiva.
For the purpose of their own ritual ablution, O brahmins, Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī
made two sacred fords under their own names, destroying sin.
Joyfully they performed ritual ablutions at the three junctures of the day there daily;
for a long time they were without food, free from desire, anger, and the like.
engaged in exceedingly severe observances, wholly devoted to meditating on Śiva,
singularly committed to chanting the great five-syllable mantra, auspicious,
for the sake of reviving their husband, indeed, Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī
thus performed austerity directed towards Mahādeva.
Then Mahādeva, Maheśvara, pleased by their austerity,
manifested His great form, desiring to grant the fruit of austerities.
Then, seeing Śambhu, Śiva, the delight of Pārvatī, who had appeared,
attended on both sides by Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya,

3.1.s: dṛṣṭvā saṃtuṣṭacitte te gāyatrī ca sarasvatī ..
3.1.d: दृष्ट्वा संतुष्टचित्ते ते गायत्री च सरस्वती ..
3.1.m: their minds filled with joy, both Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī
praised Mahādeva, the treasure of compassion, who is worthy of praise, with hymns.
Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī said:
"Obeisance to the sole cause of the destruction of the darkness of irresistible saṃsāra, / to the consumer of the kālakūṭa poison, terrible with blazing rows of flames!
To the devourer of the Kālakūṭa poison, dreadful with a mass of blazing flames;
To the sole cause of the destruction of the body of the five-arrowed god who enchants the world, / to the slayer of cruel Yama who brings an end to the universe, obeisance to you!
to the destroyer of the universe, the slayer of the fierce Yama, praise be to You!
To the one who bears a mass of matted hair touched by the waves of the Gaṅgā, / obeisance to you, O Virūpākṣa, bearer of the young, cool-rayed moon!
Praise be to You, O Virūpākṣa, wearer of the young crescent moon!
To the one who terrified the dwellers of Tripura with the terrible twang of the Pināka bow, / obeisance to you who cut off the head of the creator of the manifold universe!
Praise be to You, the severer of the head of the Creator of the manifold universe!
O you who protected the son of Mṛkaṇḍu by your calm and immaculate glance of compassion! / O lord of the mountain's daughter, obeisance to you! Protect us who have taken refuge!
Praise be to You, O Lord of the Mountain-born; protect us two who have sought refuge!
O Mahādeva, lord of the world, destroyer of Tripura, Śaṃkara, / O Vāmadeva, Mahādeva, protect us who have taken refuge!"
O Vāmadeva, O Mahādeva, protect us two who have sought refuge!
Praised in this way by the two, Śambhu, the God of gods, Maheśvara,
filled with affection, spoke to Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī.
Mahādeva said:
"O Sarasvatī, O Gāyatrī, I am pleased with you two. / Choose a boon from me, whatever is in your mind."

3.1.s: varaṃ varayataṃ matto yadvā manasi vartate .. 34 ..
3.1.d: वरं वरयतं मत्तो यद्वा मनसि वर्तते .. 34 ..
3.1.m: Choose a boon from me, whatever is in your mind.

3.1.s: ityukte te tu gāyatrīsarasvatyau hareṇa vai ..
3.1.d: इत्युक्ते ते तु गायत्रीसरस्वत्यौ हरेण वै ..
3.1.m: When this was said by Hara, Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī
spoke to Pārvatī's beloved, Mahādeva, the treasure of compassion.
Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī said:
"O Lord, O God, make our husband, the four-faced one,
alive with breath, O Lord of all, out of mercy, O maker of compassion!

3.1.s: tvamāvayoḥ pitā deva tavāpyāvāṃ sute ubhe ..
3.1.d: त्वमावयोः पिता देव तवाप्यावां सुते उभे ..
3.1.m: You are our father, O God, and we are both your daughters; / therefore, protect us by the gift of our husband, O destroyer of Tripura!"
Therefore, O Destroyer of Tripura, protect us two by the grant of our husband!
When Śambhu was thus petitioned by them, O best of brahmins,
saying, 'So be it,' to Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī,
eager to join that body of the Creator with the head,
right there, O men of good vows, the body of the Creator together with the heads,
he caused to be brought by the spirits led by Nandin and Bhṛṅgin.
Those various heads Śaṃkara, together with the body,
rejoined in a moment before Sarasvatī and Gāyatrī.
Reassembled then by Hara, this four-faced Lord of the universe
stood up that very instant, as if awoken from sleep, O twice-born.
Then Prajāpati, seeing Śaṃkara adorned with the moon,
praised [him] with choice words, accompanied by his two wives.
Brahmā said:
"Obeisance to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, O maker of compassion, Śaṃkara! / Protect me, O ocean of compassion, O Master, from prohibited conduct!
Protect me, O Ocean of Compassion, from forbidden conduct, O Lord!
May no inclination ever arise again in me toward prohibited conduct / through your grace, O Śambhu; protect me always in that manner!"

3.1.s: mā pravṛttirbhavedbhūyo rakṣa māṃ tvaṃ tathā sadā ..
3.1.d: मा प्रवृत्तिर्भवेद्भूयो रक्ष मां त्वं तथा सदा ..
3.1.m: May there not be an inclination again; protect me thus always!
"So be it indeed," the husband of the mountain's daughter said to Brahmā.

3.1.s: itaḥ paraṃ pramādaṃ tvaṃ mā kuruṣva vidhe punaḥ ..
3.1.d: इतः परं प्रमादं त्वं मा कुरुष्व विधे पुनः ..
3.1.m: "Henceforth, do not make an error again, O Creator. / I am always the punisher of men who have taken to the wrong path."
I am always the punisher of men who have taken to the wrong path.
Having spoken thus to the four-faced one, O best of the twice-born, Mahādeva
spoke to Sarasvatī and Gāyatrī, pleasing them with his speech.
Mahādeva said:
"Through my grace to you both, O Gāyatrī, O Sarasvatī, / this husband of yours, the four-faced one, has returned, alive with breath.
Here has your husband arrived alive, the Four-faced One!
Go with him to the world of Brahmā; let there be no delay."
"By the presence of you both constantly here in this pair of pools,
liberation in the form of union with God will surely accrue to men from bathing [here].
And named after both of you, this pair, called Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī,

3.1.s: idaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvaloke khyātiṃ yāsyati śāśvatīm ..
3.1.d: इदं तीर्थं सर्वलोके ख्यातिं यास्यति शाश्वतीम् ..
3.1.m: this sacred ford will attain eternal renown throughout all the worlds.
Even among all sacred fords, may this pair of sacred fords always
grant purification and destroy major sins!
May it bring great peace to men and bestow all desires!
It will engender my grace and cause delight to Viṣṇu.
Equal to this pair of sacred fords none has existed, nor will ever exist.
For by bathing here, all men will attain their every wish.

3.1.s: idaṃ kuṃḍadvayaṃ loke bhavatībhyāṃ kṛtaṃ mahat .. 54 ..
3.1.d: इदं कुंडद्वयं लोके भवतीभ्यां कृतं महत् .. 54 ..
3.1.m: This great pair of pools created in the world by the two of you
shall become renowned by your names and grant liberation.
Those who are devoid of worship of Gāyatrī, abandoned by the study of the Vedas,
lacking the domestic fire-sacrifice, and neglected of the five great sacrifices,
shall obtain their respective fruits merely by bathing in your pair of pools.
And whatever other sinners there are who neglect their daily duties,
having bathed in that pair of pools, O best of brahmins, they will become purified."
Having spoken thus to Sarasvatī and Gāyatrī, the Great Lord
vanished there in an instant, even as everyone watched.
Then, having regained their husband, Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī, filled with joy,
went along with him to Brahmaloka, O best of brahmins.
The venerable Sūta said:
"Thus has been recounted to you, O brahmins, on Mount Gandhamādana,
the manifestation of Sarasvatī and Gāyatrī, along with its cause.
Whoever hears this chapter or recites it with devotion,
undoubtedly obtains the fruit of bathing in this pair of sacred fords."

3.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhi tāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe setumāhātmye gāyatrīsarasvatītīrthapraśaṃsāyāṃ gaṃdhamādane gāyatrīsarasvatīsannidhānakathanaṃ nāma catvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 40 .. ..
