3.1.m: Thus ends the fortieth chapter, entitled 'The Account of the Manifestation of Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī on Gandhamādana,' in the Praise of the Sacred Fords of Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī, in the Setumāhātmya of the third section, the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
The venerable Sūta said:
"Now, therefore, I shall fully relate, concerning Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī,
a holy tale, O best of brahmins.
Formerly, a brahmin named Kaśyapa, in this auspicious pair of sacred fords,
having bathed, was released from a very great sin that would have consigned him to hell."
The seers said:
"O sage, what sin did this one named Kaśyapa commit,
from which he became liberated in an instant after bathing in this pair of sacred fords?
Tell this to us who are faithful, O Sūta, out of the power of your compassion;
to us who are satiated by the nectar of your speech, there is not even thirst."
The venerable Sūta said:
"I shall relate an ancient narrative establishing the māhātmya
of Gāyatrī and Sarasvatī, which destroys sin for those who hear it.
The son of Abhimanyu, a king by the name of Parīkṣit,
dwelt in Hāstinapura, protecting the earth according to righteousness.

3.1.s: sa rājā jātu vipine cacāra mṛgayā rataḥ ..
3.1.d: स राजा जातु विपिने चचार मृगया रतः ..
3.1.m: Once, that king, intent on hunting, roamed in the forest.
Sixty years of age, the king was afflicted by hunger and thirst.
Eagerly tracking a single deer that had been lost in the forest,

3.1.s: dhyānārūḍhaṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha taṃ cīravāsasam .. 8 ...
3.1.d: ध्यानारूढं मुनिं दृष्ट्वा प्राह तं चीरवाससम् .. 8 ...
3.1.m: he saw a sage immersed in meditation, clad in bark garments, and said to him:

3.1.s: mayā bāṇena vipine mṛgo viddho'dhunā mune ..
3.1.d: मया बाणेन विपिने मृगो विद्धोऽधुना मुने ..
3.1.m: 'O sage, a deer was just struck by me with an arrow in the forest;

3.1.s: dṛṣṭaḥ sa kiṃ tvayā vidvanvidruto bhayakātaraḥ .. 9 ..
3.1.d: दृष्टः स किं त्वया विद्वन्विद्रुतो भयकातरः .. 9 ..
3.1.m: was it seen by you, O wise one, fleeing in distress and fear?'
Established in absorption, [the sage] did not say anything at all because of his vow of silence.
Then, having placed a dead serpent on the shoulder of that great sage

3.1.s: nidhāya mṛtasarpaṃ tu kupitaḥ svapuraṃ yayau..
3.1.d: निधाय मृतसर्पं तु कुपितः स्वपुरं ययौ..
3.1.m: with the tip of his bow, [the king], enraged, went to his own city.
That sage had a son named Śṛṅgin.
That Śṛṅgin had a friend named Kṛśa, O best of brahmins.

3.1.s: sakhāyaṃ śṛṅgiṇaṃ prāha kṛśākhyaḥ sa sakhā tataḥ .. 12 ..
3.1.d: सखायं शृङ्गिणं प्राह कृशाख्यः स सखा ततः .. 12 ..
3.1.m: Then that friend named Kṛśa said to his friend Śṛṅgin:

3.1.s: pitā tava mṛtaṃ sarpaṃ skaṃdhena vahate'dhunā ..
3.1.d: पिता तव मृतं सर्पं स्कंधेन वहतेऽधुना ..
3.1.m: 'Your father now carries a dead snake on his shoulder!

3.1.s: mā bhūddarpastava sakhe mā kṛthāstvaṃ madaṃ vṛthā .. 13 ..
3.1.d: मा भूद्दर्पस्तव सखे मा कृथास्त्वं मदं वृथा .. 13 ..
3.1.m: Let there be no pride in you, friend; do not indulge in vain arrogance.'
Enraged and eager to pronounce a curse upon the king, Śṛṅgin said:
'That foolish-minded one who placed a snake's corpse on my father—
may he die within seven nights, bitten by the serpent Takṣaka!'
Thus the sage's son cursed Parīkṣit, the son of Subhadrā's son."

3.1.s: śamīkākhyaḥ pitā tasya śrutvā śaptaṃ sutena tam ..
3.1.d: शमीकाख्यः पिता तस्य श्रुत्वा शप्तं सुतेन तम् ..
3.1.m: Hearing that the king had been cursed by his son, his father, named Śamīka,
that foremost of sages spoke to his son Śṛṅgin:
"Why did you curse the king, the protector of all the worlds?
In a kingless world, how shall we truly survive?
Through anger sin has arisen; you will obtain no happiness.
He who dispels aroused anger solely through forbearance
flourishes with supreme happiness in this world and in the next.

3.1.s: kṣamāyuktā hi puruṣā labhaṃte śreya uttamam .. 19 ..
3.1.d: क्षमायुक्ता हि पुरुषा लभंते श्रेय उत्तमम् .. 19 ..
3.1.m: For people endowed with forbearance attain the highest good."

3.1.s: tataḥ śamīkaḥ svaṃ śiṣyaṃ prāha gauramukhābhidham ..
3.1.d: ततः शमीकः स्वं शिष्यं प्राह गौरमुखाभिधम् ..
3.1.m: Then Śamīka spoke to his disciple named Gauramukha:

3.1.s: bho gau mukha gatvā tvaṃ vada bhūpaṃ parīkṣitam .. 3.1.41.20 ..
3.1.d: भो गौ मुख गत्वा त्वं वद भूपं परीक्षितम् .. 3.1.41.20 ..
3.1.m: "O Gauramukha, go and tell King Parīkṣit
of this curse uttered by my son, of being bitten by the serpent Takṣaka.
Then come back swiftly into my presence, O wise one."
Thus addressed by Śamīka, Gauramukha went to the king,
and approaching, he spoke to King Parīkṣit, the son of Subhadrā's son:

3.1.s: dṛṣṭvā sarpaṃ pituḥ skandhe tvayā vinihitaṃ mṛtam ..
3.1.d: दृष्ट्वा सर्पं पितुः स्कन्धे त्वया विनिहितं मृतम् ..
3.1.m: "Seeing the dead snake placed by you upon his father's shoulder,

3.1.s: śamīkasya sutaḥ śṛṃgī śaśāpa tvāṃ ruṣānvitaḥ .. 23 ..
3.1.d: शमीकस्य सुतः शृंगी शशाप त्वां रुषान्वितः .. 23 ..
3.1.m: Śamīka's son Śṛṅgin, filled with fury, cursed you:
'On the seventh day from this day, by the great serpent Takṣaka
may the son of Abhimanyu be bitten and burnt swiftly by poison-fire!'

3.1.s: evaṃ śaśāpa tvāṃ rājañchṛṃgī tasya muneḥ sutaḥ ..
3.1.d: एवं शशाप त्वां राजञ्छृंगी तस्य मुनेः सुतः ..
3.1.m: Thus did Śṛṅgin, that sage's son, curse you, O king.
His father sent me into your presence to tell you this."
Having spoken thus to the king, Gauramukha departed swiftly.
After Gauramukha had gone, the king, overcome with grief,
erected a high pavilion touching the clouds, upon a single pillar, very spacious,
in the midst of the Gaṅgā, that foremost of kings,
with physicians who knew herbs and experts in the great Gāruḍa mantras,
making an effort with concentrated mind to avert the poison of Takṣaka.
Accompanied by many eminent celestial seers, divine seers, and royal seers,
the king, devoted to Viṣṇu, stayed in that lofty pavilion.
At that time, a brahmin named Kāśyapa, the best of mantra-masters,
set out on the seventh day to protect the king from the deadly poison of Takṣaka,
that foremost of brahmins, poor and desirous of wealth.
Meanwhile Takṣaka too arrived, disguised as a brahmin.
Then, seeing Kāśyapa on the way, he spoke to him:

3.1.s: brāhmaṇa tvaṃ kutra yāsi vada me'dya mahāmune .. 32 ..
3.1.d: ब्राह्मण त्वं कुत्र यासि वद मेऽद्य महामुने .. 32 ..
3.1.m: "O brahmin, where are you going today? Tell me, O great sage."
When asked thus, Kāśyapa then said to Takṣaka, O brahmins:
"Today Takṣaka will burn the great king Parīkṣit
with the fire of his poison; I am going into his presence to neutralize it."
To that brahmin who had spoken thus, Takṣaka spoke again:
"I am Takṣaka, O best of brahmins! One bitten by me cannot be cured
even in a hundred years, even with ten thousand potent mantras.
If you now have the power to heal one bitten by me,
then I shall bite this banyan tree,
many yojanas high; you revive it, and then you are indeed capable."
Having spoken thus, Takṣaka then bit that tree.
It was completely reduced to ashes, utterly stunned.
Earlier, a man had climbed that tree;
he too was burnt then by the flames of Takṣaka's poison.

3.1.s: taṃ naraṃ na vijijñāte tau ca kāśyapatakṣakau .. .. 39 ..
3.1.d: तं नरं न विजिज्ञाते तौ च काश्यपतक्षकौ .. .. 39 ..
3.1.m: Neither Kāśyapa nor Takṣaka noticed that man.
Then Kāśyapa vowed, while Takṣaka also listened:

3.1.s: tanmaṃtraśaktiṃ paśyaṃtu sarve viprā hi no'dhunā .. 3.1.41.40 ..
3.1.d: तन्मंत्रशक्तिं पश्यंतु सर्वे विप्रा हि नोऽधुना .. 3.1.41.40 ..
3.1.m: "Let all our brahmins now see the power of my mantra!"
Having spoken thus, Kāśyapa, the foremost of mantra-masters,
revived by the power of his mantra that tree that had been reduced to ashes by the poison-fire.
The man was also brought back to life along with that tree.
Then Takṣaka said to Kāśyapa, who was skilled in mantras:

3.1.s: yathā na munivāṅmithyā bhavedevaṃ kuru dvija ..
3.1.d: यथा न मुनिवाङ्मिथ्या भवेदेवं कुरु द्विज ..
3.1.m: "O brahmin, act in such a way that the sage's word may not prove false!

3.1.s: yatte rājā dhanaṃ dadyāttatopi dviguṇaṃ dhanam .. .. 43 ..
3.1.d: यत्ते राजा धनं दद्यात्ततोपि द्विगुणं धनम् .. .. 43 ..
3.1.m: Whatever wealth the king would give you, double that wealth
I will give. Turn back right now, O best of brahmins!"
Having said this and given him priceless jewels, Takṣaka

3.1.m: Having bathed here with devotion, a man attains the world of the sun.
By bathing in Sugrīvatīrtha, the fruit of a horse-sacrifice is obtained, (34)
and expiation of sins such as the killing of a brahmin also takes place.
From going to Sugrīvatīrtha, one obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows; (35)
from remembering it, one obtains the fruit of reciting the Vedas completely.
Merely by fasting for a day on the bank of that sacred ford, (36)
there is destruction of great sins without any penance, O brahmins.
Performing a ceremonial bath there, one should satisfy the ancestors and the gods; (37)
the fruit of the āptoryāma sacrifice becomes eightfold.
By bathing in Sugrīvatīrtha, one obtains the fruit of a human sacrifice. (38)
By bathing in Sugrīvatīrtha, a man remembers his previous births.
O brahmins, go to Sugrīvatīrtha for the attainment of your desires! (39)
Thus the māhātmya of Sugrīvatīrtha has been told to you, O brahmins.
Now I declare to you the glory of Nalatīrtha. (40)
From bathing in Nalatīrtha, a man attains the heavenly realm;
from bathing once in Nalatīrtha, freed from all sin, (41)
he obtains the peerless fruit of [rites] beginning with agniṣṭoma and atirātra.
Having stayed three nights there, satisfying the ancestors and deities, (42)
he shines like the sun, O brahmins, and obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.
I shall declare Nīlatīrtha, which destroys great sins, (43)
made on the causeway by Nīla, the son of Agni, granting liberation.
From bathing in Nīlatīrtha, a man, freed from all sin, (44)
obtains a hundredfold the fruit of a sacrifice with many gifts.
Having bathed in Nīlatīrtha, which bestows all desired things, (45)
a man attains the realm of Agni, enriched with all desires.

Devotion to the great liṅga Rāmeśvara is declared to be of eight kinds:

likewise the thrill of emotion in voice, eyes, and body,
and continuous remembrance of the great liṅga Rāmeśvara,
and living purely by taking refuge in the great liṅga Rāmeśvara.

The seers said:
O knower of the truth of the meaning of all the Vedas! O crosser of the ocean of the Purāṇas!
O one whose inauspiciousness was dispelled by bowing to the pair of lotus feet of Vyāsa!
O benefactor of all living beings through instruction in the meaning of the Purāṇas!
We have indeed been graced by you through the recitation of the Purāṇas.
Now, especially through the recitation of the Setumāhātmya, O sage,
we have attained our purpose, O disciple of Vyāsa, O great-minded one!
How Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, established the liṅga—
we desire to hear that; tell it to us now.
The venerable Sūta said:
The purpose for which the liṅga was installed on Mount Gandhamādana
by Rāmacandra, O best of brahmins, that I shall now tell you.
His wife having been taken from the forest by the mighty Rāvaṇa,
Rāma, resolute and exceedingly powerful, accompanied by an army of monkeys and by Saumitri,
reached Mount Mahendra and looked upon the ocean.
Having built a bridge across that shoreless ocean, the scion of Raghu,

you will see them, or to whomever you shall give this,

Placing Agastya at their head, they praised the husband of the princess of Mithilā.
The sages said:
Homage to you, Rāmacandra, who bestow grace upon the worlds,
who descended to the earth to rid the world of Rāvaṇa!
To the destroyer of Tāṭakā's body, the protector of the sacrifice of Gādhi's son,
homage to you who conquered Mārīca and took the life of Subāhu!
To the dust of whose lotus feet grants liberation to Ahalyā,
homage to you who playfully broke the bow of Hara!
Homage to you who were adorned with the festive marriage to the princess of Mithilā!
Homage to you who brought about the defeat of the son of Reṇukā!

3.1.m: homage to you who went to the forest to make true the word of your father!

Homage to the destroyer of Virādha, to you the friend of the king of vultures,
who tore apart the limbs of the very cruel Mārīca in the form of an illusory deer!
Who cast off his body in battle against the lord of the world who abducted Sītā—
having cremated Jaṭāyus, [homage to you] who bestowed isolation upon him!
Homage to the destroyer of Kabandha, whose feet were worshiped by Śabarī,
to you who attained the friendship of Sugrīva and brought about the slaying of Vālin!
Homage to you who built the bridge across the ocean, the abode of Varuṇa,
the destroyer of all rākṣasas, the taker of Rāvaṇa's life!
To you whose lotus feet are the boat for crossing over the ocean of worldly existence,
homage to the remover of the distress of devotees, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss!
Homage to you, Rāmabhadra, the cause of the prosperity of the worlds,
who take away the sins of those who chant your holy names such as Rāma!
Homage to you who bring about the creation, maintenance, and destruction of all the worlds!
Homage to you, the embodiment of compassion, consecrated to protecting devotees!
Homage to you who are with Sītā, who bestow happiness upon Vibhīṣaṇa;
for by the slaying of the lord of Laṅkā, O Rāma, the world has indeed been protected by you!
Protect, protect, O Lord of the Universe! Protect us, O lord of Jānakī!

3.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतुमाहात्म्ये रामनाथलिंगप्रतिष्ठाविधिवर्णनंनाम चतुश्चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः .. 44 ..
3.1.m: Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter, entitled “Description of the Rite of Consecration of the Rāmanāthaliṅga” in the Setumāhātmya of the third [section], the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses]. (44)

3.1.m: Śrī Sūta said: / When the liṅga had thus been consecrated by Rāma of untiring deeds, / Māruti quickly arrived, bringing an excellent liṅga. (1) / Having bowed to heroic Rāma, son of Daśaratha, that Māruti / then bowed to Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa, and saluted Sugrīva. (2) / Then, seeing the scion of Raghu worshipping that sandy liṅga / together with the sages, the son of the wind became furious. (3) / Extremely distressed with sorrow, his toil rendered vain, / Hanūmān, son of Añjanā, spoke to righteous Rāma: (4) / Hanūmān said: / “Ill-born was I, O Rāma, in vain, solely for affliction in the world! / I have often been tormented, O Lord, by the demons of cruel deeds. (5) / May no woman ever bear a son like me, / through whom endless sorrow is experienced in the ocean of worldly existence! (6) / I was tormented earlier by service, and even more so by battle; / now there is endless sorrow because you disregard me! (7) / By Sugrīva for the sake of a wife, and by the demon, / the younger brother of Rāvaṇa, for a kingdom, you were served, O scion of Raghu. (8) / By me you have been served without motive, O Rāma, O broad-minded one! / Among the many monkeys, I was indeed commanded by you today (9) / to bring a Śivaliṅga from Kailāsa, the supreme mountain. / Having gone swiftly to Kailāsa, I did not see the wielder of the Pināka. (10) / Having pleased him, the one accompanied by Ambā, whose mount is the bull, through tapas, / and having obtained the liṅga, O lord of the Raghus, I quickly returned. (11) / But now, having consecrated another liṅga made of sand, / you are worshipping it, O lord, along with the sages, gods, and gandharvas! (12) / In vain was this liṅga brought by me from Mount Kailāsa! / Ah, my body has become a burden to this earth, / O unfortunate as I am, O great king, O delight of Jānakī, O sovereign! / I am unable to endure this grief, O scion of Raghu! (14)”

3.1.d:
किं करिष्यामि कुत्राहं गमिष्यामि न मे गतिः ..
अतः शरीरं त्यक्ष्यामि त्वयाहमवमानितः .. 15 ..
.. श्रीसूत उवाच ..
एवं स बहुशो विप्राः क्रुशित्वा पवनात्मजः ..
दण्डवत्प्रणतो भूमौ क्रोधशोकाकुलोऽभवत् .. 16 ..
तं दृष्ट्वा रघुनाथोऽपि प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत् ..
पश्यतां सवदेवानां मुनीनां कपिरक्षसाम् ..
सांत्वयन्मारुतिं तत्र दुःखं चास्य प्रमार्जयन् .. 17 ..
.. श्रीराम उवाच ..
सर्वं जानाम्यहं कार्यमात्मनोऽपि परस्य च .. 18 ..
जातस्य जायमानस्य मृतस्यापि सदा कपे ..
जायते म्रियते जन्तुरेक एव स्वकर्मणा 19 ..
प्रयाति नरकं चापि परमात्मा तु निर्गुणः ..
एवं तत्त्वं विनिश्चित्य शोकं मा कुरु वानर .. 3.1.45.20 ..

3.1.m:
“What shall I do? Where shall I go? I have no refuge.
Therefore, disregarded by you, I shall abandon my body!” (15)
Śrī Sūta said:
Having thus lamented repeatedly, O brahmins, the son of the wind,
prostrated on the ground like a stick, overcome by anger and grief. (16)
Seeing him, the lord of the Raghus too, smiling gently, said this,
while all the gods, sages, monkeys, and demons were watching,
consoling Māruti there and wiping away his sorrow: (17)
Śrī Rāma said:
“I know all the actions of oneself and of another, (18)
of what is born, what is being born, and even what is dead at all times, O monkey!
A creature is born and dies alone by its own karma; (19)
and it goes to hell, while the supreme Self is free of attributes.
Having ascertained the truth thus, do not grieve, O monkey! (20)
Free from the three liṅgas, the single light, taintless,
without support, immutable—behold that Self constantly! (21)
Why do you succumb to grief, an obstacle to the knowledge of truth?

3.1.d:
तत्त्वज्ञाने सदा निष्ठां कुरु वानरसत्तम .. 22 ..
स्वयंप्रकाशमात्मानं ध्यायस्व सततं कपे ..
देहादौ ममतां मुंच तत्त्वज्ञानविरोधिनीम् .. 23 ..
धर्मं भजस्व सततं प्राणिहिंसां परित्यज ..
सेवस्व साधुपुरुषाञ्जहि सर्वेंद्रियाणि च .. 24 ..
परित्यजस्व सततमन्येषां दोषकीर्तनम् ..
शिवविष्ण्वादिदेवानामर्चां कुरु सदा कपे .. 25 ..
सत्यं वदस्व सततं परित्यज शुचं कपे ..
प्रत्यग्ब्रह्मैकताज्ञानं मोहवस्तुसमुद्गतम् .. 26 ..
शोभनाशोभना भ्रांतिः कल्पि तास्मिन्यथार्थवत् ..
अध्यास्ते शोभनत्वेन पदार्थे मोहवैभवात् .. 27 ..
रोगो विजायते नृणां भ्रांतानां कपिसत्तम ..
रागद्वेषबलाद्बद्धा धर्मा धर्मवशंगताः .. 28 ..
देवतिर्यङ्मनुष्याद्या निरयं यांति मानवाः ..
चंदनागरुकर्पूरप्रमुखा अतिशोभनाः .. 29 ..
मलं भवंति यत्स्पर्शात्तच्छरीरं कथं सुखम्..
3.1.m:
Remain ever steadfast in the knowledge of truth, O best of monkeys! (22)
Continually meditate, O monkey, on the Self which is self-luminous!
Cast off the sense of ‘mine’ in the body and the rest, which opposes the knowledge of truth! (23)
Ever practice righteousness; abandon violence toward living beings;
serve virtuous persons; and conquer all the senses! (24)
Always abandon the recounting of the faults of others;
worship the deities, Śiva, Viṣṇu, and the rest at all times, O monkey! (25)
Speak the truth constantly; cast away sorrow, O monkey!
Knowledge of the oneness of the inner self with Brahman [destroys that which] arises from the object of delusion. (26)
The delusion of agreeable and disagreeable is imagined in this [world] as if real;
one superimposes agreeableness upon an object through the power of delusion. (27)
Affliction arises in deluded men, O best of monkeys!
Bound by the force of passion and aversion, subject to merit and demerit, (28)
mortals go to hell, [or are reborn as] gods, animals, humans, and so on.
Exceedingly pleasing substances such as sandalwood, agallochum, and camphor (29)
turn to filth through contact with the body; how can that body bring happiness?

3.1.m:
And that knowledge arises in one who is dispassionate, not in any other,
truly in one who is qualified foremost, by the grace of the teacher.
When all desires that abide in his heart are released,
then a mortal becomes immortal, and here itself attains the supreme Brahman.
Whether waking, sleeping, eating, or standing still,
cruel Death drags this person away constantly.
All accumulations end in depletion; all elevations end in fall;
unions end in separation; and life ends in death.
Just as for ripe fruits there is no fear other than falling,
so for men who are born there is no fear other than falling [into death].
Just as a house with firm pillars perishes when it decays in time,
so men perish, subject to old age and death.
Through the passing of day and night, the lifespan of men is destroyed;
grieve for yourself! Why do you grieve for another?
Lifespan perishes whether standing or running, O lord of monkeys:

3.1.m:
death walks together with [man]; death sits together [with him];
having travelled to a distant land, death returns along with [him].
Wrinkles have come upon the body, the hair has turned white;
the body decays through old age, and through breathing difficulty, coughing, and the like.
Just as two pieces of wood might come together in the great ocean,
and having come together, drift apart through the course of time, O monkey,
so wife, son, daughter-in-law, fields, and wealth
meet together somewhere and then depart elsewhere, O monkey.
Just as someone standing along the road [says] to a traveler walking on the way:
“I too will travel along with you,”
and the two, having joined together for a time, depart elsewhere again,
even so the union with wives, sons, and others is transitory, O monkey.
Along with the birth of the body, death is certainly born;
there is never any counteracting an inevitable death.
When this body falls, the embodied soul follows the course of its karma;

3.1.m:
having obtained another body, my child, it abandons the former body.
Living beings do not dwell constantly in one place, O monkey;
all are separated one by one according to their own karma.
Just as the bodies of living beings perish and come into existence,
the self has no birth and death, O best of monkeys.
Therefore, O son of Añjanā, meditate day and night on griefless, non-dual,
pure Brahman whose nature is being.
Action done by you is action done by me; what is done by me is done by you;
therefore the installation of my liṅga is the installation of your liṅga, O monkey.
Because the auspicious moment was passing, the sandy liṅga made by Sītā
was installed here by me; therefore, do not feel anger or sorrow.
Install the liṅga brought from Kailāsa on this auspicious day;
let this liṅga become renowned in the three worlds by your name!
Having seen Hanūmadīśvara, Rāghaveśvara must be seen.
The hosts of Brahmarākṣasas were slain by you, O monkey;

3.1.m:
Therefore, by establishing a liṅga in your own name, you will be liberated.
Given personally by Hara, the Śiva named Hanūmat,
a man who beholds it and Rāmanātha will have accomplished his purpose.
Even at a distance of a thousand yojanas, by remembering Hanūmat's liṅga,
and remembering Rāmanātheśvara as well, he will attain union [with Śiva].
He has performed sacrifices with all rituals and carried out austerity completely,
by whom the two Great Gods, Hanūmadīśvara and Rāghaveśvara, have been seen.
The liṅga made by Hanūmat, the liṅga made by me,
the liṅga belonging to Jānakī, and the liṅga Lakṣmaṇeśvara;
that which was made by Sugrīva, and by Nala the builder of the bridge;
made by Aṅgada, by Nīla, and likewise by Jāmbavat;
and the jewel-liṅga established by Vibhīṣaṇa;
the liṅga made by Indra and the gods, and that established by Śeṣa and others—
thus this Śiva manifests directly in eleven forms.
For Maheśvara is always present in these liṅgas.

3.1.m:
Therefore, install Maheśvara for the purification of your multitude of sins.
Moreover, if you, O fortunate one, will uproot the liṅga
made of sand by Sītā and installed here by me, my child,
I will then install this liṅga brought by you.
Reaching Pātāla, Sutala, Vitala, and Rasātala,
and piercing Talātala, this [liṅga] firmly stands.
Who could have the strength to break the liṅga consecrated by me?
Arise, monkey! Uproot this liṅga installed by me,
and quickly install the liṅga brought by you; do not grieve!"
Addressed thus, having bowed to him, the monkey, unaware of its true reality, [thought]:
"I will swiftly uproot the excellent sandy liṅga,
and respectfully install the liṅga brought from Kailāsa.
What burden could the uprooting of a sandy [liṅga] be for me?"
Having reflected thus in his mind, Hanūmat, the son of the wind-god,
as all the gods, sages, monkeys, and rakṣasas were watching,

3.1.m:
as Rāmacandra looked on, and as Lakṣmaṇa looked on,
and as Vaidehī looked on, that mighty one forcefully seized
that sandy liṅga with his hand swiftly, using all his effort.
Even shaking it with great effort, the son of the wind-god
was unable by his power to move the sandy liṅga.
Then, making a clamorous shout, the bull among monkeys,
raising his tail, hurled it with his hands, using his own strength.
Even shaking it in numerous ways thus, the monkey,
the son of the wind, was not at all able to move it.
Wrapping it with his tail and touching the earth with both hands,
the monkey, the son of the wind, then flew up swiftly into the sky,
shaking the entire earth with its seven continents and mountains.
At a mere krośa from the liṅga, swooning and vomiting blood,
Hanūmān fell upon the ground, O brahmins, his limbs trembling.
From the mouth and from both eyes of the falling son of the wind,

Then a cry of distress arose from all, including gods, asuras, and humans.
Both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, running along with the monkeys
accompanied by Jānakī, O brahmins, were then agitated with grief.
Accompanied by Sītā and the mighty monkeys, the two heroes
shone then upon Mount Gandhamādana, O brahmins,
like the moon and sun accompanied by the host of stars in the night.
They saw Hanūmat, his body shattered,
fallen on the ground in a swoon, vomiting blood from his mouth.
Seeing him, all the monkeys, crying out in grief, fell to the ground.
With both hands, Sītā compassionately touched Hanūmat, the son of the wind,
who had fallen upon the surface of the earth, saying, "Dear child! Dear child!"
Rāma too, having seen Hanūmat, the lord of monkeys, fallen down,
placed him in his lap and stroked his body with both hands.

3.1.m: Surasā, the mother of the Nāgas, was also overcome by you for my sake.
You slew the exceedingly cruel demoness who seized shadows.
Having reached Suvela in the evening and struck Laṅkā with your hand,
you went to Rāvaṇa's palace for my sake, O great monkey.
Searching for Sītā in Laṅkā by night, free from fear,
not seeing Jānakī, you then went to the Aśoka grove.
Bowing to Vaidehī and giving the token of recognition,
and taking the crest-jewel from Jānakī's hand for my sake,
you broke the trees of the Aśoka grove, O great monkey.
Then the eighty thousand rākṣasas named Kiṃkaras,
equal to Rāvaṇa in battle, crowded with infantry, horses, elephants, and chariots,
possessing great strength and prowess, you indeed slew for my sake.
Then, Prahasta's son Jambumālin having arrived,
you slew [him and] the seven sons of the ministers, who were radiant as fire.
Next you dispatched five army commanders to the abode of Yama;
then you killed prince Akṣa at the vanguard of battle.

He established it according to the Vedic rite, O best of brahmins.

Concerning Rāmanātha, a sin-destroying story

Formerly there was a king, the ruler of the Pāṇḍya country, named Śaṅkara,
devoted to brahmins, true to his word, performing many sacrifices, and righteous.
Knowing the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, tearing through enemy armies,
protecting all four stages of life and social classes according to dharma,
devoted to Vedic conduct, well-versed in the Purāṇas and Smṛtis,
a perpetual worshipper of Śiva and Viṣṇu, and a worshipper of other deities as well,
always giving great gifts to noble brahmins.
Once that wise man went to an ascetic grove for hunting,
which was terrifying with cruel creatures—lions, tigers, elephants, and buffaloes—
resounding with the dreadful chirping of crickets, teeming with serpents,
full of fierce wild beasts, terrifying with forest fire.
Having entered that great forest, King Śaṅkara,
accompanied by many soldiers, surrounded by a band of hunters,
with his feet hidden in leather sandals, wearing a red turban and green garments,
with bowman's wrist-guard and finger-guards fastened, holding a bow and arrows,
with a large sword strapped to his side, mounted on an excellent white horse,
splendidly dressed, armored, surrounded by troops of foot-soldiers,

3.1.m: Thus the majesty of Rāmanātha has been told to you, O brahmins,
and the meritorious deed, the sacred story of the king named Śaṃkara. (32)
A person who hears or reads this chapter with respect,
freed from all sins, attains Rāmanātha. (133)

3.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe setumāhātmye rāmanāthapraśaṃsāyāṃ śākalyadurmaraṇadoṣaśāṃtipūrvaka śaṃkarastrīhatyābrahmahatyādoṣaśāṃtivarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 48 .. .. cha .. .. ..
3.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतुमाहात्म्ये रामनाथप्रशंसायां शाकल्यदुर्मरणदोषशांतिपूर्वक शंकरस्त्रीहत्याब्रह्महत्यादोषशांतिवर्णनंनामाष्टचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः .. 48 .. .. छ .. .. ..
3.1.m: Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Appeasement of the Sins of Slaying a Woman and Slaying a Brahmin by Śaṃkara Preceded by the Pacification of the Fault of Śākalya's Bad Death, in the Praise of Rāmanātha, in the Setumāhātmya, in the Third Book, the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the Glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of Eighty-One Thousand Verses.' (48)
Śrī Sūta said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully relate the chapter of the hymn to the trident-bearing Rāmanātha;
listen with faith, O twice-born ones, to this greatly meritorious [account]. (1)
When the liṅga was established, Rāma praised the Supreme Lord.
Lakṣmaṇa, Jānakī Sītā, Sugrīva and the other lords of monkeys, (2)
the gods headed by Brahmā, and the great seers headed by the pot-born [Agastya],
endued with devotion, praised Rāghaveśvara individually. (3)
I shall relate that in proper order; listen with reverence.
By the mere hearing of this, a human being would become liberated, O twice-born ones. (4)
Śrī Rāma said:
Homage to you, the Great-Souled, the wielder of the great illusion, the bearer of the trident,
the remover of distress for the devotees of your own lotus-feet, the wearer of serpents! (5)
Homage to the God of gods, to Rāmanātha, the witness;
homage to the one to be known through Vedānta, the granter of ultimate truth to yogins; (6)
to the one always full of bliss, to Viśvanātha, to Śambhu;
homage to the dust of whose lotus-feet is the cause of cutting off the fear of devotees! (7)
Homage to you, the Lord of all; homage to the Supreme Self manifest;
homage to you of wondrous valour, the destroyer of great sins! (8)
Homage to you, the Death of Death, Time itself, and transcending time;
homage to you, the slayer of ignorance, and homage to the remover of sin! (9)
Homage to the sole cause of extinguishing the burning heat of those scorched by transmigration!
Homage to the destroyer of my [sin of] murdering a brahmin, and the consumer of poison! (10)
Homage to you, lord of Pārvatī, imperishable dweller of Kailāsa!
O bearer of Gaṅgā, odd-eyed one, protect me from all misfortunes! (11)
Homage to you who hold the Pināka bow in hand, the destroyer of Madana!
Repeated homage to you in all states at all times! (12)
Lakṣmaṇa said:
Homage to you, Śambhu, the lord of Rāma, the destroyer of Tripura,
The lord of Pārvatī's life, father of Gaṇeśa and Skanda! (13)
Homage to you whose eyes are the sun, moon, and fire, who wear braided hair!
Homage to Śiva, accompanied by Umā, who dispels the fear of Mārkaṇḍeya! (14)
Homage to the cause of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the entire phenomenal world!
Homage to the fierce, the dreadful, the great god, the witness! (15)
To the all-knowing, the most worthy of choice, the giver of boons, the best,
Homage to you, Śrīkaṇṭha, the dispeller of the five great sins! (16)
Let there be homage to you whose nature is supreme bliss, reality, and consciousness!
Homage to you, the destroyer of the disease of transmigratory existence; homage to the lord of sinews! (17)

3.1.s: pataye taskarāṇāṃ te vanānāṃ pataye namaḥ ..
3.1.d: पतये तस्कराणां ते वनानां पतये नमः ..
3.1.m: Homage to you, the lord of thieves, the lord of forests!
Homage to you, the lord of the Gaṇas, the universal form, the witness! (18)

3.1.s: karmaṇā preritaḥ śambho janiṣye yatrayatra tu ..
3.1.d: कर्मणा प्रेरितः शम्भो जनिष्ये यत्रयत्र तु ..
3.1.m: Impelled by my action, O Śambhu, wherever I shall be born,
There let me have devotion to your pair of feet! (19)
By your grace, let there be no pleasure for me on the unrighteous path,
And let my delight be in the path of Vedic conduct; homage to you! (20)
Sītā said:
O ultimate cause, Śaṃkara, matted-haired one, adorned with the saffron from the breasts of the Mountain's daughter!

3.1.s: mama patau paridehi matiṃ sadā na viṣamāṃ parapūruṣagocarām .. .. 21 ..
3.1.d: मम पतौ परिदेहि मतिं सदा न विषमां परपूरुषगोचराम् .. .. 21 ..
3.1.m: Bestow upon me a mind always directed toward my husband, never turned adversely toward another man. (21)
O bearer of Gaṅgā, odd-eyed one, blue-and-red one, Śaṃkara,
Lord of Rāma, homage to you; protect me, O mine of compassion! (22)
Homage to you, lord of the god of gods; homage to you, abode of compassion!
Homage to you, the crusher of the fear of transmigration for those afraid of transmigration! (23)
O Lord, by meditating on your lotus-feet, swiftly casting off fear of the son of the Sun, O Śambhu,

3.1.s: nityatvamāśu gatavānsa mṛkaṃḍuputraḥ kiṃ vā na sidhyati tavāśrayaṇātpareśa .. 24 ..
3.1.d: नित्यत्वमाशु गतवान्स मृकंडुपुत्रः किं वा न सिध्यति तवाश्रयणात्परेश .. 24 ..
3.1.m: That son of Mṛkaṇḍu swiftly attained immortality; what indeed is not accomplished by taking refuge in you, O supreme Lord? (24)
O supreme Lord, supreme bliss, protector of those who take refuge [in you]!

3.1.s: pātivratyaṃ mama sadā dehi tubhyaṃ namonamaḥ .. .. 25 ..
3.1.d: पातिव्रत्यं मम सदा देहि तुभ्यं नमोनमः .. .. 25 ..
3.1.m: Bestow devotion to my husband upon me forever; homage, homage to you! (25)
Hanūmān said:
O god of gods, lord of the world, lord of Rāma, treasure of mercy!
Let there be unswerving devotion in me toward your lotus feet! (26)

3.1.s: yaṃ vinā na jagatsattā tadbhānamapi no bhavet..
3.1.d: यं विना न जगत्सत्ता तद्भानमपि नो भवेत्..
3.1.m: Without whom the world has no existence, and whose appearance even would not be,
Homage to Śambhu, the lord of Rāma, whose form is true manifestation! (27)
Aṅgada said:

3.1.s: yasya bhāsā jagadbhānaṃ yatprakāśaṃ vinā jagat ..
3.1.d: यस्य भासा जगद्भानं यत्प्रकाशं विना जगत् ..
3.1.m: By whose light the world appears, without whose illumination the world
Does not shine—homage to that Śambhu, the lord of Rāma! (28)
Jāmbavān said:
Whose bliss shines in reality as all bliss—
Homage to this Rāmeśvara, whose form is supreme bliss! (29)
Nīla said:
Which [reality] is always undivided, devoid of duality by distinctions of space, time, and direction—
Homage to this Rāmeśvara whose nature is non-difference! (30)
Nala said:
Through whose ignorance Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśāna are manifested,
Homage to you, that Rāmeśvara who is free of ignorance! (31)
Kumuda said:
Because whose true nature is not known, the Pradhāna has been conceived as the cause—
To that cause, Śambhu, the lord of Rāma! (32)
Panasa said:
Waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the rest are the manifestation of whose ignorance—
To him who is free from waking and the other [states], whose nature is consciousness, homage! (33)
Gaja said:
Because whose true nature is not known, atoms have in vain been imagined
As the cause of effects by wretched logicians. (34)
I always worship that Rāmanātha, the Great Lord, highest bliss,
the witness of all, as the nature of the Self. (35)
Gavākṣa said:
I perpetually seek refuge in Rāmeśvara, Śiva, the tranquil,
who releases bound souls bound by the fetter of ignorance. (36)
Gavaya said:
I praise Rāmanātha, Śiva, the support of all the worlds, / who bears the moon on his crest, the lord of Umā,
the remedy for the disease of worldly existence. (37)
Śarabha said:
I bow to that Rāmanātha, the Self, / who is proclaimed to be merely the internal organ
by those deluded by ignorance of Him. (38)
Gandhamādana said:
I worship the Lord of the Universe, Rāmanātha, the lord of Umā,
the lord of the gaṇas, the three-eyed one, for purification from all sins. (39)
Sugrīva said:
In the midst of the ocean of worldly existence, in fearful water of birth and death,
crowded with rows of waves that are sons, wives, wealth, and fields; (40)
and fallen into a sinking piece of the cosmic egg, finding no ferryman,
crying out, helpless, wretched, trembling before the serpents of sense objects, (41)
terrified by the crocodile of disease, tormented by the fish of the three afflictions—

3.1.s: māṃ rakṣa girijānātha rāmanātha namo'stu te .. 42 ..
3.1.d: मां रक्ष गिरिजानाथ रामनाथ नमोऽस्तु ते .. 42 ..
3.1.m: protect me, O lord of the mountain's daughter, O Rāmanātha, homage be to you! (42)
Vibhīṣaṇa said:
In the midst of the forest of worldly existence, having lost my own path,
where disease is a thief, anger a lion, birth a tiger, and dissolution a serpent; (43)
in the greatly terrifying, blind well of childhood, youth, and old age,
in the fire of anger, jealousy, and greed, on the cruel mountain of sense objects; (44)
and filled with the thorns of fear on the ground—lead me, blind and fainting now,
to the auspicious state, O Śambhu, O Rāmeśvara, now! (45)
All the monkeys said:
Having taken birth, O Lord, everywhere in censurable and uncensurable wombs,
and having fallen again into hells such as Kumbhīpāka; (46)
and having taken birth again in a vile womb through residual karma,
fallen into worldly existence—save us, O Rāmanātha, treasure of compassion! (47)
Protect us, lordless, helpless, wretched, crying out, O Śaṃkara!
Homage be to you, ocean of compassion, Rāmanātha, Great Lord! (48)
Brahmā said:
Homage to you, the lord of the worlds, to Rāmanātha, to Śambhu!
Be gracious to me, Lord of All! Destroy my ignorance! (49)
Indra said:
Whose power is goddess Umā, the mother of the universe, consisting of the three Vedas—
I praise that Śaṃkara, Rāmanātha, the lord of Umā. (50)
Yama said:

3.1.s: putrau gaṇeśvaraskaṃdau vṛṣo yasya ca vāhanam ..
3.1.d: पुत्रौ गणेश्वरस्कंदौ वृषो यस्य च वाहनम् ..
3.1.m: Whose sons are the Lord of Gaṇas and Skanda, and whose vehicle is the bull—
him indeed, Rāmeśvara, I serve for the cessation of all ignorance. (51)
Varuṇa said:
By the power of whose worship the son of Mṛkaṇḍu conquered death,
that Rāmanātha, the conqueror of death, I indeed worship in my heart. (52)
Kubera said:
To the Lord, whose ornament is shining earrings,
whose body is red as lac, homage indeed to Rāmeśvara! (53)
Āditya said:
Homage be to you, Mahādeva, Rāmanātha, Three-Eyed One,
to the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, homage to you; protect me, O Śiva! (54)
Soma said:
Homage to you who are smeared with ashes, who bear the trident, garlanded with serpents,
O Rāmanātha, ocean of compassion, to you who dwell in the cremation ground! (55)
Agni said:
O you whose lotus feet are served by Indra and all the guardians of the directions,
to pure Rāmanātha, space-clad, perpetual homage! (56)
Vāyu said:
To Hara, who has the form of Hari, and whose garment is a tiger skin,
O Rāmanātha, obeisance to you! Grant me my desired wish! (57)
Bṛhaspati said:
To the eternal witness of the ego-sense, to the inward, non-dual reality,
O Rāmanātha, quickly destroy my ignorance! Obeisance to you! (58)
Śukra said:
To the one unattainable by deceivers, whose form is the meaning of the great mantra,
Obeisance to Śambhu, to Rāmanātha, who is free from duality! (59)
The two Aśvins said:
Who constantly shines in the hearts of yogins as the nature of the Self,
Known through undivided manifestation: obeisance to you, O Rāghaveśvara! (60)
Agastya said:
O primeval god, O Mahādeva, O Lord of the Universe, auspicious, imperishable one,
O Rāmanātha, Lord of Ambikā, be pleased, O bull-bannered one! (61)
Forgive my thousand offenses, O moon-crested one;
release me from the sense of “I” and “mine” concerning sons and the rest! (62)
Sutīkṣṇa said:

3.1.s: kṣetrāṇi ratnāni dhanāni dārā mitrāṇi vastrāṇi gavāśvaputrāḥ ..
3.1.d: क्षेत्राणि रत्नानि धनानि दारा मित्राणि वस्त्राणि गवाश्वपुत्राः ..
3.1.m: Lands, gems, wealth, wives, friends, garments, cattle, horses, and sons

3.1.s: naivopakārāya hi rāmanātha mahyaṃ prayaccha tvamato viraktim .. 63 ..
3.1.d: नैवोपकाराय हि रामनाथ मह्यं प्रयच्छ त्वमतो विरक्तिम् .. 63 ..
3.1.m: are indeed of no real benefit, O Rāmanātha; therefore, grant me dispassion! (63)
Viśvāmitra said:

3.1.s: śrutāni śāstrāṇyapi niṣphalāni trayyapyadhītā viphalaiva nūnam ..
3.1.d: श्रुतानि शास्त्राण्यपि निष्फलानि त्रय्यप्यधीता विफलैव नूनम् ..
3.1.m: The scriptures that have been heard are fruitless, and the three Vedas that have been studied are surely vain,

3.1.s: tvayīśvare cenna bhaveddhi bhaktiḥ śrīrāmanāthe śiva mānuṣasya ..64.. ..
3.1.d: त्वयीश्वरे चेन्न भवेद्धि भक्तिः श्रीरामनाथे शिव मानुषस्य ..64.. ..
3.1.m: if a mortal has no devotion to you, Īśvara, the auspicious Śrī Rāmanātha. (64)
Gālava said:
Gifts, sacrifices, observances, austerities, and immersions in sacred fords like the Gaṅgā—

3.1.s: rāmeśvaraṃ tvāṃ na namaṃti ye tu vyarthāni teṣāmiti niścayo'tra .. 65 ..
3.1.d: रामेश्वरं त्वां न नमंति ये तु व्यर्थानि तेषामिति निश्चयोऽत्र .. 65 ..
3.1.m: for those who do not bow to you, Rāmeśvara, these are all useless; this is certain here. (65)
Vasiṣṭha said:
Even if someone has committed all sins, if, endowed with devotion, he approaches you, O Rāmeśvara,
and bows, those [sins] will dissolve just as darkness truly does before the light of the sun. (66)
Atri said:

3.1.s: dṛṣṭvā tu rāmeśvaramekadāpi spṛṣṭvā namaskṛtya bhavaṃtamīśam ..
3.1.d: दृष्ट्वा तु रामेश्वरमेकदापि स्पृष्ट्वा नमस्कृत्य भवंतमीशम् ..
3.1.m: Having beheld Rāmeśvara even once, having touched and bowed to you, the Lord,

3.1.s: punarna garbhaṃ sa naraḥ prayāyātkiṃ tvadvayaṃ te labhataṃ svarūpam .. 67 ..
3.1.d: पुनर्न गर्भं स नरः प्रयायात्किं त्वद्वयं ते लभतं स्वरूपम् .. 67 ..
3.1.m: that man will not enter a womb again; rather, he attains your non-dual nature. (67)
Aṅgiras said:
That person who, approaching you, Rāmanātha, remembers his kinsmen while bowing,
delivers even them from all sins; what wonder is there, then, in his own attainment of his goal? (68)
Gautama said:
O holy lord Rāmanātheśvara, this supreme mystery is hidden and free from grief:

3.1.s: tvatpādamūlaṃ bhajatāṃ nṛṇāṃ ye sevāṃ prakurvaṃti hi te'pi dhanyāḥ .. 69 ..
3.1.d: त्वत्पादमूलं भजतां नृणां ये सेवां प्रकुर्वंति हि तेऽपि धन्याः .. 69 ..
3.1.m: those men who render service to those who worship the soles of your feet are fortunate indeed! (69)
Śatānanda said:
This is to be known by seekers of liberation who know the secret of the knowledge of Vedānta:

3.1.s: śāstrāṇi sarvāṇi vihāya deva tvatsevanaṃ yadraghuvīranātha .. 3.1.49.70 ..
3.1.d: शास्त्राणि सर्वाणि विहाय देव त्वत्सेवनं यद्रघुवीरनाथ .. 3.1.49.70 ..
3.1.m: abandoning all scriptures, O God, Lord of the hero of the Raghus, service to you [is everything]! (70)
Bhṛgu said:
O Rāmanātha, having shaken off all impurities through contemplation of the dualities,

3.1.s: nirbhayaṃ vrajati satsukhādvayaṃ suprabhaṃ tvatha amoghaciddhanam .. 71 ..
3.1.d: निर्भयं व्रजति सत्सुखाद्वयं सुप्रभं त्वथ अमोघचिद्धनम् .. 71 ..
3.1.m: one goes fearlessly to the lotus of your feet, which is non-dual true bliss, radiant, and an unerring mass of consciousness. (71)
Kutsa said:

3.1.s: rāmanātha tava pādasevanaṃ bhogamokṣavaradaṃ nṛṇāṃ sadā ..
3.1.d: रामनाथ तव पादसेवनं भोगमोक्षवरदं नृणां सदा ..
3.1.m: O Rāmanātha, service to your feet always bestows the boons of enjoyment and liberation upon men
and destroys hells such as Raurava; what person of discerning taste would not worship [them]? (72)
Kāśyapa said:

3.1.s: rāmanātha tava pādasevināṃ kiṃ vratairuta tapobhiradhvaraiḥ ..
3.1.d: रामनाथ तव पादसेविनां किं व्रतैरुत तपोभिरध्वरैः ..
3.1.m: O Rāmanātha, for those who serve your feet, what need is there of vows, austerities, or sacrifices?

3.1.s: vedaśāstra japacintayā ca kiṃ svargasindhupayasāpi kiṃ phalam .. 73 ..
3.1.d: वेदशास्त्र जपचिन्तया च किं स्वर्गसिन्धुपयसापि किं फलम् .. 73 ..
3.1.m: What need of meditating on the Vedas, scriptures, and recitation? What fruit even from the water of the river of heaven? (73)

3.1.s: śrīrāmanātha tvamāgatya śīghraṃ mamotkrāṃtikāle bhavānyā ca sākam ..
3.1.d: श्रीरामनाथ त्वमागत्य शीघ्रं ममोत्क्रांतिकाले भवान्या च साकम् ..
3.1.m: O venerable Rāmanātha, come quickly together with Bhavānī at the time of my death,

3.1.s: māṃ prāpaya svātmapādāravindaṃ viśokaṃ vimohaṃ sukhaṃ citsvarūpam .. 74 ..
3.1.d: मां प्रापय स्वात्मपादारविन्दं विशोकं विमोहं सुखं चित्स्वरूपम् .. 74 ..
3.1.m: and lead me to the lotus of your own feet, which is free from sorrow, free from delusion, blissful, and whose nature is consciousness. (74)
The gandharvas said:
O Rāmanātha, for us who worship [you] in the ocean of worldly existence,

3.1.s: apāre duḥkhakallole na tvattonyā gatirhi naḥ .. 75 ..
3.1.d: अपारे दुःखकल्लोले न त्वत्तोन्या गतिर्हि नः .. 75 ..
3.1.m: which is boundless with waves of suffering, there is indeed no other refuge than you. (75)
The kinnaras said:
O Rāmanātha, in the forest of worldly existence, terrifying with diseases and tigers,
there is no guide to show us the path other than you. (76)
The yakṣas said:
O Rāmanātha, the torment caused by the enemies that are our senses is constantly unbearable for us;
O Dhūrjaṭi, be our helper in conquering them! (77)
The nāgas said:
O Rāmanātha, of inconceivable majesty, how can we,
being of small intellect, be able to praise you, O lord of Ambikā?
The kiṃpuruṣas said:
Destroy our birth in various wombs and death many times over,
and likewise our ignorance, O Rāmanātha! Homage be to you!
The vidyādharas said:
To the lord of Ambikā, to you, unattached, the great soul,
homage to you, Rāmanātha! Be pleased, O bull-bannered one!
The vasus said:
To Rāmanātha, lord of the gaṇas, whose feet are worshipped by host of attendants,

3.1.s: gaṃgādharāya guhyāya namaste pāhi naḥ sadā .. 81 ..
3.1.d: गंगाधराय गुह्याय नमस्ते पाहि नः सदा .. 81 ..
3.1.m: to the bearer of the Gaṅgā, the hidden one, homage to you! Protect us always!
The viśvedevas said:
To the giver of liberation to noble yogins who are devoted solely to pure consciousness,
to Rāmanātha, accompanied by Ambā, homage! Protect us, O Śaṃkara!
The maruts said:
To the supreme reality, who in truth is the ultimate essence of all principles,
homage to you, Rāmanātha, self-luminous Śambhu!
The sādhyas said:
To him devoid of anything apart from himself, the giver of existence to the universe,
to the god Rāmeśvara, the destroyer of ignorance, homage!
All the gods said:
[He who is] full of being, consciousness, and bliss, free from any dual entity,
whose self is Brahman, self-luminous, devoid of beginning, middle, and end,
immutable, unattached, completely pure, eternal,
the witness of the manifest world consisting of space and the rest, the supreme nectar,
beyond valid cognition, yet the bestower of consciousness even upon the means of knowledge,
eternally free from manifestation, disappearance, and contraction,
the witness of this universe whose form is super-imposed upon himself,
untainted, supreme bliss, devoid of all action,
infinite bliss, the great soul, whose form is consciousness, devoid of enjoyment—

who appears differentiated through his own māyā in the form of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and others!

And each of the names of the pervasive Lord ending in the dative case, O twice-born ones,
and [to] the gods, seers, and ancestors, according to rule, with water and sesame seeds;
and uttering the names ending in the accusative case, one should offer water-oblations, O twice-born ones.
Wearing a purifying ring of darbha, standing in the water with a serene mind, one should offer water-oblations;
from offering water-oblations, one obtains the fruit of ritual ablution in all sacred fords.
Having thus offered water-oblations to them and bowed, he should come up out of the water;
casting off wet clothes and wrapped in dry garments,
having sipped water and wearing a purifying ring of darbha, he should perform the śrāddha according to rule.
And he should offer rice-balls to the ancestors with sesame seeds and grains of rice.
This śrāddha for one who is unable has been proclaimed by me, O best of the twice-born;
a wealthy man should indeed perform the śrāddha with food of six flavours.
A prosperous person should make gifts of cows, land, sesame seeds, gold, and the like.
At Rāmacandra's Dhanuṣkoṭi, one should perform [the rites] in this very manner;
beginning with the gift of stones and ending with water-oblations, O twice-born ones,
just as the twice-born performed them according to rule at Setumūla.
Having gone then to Cakratīrtha, one should perform a ritual ablution there as well,
and behold the god Hari Nārāyaṇa, the sovereign of the Setu.
Going along the western route, at Cakratīrtha located there,
having bathed, one should behold with devotion the god who reclines on darbha grass.
Then having reached Kapitīrtha, one should perform a ritual ablution there as well;
then having reached Sītākuṇḍa, one should perform a ritual ablution there as well.
Then having reached Ṛṇamocanatīrtha, which yields great fruit,

3.1.s: snātvā praṇamya rāmaṃ ca jānakīramaṇaṃ prabhum .. 53 ..
3.1.d: स्नात्वा प्रणम्य रामं च जानकीरमणं प्रभुम् .. 53 ..
3.1.m: having bathed and bowed to Rāma, the Lord who delights the daughter of Janaka,
he should go to Lakṣmaṇatīrtha, and having shaved [all hair] above the neck,
he should bathe there as well, reflecting upon his misdeeds.

3.1.s: tataḥ snātvā rāmatīrthe tato devālayaṃ vrajet ..
3.1.d: ततः स्नात्वा रामतीर्थे ततो देवालयं व्रजेत् ..
3.1.m: Having then bathed in Rāmatīrtha, he should go to the temple of the deity,
and having bathed in Pāpavināśana, and likewise in Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

3.1.s: sāvitryāṃ ca sarasvatyāṃ gāyatryāṃ ca dvijottamāḥ ..
3.1.d: सावित्र्यां च सरस्वत्यां गायत्र्यां च द्विजोत्तमाः ..
3.1.m: and in the Sāvitrī, Sarasvatī, and Gāyatrī, O best of brahmins,
and having bathed in Hanumatkuṇḍa, one should then bathe in [the pool of] great fruit.
Then, having reached Brahmakuṇḍa, one should bathe according to the rules. (56)
Then, having reached Nāgakuṇḍa, which destroys all sins,
a man should perform his ritual ablution, O brahmins, which destroys the afflictions of hell.
All the rivers, beginning with the Gaṅgā, and indeed all sacred fords, (57)
dwell perpetually in Nāgakuṇḍa for the appeasement of their own sins.
This excellent, auspicious sacred ford on Rāma's bridge, granting liberation, (58)
was established by the eight great Nāgas, beginning with Ananta.
Having reached Agastyakuṇḍa, one should then bathe in that peerless [pool]. (59)
Then, having approached Agnitīrtha, which destroys all bad karma,
having bathed and performed libations according to rule, one should perform a śrāddha, remembering the ancestors. (60)
Having given cows, land, gold, grain, and the like to brahmins according to one's capacity (61ab)
on the bank of Agnitīrtha, one is released from all sins. (61cd)
Alternatively, whatever sacred fords, beginning with Cakratīrtha, (62ab)
have been enumerated, O chiefs of brahmins, which remove all sins, (62cd)
one should bathe in them in succession, or bathe according to one's inclination.
Having thus bathed in all the sacred fords, one should perform śrāddha and the other rites. (63)
Afterward, having reached Rāmeśvara and worshipped the Supreme Lord,
having approached Setumādhava, as well as Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, (64)
Sītā, the son of the wind (Hanumān), and the other excellent monkeys,
and having bathed in all the sacred fords there according to the vows, (65)
having bowed to Rāmanātha, Rāmacandra, and the others,
and having paid homage to Dhanuṣkoṭi, a person should then go to bathe [there]. (66)
There one should observe the previously mentioned rules, such as the offering of stones,
and give gifts at Dhanuṣkoṭi according to one's wealth: (67)
umbrellas, cows, and various garments, reverently (68ab)
to brahmins who know the Veda, according to one's wealth. (68cd)
Then, having reached Koṭitīrtha, one should bathe according to the rules.
Then one should bow to the god Rāmeśvara, whose emblem is the bull. (69)
If one has the means, one should give a priestly gift of gold to the brahmins,

3.1.s: tilāndhānyaṃ ca gāṃ kṣetraṃ vastrāṇyanyāni taṃḍulān .. 3.1.51.70 ..
3.1.d: तिलान्धान्यं च गां क्षेत्रं वस्त्राण्यन्यानि तंडुलान् .. 3.1.51.70 ..
3.1.m: sesame seeds, grain, a cow, land, garments, and rice grains. (70)
Free from greed for wealth, one should give according to one's means (71ab)
incense, a lamp, food offering, and implements of worship (71cd)
to the god Rāmeśvara according to one's means.

3.1.s: stutvā rāmeśvaraṃ devaṃ praṇamya ca sabhaktikam .. 72 ..
3.1.d: स्तुत्वा रामेश्वरं देवं प्रणम्य च सभक्तिकम् .. 72 ..
3.1.m: Having praised the god Rāmeśvara and bowed with devotion, (72)
having taken leave, one should then go to the presence of Setumādhava.

3.1.s: tasmai dattvā ca dhūpādīnanujñāpya ca mādhavam .. 73 ..
3.1.d: तस्मै दत्त्वा च धूपादीननुज्ञाप्य च माधवम् .. 73 ..
3.1.m: Having offered incense and the like to him and taken leave of Mādhava, (73)
observing the previously mentioned rules, one should return to one's own home.
One should feed brahmins with dishes full of the six flavors. (74)
By that alone, Rāmanātha, being pleased, grants him his desired wish;

3.1.s: nārakaṃ cāsya nāstyeva dāridryaṃ ca vinaśyati .. .. 75 ..
3.1.d: नारकं चास्य नास्त्येव दारिद्र्यं च विनश्यति .. .. 75 ..
3.1.m: there is no hell for him, and poverty is destroyed; (75)
the lineage of that man flourishes, O best of brahmins;
having quickly cast off worldly existence, he attains even union [with the Divine]. (76)
If one is unable to come here, whatever collection of texts in the Śruti, Smṛti, and Āgama (77ab)
is very meritorious and proclaims the greatness of the Setu, (77cd)
one should cause that text to be recited, O brahmins, which destroys great sins,
or one should read this Setumāhātmya with devotion. (78)
Thereby one undoubtedly obtains the meritorious fruit of bathing at the Setu.
This has been declared by the wise regarding the blind, the lame, and others. (79)
Śrī Sūta said:

3.1.s: evaṃ vaḥ kathito viprāḥ setuyātrākramo dvijāḥ ..
3.1.d: एवं वः कथितो विप्राः सेतुयात्राक्रमो द्विजाः ..
3.1.m: Thus the sequence of the pilgrimage to the Setu has been told to you, O twice-born brahmins.
Reading or hearing this, one is freed from all suffering. (80)

3.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे सेतुमाहात्म्ये यात्राक्रमवर्णनंनामैकपंचाशत्तमोऽध्यायः .. 51 ..
3.1.m: Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, entitled 'Description of the Sequence of Pilgrimage' in the Setumāhātmya of the third Brahmakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. (51)

O eminent brahmins, according to the path declared in the Veda—
their sins are destroyed by immersing in Rāma's bridge.
Incense, a lamp, sandalwood,
and flowers they do not offer with devotion to Śiva, Viṣṇu, and the other gods, O best of brahmins;
those evil-minded men who do not perform the ritual ablution of Śiva, Viṣṇu, and the other gods with the Śrīrudra hymns and the Camaka hymns,

those whose intellects are ruined by sin do not perform with devotion;
and who do not perform worship at dawn during the month of Dhanus,
preceded by the great food offering to Śiva, Viṣṇu, and the other gods—
their sins are destroyed by immersing in Rāma's bridge.

Whether ill-behaved or well-behaved, whoever attends upon Dhanuṣkoṭi,
his worldly transmigration is severed without rebirth.
Whoever desires to cross the ocean of worldly existence, O eminent sages,
should go without delay to Rāmacandra's Dhanuṣkoṭi.
I speak the truth, I speak what is beneficial, I speak the essence, and what is beneficial again:
go to Rāmacandra's Dhanuṣkoṭi for the attainment of liberation.
One should bathe at Rāmacandra's Dhanuṣkoṭi for release;
there is no other means, O brahmins—I say this again and again.
Those men who take a bath at Rāmacandra's Dhanuṣkoṭi—
for them, the destruction of the fear of worldly existence will be accomplished without effort.
Truth, knowledge, infinite, the full, eternal Brahman—
attainment of that comes from bathing at Dhanuṣkoṭi; there is no doubt of this.

Thus has the supreme Setumāhātmya been told to you, O brahmins;
it calms great sorrow, destroys great diseases,

bringing great peace to men who read or even listen to it,
granting heaven and liberation, meritorious, bestowing the fruit of all sacred fords.
Whoever, being attentive, recites this meritorious [text] or listens to it,
attains the abundant fruit of sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma.
Whatever fruit comes from reciting the four Vedas with their auxiliary limbs a hundred times,
that fruit one surely obtains from proclaiming this māhātmya.
By reading or hearing a single chapter here, O lords of sages,
one obtains the complete fruit of a horse sacrifice.
By reciting two chapters, and likewise by hearing them,
one attains the unsurpassed fruit of the sacrifice called Gomedha.
Whoever reads ten chapters, or listens with devotion,
attains the realm of heaven and rejoices with Śakra.
From reading and hearing twenty chapters, O lords of sages,
one attains the realm of Brahmā and rejoices with Brahmā.

one attains the realm of Viṣṇu and rejoices with Viṣṇu.
Whoever reads or even listens to forty chapters,
attains the realm of Rudra and rejoices with Rudra.
Whoever reads or hears fifty chapters,
attains Hara accompanied by Ambā, Śiva who bears the crescent moon on his crest.
Whoever reads and listens to this entire supreme māhātmya,
attains residence in the same world as Śiva accompanied by Ambā; there is no doubt of this.

goes to proximity with Śiva, seated in an excellent aerial chariot.

attains similarity of form with Śiva, bringing delight to Śiva.
Whoever reads this supreme [text] four times, or hears it,
attains union with Śiva, the lord of the mountain's daughter.

When this entire Setumāhātmya is recited or heard,
as many letters as there are in these verses,
that many killings of brahmins, that much drinking of liquor,
that much theft of gold, that many violations of the guru's bed,
and that many sins of association are indeed destroyed instantly in this way.
As many hosts of letters as there are in this greatly meritorious [text],
that many times the fruit born of bathing in the twenty-four sacred fords,
and likewise in the other sacred fords located within the Setu,
that fruit one fully obtains by reciting or hearing [it].
He by whom this supreme Setumāhātmya is copied out with devotion,
with the continuity of his ignorance destroyed, shall attain union with Śiva.
In whose house this auspicious māhātmya is kept copied down,
there is no fear there from bhūtas, vetālas, and the like.
There is no affliction from disease there, nor is there fear of thieves;

In whose house this meritorious, supreme māhātmya is present,
know that house, O bulls among sages, to be Rāmasetu.
The twenty-four sacred fords indeed dwell right there;
right there is the holy mountain Gandhamādana;
and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa dwell there with respect.
Having written down the Setumāhātmya, one should present it to a brahmin;
by him the earth bounded by the four oceans has been given.
The mantra for the gift of the Setumāhātmya:
All other gifts do not equal a sixteenth part
of the gift of the Setumāhātmya; therefore, grant me peace.
What need is there to say much more? The three worlds reside here.
He who recites even a single chapter of this at the time of a śrāddha,
any defect in the śrāddha will vanish, and the ancestors become overjoyed.

whether a single chapter or a verse, his cows will be free from affliction,

This holy [work] should be recited in a monastery, in a temple,
on the banks of rivers and lakes, on holy ground in a forest,
or in the house of learned Vedic scholars, but never anywhere else.
At the times of equinoxes and solstices, and on holy Hari-days,
and on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, it should be read especially.
This should be read during the full moon of Śrāvaṇa, and in the month of Bhādrapada,
in the month of Dhanus, and during the northern solstice.
O twice-born, this māhātmya must be recited with self-restraint alone,
and the listeners, bound by vows, should hear this supreme [work].
Many holy sacred fords are celebrated in this māhātmya,
and those of virtuous conduct are celebrated, as well as the best of royal seers.
Exalted seers are celebrated in this peerless [text];
righteousness and unrighteousness are celebrated in this holy [work], O best of the twice-born.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra—the three deities—are praised here.

3.1.m:
This sacred, sin-destroying [work], augmented with the teachings of the Vedas,
is approved by the authors of the Smṛtis and dear to the sage Dvaipāyana.
It should be heard and read by one who desires his own highest good.
And something, such as gold, must be given to the reciter;
in accordance with one's own capacity, one should not practice deceit regarding wealth.
Giving cloth, gold, grain, land, or a cow according to one's means,
this reciter should be honored by the listeners.
When that reciter is worshipped, the three deities are worshipped;
when the three deities are worshipped, the three worlds are worshipped.
Hari, incarnate on earth directly as Rāma, the son of Daśaratha,
together with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, ever to the listeners and the reciter,
having granted pleasures in this world, grants liberation at the end.
Issued from the lotus mouth of Dvaipāyana, bestowing the highest auspiciousness,
this very Setumāhātmya, King Yudhiṣṭhira, the embodiment of righteousness,
surrounded by all his younger brothers, beginning with Bhīmasena,

observing vows and right conduct, together with his army, day after day,
hears as it is recited by the great seer Dhaumya, his family priest.
The venerable Sūta said:
"O ascetics, all dwellers of the Naimiṣāraṇya forest!
This secret māhātmya, equal to the Vedas, has been heard by you
from me with restraint; recite it daily with reverence,
and teach it continually to your disciplined pupils."
Having spoken thus to those sages, Sūta, with his hair standing on end all over his body,
remembering his guru Vyāsa in his heart, danced, shedding tears.
Meanwhile, the greatly learned great sage, the son of Parāśara,
quickly appeared there out of a desire to bestow grace upon his disciple.
Seeing that sage, the son of Satyavatī, arrived,
Sūta, together with all the dwellers of Naimiṣāraṇya,
prostrated like a stick at the lotus feet of Vyāsa
and poured forth water born of bliss from his eyes.
Raising his devoted disciple who was bowed down with both arms,

Upon an excellent seat brought by the sages of Naimiṣāraṇya,
Dvaipāyana, of great splendour, rich in austerity, sat down.
When the sages and Sūta had also sat down by his command,
the grandson of Śakti addressed all the sages headed by Śaunaka:
"All this has been known to me, O dwellers of Naimiṣāraṇya,
that by my pupil Sūta this excellent Setumāhātmya
has been declared to you today, destroying heinous sins. (44)
Of the Śrutis, Smṛtis, and Purāṇas as well,
and of all treatises and histories entirely, (45)
this is the ultimate conclusion, namely this great māhātmya.
Among all the Purāṇas, this is highly esteemed by me. (46)
Dharma's son [Yudhiṣṭhira] listens to this daily from Dhaumya at my command.
Therefore, you also, always, this supreme Setumāhātmya (47)
should recite, listen to, and teach to your disciples."
Hearing that speech of his, they said, "Certainly!" (48)

Then Vyāsa, accompanied by his disciple Sūta,
took leave of all the sages and went to Mount Kailāsa. (49)
The seers dwelling in Naimiṣāraṇya attained contentment;
every day they listen to and recite the Setumāhātmya. (50)
Thus ends the fifty-second chapter in the Setumāhātmya of the Brahmakhaṇḍa, the third [section] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. (52)
Here ends the Setumāhātmya contained within the Brahmakhaṇḍa of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

3.1.m: Śrī Sūta said: / Once again I shall declare the majesty concerning the Setu / out of regard for you, O eminent sages; listen! (1) / Even among all holy places, this place is greater; / what is muttered in japa here, offered in oblation, practiced in austerity, or given in charity is said to be inexhaustible. (2) / In this very great place, from plunging into Dhanuṣkoṭi, / the meritorious fruit equal to ten years' residence in Vārāṇasī is obtained. (3) / Having bathed at that site in Dhanuṣkoṭi, and having seen the auspicious Rāmeśvara, / if a man full of devotion resides there for three days, O twice-born, (4) / the merit born of ten years' residence in Puṇḍarīkapura / is his, O chiefs of brahmins, destroying great sins. (5) / Having muttered the six-syllable primal mantra one thousand and eight times / here with devotion, a man attains union with Śiva. (6) / The merit born of living for a year in Madhyārjuna, Kumbhakoṇa, / Māyūra, Śvetakānana, / Hālāsya, Gajāraṇya, / Vedāraṇya, Naimiṣa, (7) / Śrīparvata, Śrīraṅga, / the glorious Vṛddhagiri, / Cidambara, Vālmīka, / Śeṣādri, Aruṇācala, (8) / the glorious Dakṣiṇakailāsa, / Veṅkaṭādri, Haristhala, / Kāñcīpura, Brahmapura, / Vaidyeśvarapura, (9) / and elsewhere in places of Śiva / and places of Viṣṇu, O best of men, / a man joyfully obtains undoubtedly, / if he bathes in Dhanuṣkoṭi in the month of Māgha. (10) / With reference to this Setu, the Śruti passage 'There are two oceans' (11) / exists, O best of brahmins, being ancient and mother-like. / There is another [Śruti passage], O eminent sages, 'That which is wood', (12) / and that which mentions the Setu's glory: 'Beholding the acts of Viṣṇu'; / there is another Śruti, and yet another: 'That [supreme foot] of Viṣṇu'. (13) / The Itihāsas, the Purāṇas, / and the Smṛtis, O rich in austerity, / proclaim the majesty of the Setu in complete consensus. (14) / Performing ablution at the Setu during eclipses of the moon and sun...

3.1.m: one obtains the fruit of ten years of ritual ablution in the Gaṅgā at Avimukta. / The sin committed in ten million births is destroyed in that very instant; // he obtains the unsurpassed fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices. / At the equinoxes, the solstices, on a Monday, and on a parvan day, // by the mere darśana of the Setu the misfortune earned across seven births / is destroyed, and [such men] attain the heavenly realm, O best of brahmins. / When the sun enters Capricorn in the month of Māgha, just as the sun has slightly risen, // a mortal who bathes for three days at Dhanuṣkoṭi becomes free from sin, / and obtains the merit of bathing in all sacred fords beginning with the Gaṅgā. // A man who performs ritual ablution at Dhanuṣkoṭi for five days, / O best of brahmins, attains the merit of a horse-sacrifice and others; // he gains the fruit of the observance of the Cāndrāyaṇa and other penances, / and likewise the fruit of reciting the four Vedas from beginning to end. // By immersing oneself at Dhanuṣkoṭi on ten days in the month of Māgha, / ten thousand murders of a brahmin are destroyed; there should be no doubt about this. // The person who performs ritual ablution at Dhanuṣkoṭi for fifteen days / in the month of Māgha reaches Vaikuṇṭha. // Performing ritual ablution at Rāmasetu for twenty days in the month of Māgha, / one attains proximity to Śiva and rejoices together with Śiva. // Performing ritual ablution for twenty-five days, one attains similarity of form [with the deity]; / performing ritual ablution for thirty days, one surely attains absorption [into the divine]. // Therefore, O best of brahmins, in the month of Māgha a wise man / should certainly perform ritual ablution at Rāmasetu just as the sun has slightly risen. // During an eclipse of the moon or sun, and likewise at the Ardhodaya yoga, O twice-born, / or at the Mahodaya yoga, performing ritual ablution at Rāmasetu, O best of brahmins, // one does not experience dwelling in the womb fraught with numerous afflictions. / And it is proclaimed as destroying sins such as the murder of a brahmin; // it is proclaimed as warding off all hells, / and it is proclaimed as the source of all prosperities.

3.1.m: Likewise, it grants dwelling in the same world as Indra and all the other worlds. / During an eclipse of the moon or sun, and likewise at the Ardhodaya yoga, O twice-born, // or at the Mahodaya yoga, immersion at Dhanuṣkoṭi is most decisive. / In ancient times, it was constructed by Rāma for the destruction of Rāvaṇa; // it is resorted to by Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, and serpents, / and attended by hosts of brahmin seers, divine seers, royal seers, and ancestors; // it is served with devotion by the host of deities headed by Brahmā. / O twice-born, whatever person, recollecting the holy Rāmasetu, // should bathe anywhere in a pond or other body of water, / no wicked deed shall ever belong to him. // By offering a mere handful of water in the sacred fords situated within the Setu, / all diseases are destroyed, and likewise [sins such as] the murder of an embryo. // Whoever sees the holy line made by the tip of Rāma’s bow, / for him there is never any return from Vaikuṇṭha. // That which is famed in the world as Dhanuṣkoṭi, destroying sins, / was made by wise Rāma at the petition of Vibhīṣaṇa. // Dhanuṣkoṭi is exceedingly holy; having bathed there with devotion, / one should give gifts of wealth, lands, and cows, // of sesame seeds, rice grains, grains, and milk, / of garments, ornaments, black gram, and cooked rice, // of curd, ghee, water, vegetables, and buttermilk, / of refined sugar, crops, and honey, // and indeed the giving of modaka sweets, cakes, and other things / at Rāmasetu, O twice-born, is declared to bestow all desired wishes. // Therefore, free from greed for wealth, one should give at Rāmasetu. / What is given, offered in fire, practiced as austerity, recited in japa, or observed as vows and the like // at the tip of the bow of glorious Rāma becomes infinite in its fruit. / By that, the Vedas are pleased, and the ancestors are pleased; // all the sages are pleased, as are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva;

3.1.m: the nāgas, kimpuruṣas, and yakṣas are all surely pleased. / And by beholding Dhanuṣkoṭi, one personally becomes purified; // one purifies all the men born in one's family and one's grandfathers, / and through the darśana of Dhanuṣkoṭi delivers one's entire lineage. // By immersing oneself in the furrow made by the tip of Rāma's bow, / the destruction of tens of millions of major sins surely occurs in that very instant. // Whoever sees the line made by the tip of glorious Rāma’s bow / does not behold dwelling in the womb full of countless afflictions. // By plunging into that pool where Sītā entered the fire, / O brahmins, a hundred murders of an embryo are destroyed in a mere instant. // Just as Rāma is, so is the Setu; just as the Gaṅgā is, so is Hari. / Proclaiming 'O Gaṅgā! O Hari! O Rāmasetu!', / wherever a person bathes outside, through that he reaches the supreme state. // Having bathed at the Setu during an Ardhodaya yoga on Mount Gandhamādana, / whoever presents balls of rice measuring merely a mustard seed dedicated to the ancestors, // his ancestors attain satisfaction for as long as the moon and sun endure. / If a ball of rice measuring the size of a leaf of the śamī tree is given with devotion / dedicated to the ancestors by a twice-born, he is released from all sin; / if [the ancestor] is in heaven, he attains liberation, and if in hell, he goes to heaven. // At the Setu, at Padmanābha, at Gokarna, and at Puruṣottama, / bathing in the water of the ocean is desired at all times. // On the days of Venus, Mars, and Saturn, one desirous of offspring / should never bathe in saltwater anywhere other than the Setu. // Or one who has not performed the funeral rites for a departed soul, or the husband of a pregnant woman— / a wise person should never bathe in the ocean anywhere other than the Setu. // There is no awaiting a proper time for the Setu; constant bathing is praised. / The rules concerning the day of the week, the lunar day, and the lunar mansion apply only outside the Setu, O twice-born. // One should bathe dedicated to the living, but not dedicated to the deceased; / having made an effigy of kuśa grass, one should bathe it with water from the sacred ford.

3.1.m:
Reciting this mantra with joyful senses and mind:
‘You are the kuśa grass, you are pure, formerly held by Viṣṇu;
when you are bathed, he is bathed to whom this knot-binding belongs.’
The ocean is everywhere sacred, always on every full- and new-moon day.
At the bridge, at the confluence of the river and the sea, at Gaṅgāsāgara,
and at Gokarṇa and Puruṣottama, daily bathing is indeed prescribed.
One should never touch the lord of rivers on ordinary days elsewhere.
In the hearing of the ancestors, of all the gods, and of the sages,
Rāma, accompanied by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, made a solemn vow:
‘The men who bathe here at the bridge made by me,
they all, by my grace, shall not return to rebirth.
All sins are destroyed by merely looking upon my bridge.
The majesty of Rāmanātha and the grandeur of my bridge
I am unable to describe even in hundreds of millions of years.’
Having heard this speech of Rāma, the celestial seers and great seers,
delighted, praised those words, saying, ‘Excellent! Excellent!’
In the middle of the bridge, the Four-faced [Brahmā], accompanied by all the gods,
dwells constantly by command of Īśvara for its protection.
For the protection of Rāma's bridge, indeed, under the name of Setumādhava,
Mahāviṣṇu resides there bound by a chain.
And the great seers, the ancestors, the promoters of the dharmaśāstras,
the gods together with gandharvas, kinnaras, and great serpents,
vidyādharas, cāraṇas, yakṣas, and kimpuruṣas,
and all other beings dwell upon it day and night.
That very Rāma's bridge, O best of brahmins, seen, heard of, remembered, touched, or bathed at,
protects one from all sin.
Ablution at the bridge during Ardhodaya is the cause of attaining bliss,
giving liberation, exceedingly meritorious, and destroying the great hell.

3.1.m:
if the new-moon day is joined without the Nāga tithi, under the conjunction (pāta) and Viṣṇu's asterism, it becomes the meritorious Ardhodaya.
At that Ardhodaya, ablution at the bridge is the cause of sāyujya liberation.
A single new-moon day is considered equal to a thousand vyatīpātas.
If it falls on a Sunday, the merit equals ten thousand new-moon days;
if the asterism of Śravaṇa is combined with a Sunday,
it is known to be truly auspicious from their mutual conjunction.
Even each one individually grants immortality through bath, donation, recitation, and worship;
what need be said here when all five are united?
Śravaṇa is best among asterisms; the new moon is best among tithis;
Vyatīpāta among conjunctions; and Sunday among the days of the week.
The conjunction of all four that occurs when the Sun is in Capricorn:
if a person bathes at Rāma's bridge at that time,
he does not enter a mother's womb, but attains sāyujya liberation.
No time equal to Ardhodaya has been or ever will be.
Similarly, the time of Mahodaya is proclaimed as a time of righteousness.
During these meritorious times, giving donations at the bridge is extolled.
Right conduct, austerity, Vedic study, and hearing the Vedānta,
worship of Śiva, Viṣṇu, and others, and the exposition of the meaning of the Purāṇas:
in whatever brahmin these exist, he is said to be a worthy recipient of gifts.
To that worthy recipient, a twice-born, one should give gifts at the bridge.
If a worthy recipient endowed with right conduct cannot be found at the bridge,
having made a resolution and designated a worthy recipient, one should give [the gift] upon returning to one's village.
Therefore, those desiring the fruit [of gifts] must not give to an unworthy recipient.
The excellent Setumāhātmya should be given to the narrator, and to no one else.
Here I shall relate an incomparable ancient story, uttered by Vasiṣṭha
to the great king Dilīpa, who wished to know about worthy recipients of gifts.
Dilīpa said:
To whom should gifts be given, O son of Brahmā, O family priest?
Explain this to me in truth, O great sage, to your disciple.
Vasiṣṭha said:

3.1.m: No time equal to the Ardhodaya has existed, nor will there be. / Kumbhakoṇa, the base of the Setu, Gokarṇa, and likewise Naimiṣa, / Ayodhyā, the Daṇḍaka forest, Virūpākṣa, and Veṅkaṭa, / Śāligrāma, Prayāga, Kāñcī, Dvārāvatī likewise, / Madhurā, Padmanābha, and Kāśī, the dwelling of the Lord of the Universe, / all rivers and oceans, and the mountain [called] Bhāskara are commemorated [as such]. / Tonsure and fasting are proclaimed in these sacred fields; / the person who, out of greed or delusion, goes to his own home without performing [them], / sins go with him indeed right into his house. / There are twenty-four sacred fords on Mount Gandhamādana; / there, at the Lakṣmaṇatīrtha, shaving of the head is taught by the sages. / On the shore of Lakṣmaṇatīrtha, avoiding [cutting the other] hair by the command of Śiva, / having shaved only the head and having given a priestly fee, / having bathed at Lakṣmaṇatīrtha and having beheld Lakṣmaṇaśaṅkara, / a man, freed from all sins, goes to Śaṃkara. / At the Ardhodaya one should always perform the ritual ablution at the Setu in this manner. / There is no sacred ford equal to the Setu, there is no austerity equal to the Setu, / there is no merit equal to the Setu, there is no state equal to the Setu. / The Ardhodaya is regarded as equal to a thousand eclipses; / there is no time equal to the Ardhodaya that releases from the cycle of rebirth. / The ritual ablution that takes place at Rāmasetu during that Ardhodaya— / throughout all the scriptures, no merit can ever equal that. / The merit that is pointed out by seers from immersing oneself in the Bhāgīrathī for sixty thousand years— / that merit, O bulls among sages, / is certainly accomplished from a single ritual ablution at Rāmasetu, / especially during the Ardhodaya, and likewise during the Mahodaya. / The merit that a man gains by a thousand ritual ablutions in the month of Māgha at Prayāga that frees from sin, / when the sun is in Capricorn in Māgha, / from plunging into the Rāmasetu during that Ardhodaya, O brahmins,
