3.1.m: he obtains that merit with a single time; there is no doubt about this. / Whatever fruit belongs to those who have bathed in the sacred fords situated in the three worlds, / having bathed once at the Setu during the Ardhodaya, one becomes a sharer of that merit. / For those destitute of knowledge of Brahman, for the ungrateful, for the wicked, / for other sinners, and likewise for perpetrators of heinous sins, / purification is assured through ritual ablution at the Setu during the Ardhodaya. / For the ungrateful, there is never any expiation at another place; / even for them there is indeed expiation through ritual ablution at the Setu during the Ardhodaya. / Those who, through delusion, do not perform the ritual ablution at the Setu during the Ardhodaya, / sink down into worldly transmigrations as blind men fall downward. / Having bathed at the Setu during the Ardhodaya, having pierced the solar disc, / they will go to the world of Brahmā; no doubt should be entertained on this point. / But when the Ardhodaya has arrived, having bathed at the Setu that bestows complete liberation, / having bathed, having properly meditated on the Lord of the Universe, Rāghava, along with Sītā, / on Rāmeśvara the Great God, on the monkeys headed by Sugrīva, / and on the gods, the seers, and also the groups of ancestral spirits, / he should also make water offerings to all of them for the sake of release from his own poverty. / One should worship the spotless Lord of the Universe named Ardhodaya; / at the time of the Ardhodaya at the Setu, Keśava is pleased by this. / 'O Maker of the Day, homage to you, mass of splendor, Lord of the Universe! / O you born of the Atri lineage, brother of the goddess Lakṣmī! / Accept this guest-offering, O Blessed One, pitcher of nectar, homage to you! / O great yogin of the Vyatīpāta, destroyer of heinous sins, / O thousand-armed one, Soul of All, accept the guest-offering, homage to you! / O supreme lord, sovereign of lunar days, lunar mansions, and weekdays, / O you whose form is the month, accept the guest-offering, homage to you whose form is time!' / Having offered the guest-offering in this manner with separate mantras during the Ardhodaya, a man / should give presents to brahmins according to his wealth. / Fourteen, twelve, eight, seven, six, or five twice-borns,

3.1.m: he should honor according to his ability with food, drinks, and other things, with separate mantras. / Taking a bronze vessel, or a new wooden one, / placing it before the brahmins filled to the brim with milk, / accompanied by fruit, accompanied by jaggery, accompanied by clarified butter, accompanied by betel, accompanied by a priestly fee, / he should give a sacred thread and a cow with her calf, rich in milk. / To the decorated brahmins, he should say this according to his ability: / 'In the Śravaṇa lunar mansion, O Lord of the Universe, in your birth-star, O Keśava, / whatever has been given by me to petitioners, let that be imperishable for me here! / O lord of the lunar mansions, giver of nectar to the gods, / protect me, beloved of Rohiṇī, homage to you who remain as [digits of] light! / O protector of the wretched, Lord of the Universe, master of the arts, compassion-maker, / let my devotion to your pair of lotus feet be unswerving! / Homage to you, O Vyatīpāta, resembling moon, sun, and fire! / Whatever donation and the like has been made, let that be imperishable here for you! / You are the wishing-tree of petitioners, O Vāsudeva, Janārdana! / O Lord of months, seasons, solstices, and time, pacify my sin, O Hari!' / Having thus worshipped the foremost brahmins, he should then perform the ancestral rites: / an ancestral offering with gold, or uncooked food, or cooked food, / and then he should perform the ancestral ceremony for conjunctions; he must not practice deceit regarding wealth. / Afterward he should worship the preceptor with garments, ornaments, and earrings; / he should present an icon to him, and a cow, an umbrella, and shoes. / In this way, O best of twice-borns, one should perform the observance at the Setu during the Ardhodaya; / by that alone he becomes one who has accomplished his duty; there is nothing whatever left to be done. / In another place also, one should perform this observance in this very manner during the Ardhodaya. / The Setu was constructed in the ocean by Rāma on Mount Gandhamādana; / because of proclaiming its name here as 'Setu, Setu', O wise ones, / at the time of ritual ablution, the crores of sins of men / are destroyed at that very moment, and they will go to the highest abode. / Whatever person stays at the Setu for an instant, or for half an instant...

3.1.m: The servants of Yama are unable to come within his sight. / Then, meditating in mind upon Rāma's bridge, Dhanuṣkoṭi, Rāma, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, / Rāmanātha, Hanūmat, the monkeys headed by Sugrīva, / Vibhīṣaṇa, Nārada, Viśvāmitra, the jar-born [Agastya], / Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli, and Kāśyapa, / and similarly other devotees of Rāma, / one is freed from all suffering and goes to the supreme abode. / Whatever sins are destroyed by bathing in Satyakṣetra, Harikṣetra, Kṛṣṇakṣetra, Naimiṣa, / Śālagrāma, Badarī, Hastiśaila, Vṛṣācala, / Śeṣādri, Citrakūṭa, Lakṣmīkṣetra, Kuraṅgaka, / Kāñcī, Kumbhakoṇa, and Mohinīpura, / in sacred Śvetācala belonging to Indra, the great site Padmanābha, / at the site named Phulla, Ghaṭikādri, Sārakṣetra, Haristhala, / in the great sacred field Śrīnivāsa, the great site Bhaktanātha, / in the great sacred field named Aliṅda, and Śukakṣetra belonging to Varuṇa, / in Mathurā, Harikṣetra, Śrīgoṣṭhī, Puruṣottama, / Śrīraṅga, Puṇḍarīkākṣa, and other places of Hari, O best of brahmins— / all those sins are certainly destroyed by bathing at the bridge. / Those men who do not bathe at the bridge built by Raghunātha and frequented by great sages / have no cessation of worldly transmigration. / Or whoever do not speak, do not hear, and do not remember the auspicious five-syllable mantra, ‘Namaḥ Śivāya’, O chiefs of sages, / or do not recite or remember the eight-syllable mantra, ‘Namo Nārāyaṇāya’, / endowed with the praṇava, / or similarly, O best of men, do not recite, hear, or remember / the six-syllable mantra of venerable Rāmacandra— / their sins are destroyed by immersing in Rāma's bridge. / Or those who do not fast on the auspicious day of Hari,

3.1.m: 1. Benediction; arrival of the Purāṇic reciter, the great sage Sūta, into the assembly of the great seers Śaunaka and others dwelling in Naimiṣāraṇya; questioning [him] by Śaunaka and the other great seers after offering hospitality out of a desire to know the glorification of sacred fields and sacred fords; commencement of the description of the glorification of the sacred field of Śrī Rāmeśvara by Sūta; therein at the outset, the narration of the glorification of the pilgrimage to the bridge constructed by Śrī Rāma situated on the southern ocean, the darśana of the bridge, the ritual ablution at Rāmasetu, and the darśana of the Rāmeśvara liṅga -- 1 1
Esoteric aspect of Setu

3.1.s: 2 atha setubandhanavṛttāntaprasaṅgena śrīrāmacandrasya piturājñayā daṇḍakāranyagamanasītā- haraṇasugrīvasakhyasamudratīragamanavibhīṣaṇasamāgamāntarāmāyaṇavṛttāntavarṇanam, atha sarvarākṣasarājye vibhīṣaṇābhiṣecanānantaraṃ samudrataraṇopāyacintayā cakratīrthe sugrīvādibhiḥ saha darbhaśayane sthitvā mantrakaraṇam, tatastrirātraparyantaṃ samudra- taraṇopāyaṃ cintayānena rāmeṇa samudrasyopāsanāpūrvakaṃ pratīkṣaṇam, atha samudrasya svaṃ pratyanāgamanādirūpamanādaraṃ dṛṣṭvā śrīrāmeṇa samudraṃ śoṣayituṃ pratijñāyā kṛtāyāṃ bhayabhītena samudreṇa śrīrāmaṃ prati śaraṇamāgatya śrīrāmasya stutikaraṇam, tatastatstutiprasannena śrīrāmeṇa laṅkāgamanārthaṃ taraṇārthamukte samudreṇa svopari setu- bandhanārthaṃ vijñaptikaraṇam, tataḥ śrīrāmeṇa sarvavānarasāhāyyena viśvakarmasutanala- vānaradvārā samudre setubandhanam darbhaśayanasya setumūlatvavarṇanam, setau sthitānāṃ cakratīrthādicaturviṃśatitīrthānāṃ varṇanam 4 1
3.1.d: 2 अथ सेतुबन्धनवृत्तान्तप्रसङ्गेन श्रीरामचन्द्रस्य पितुराज्ञया दण्डकारन्यगमनसीता- हरणसुग्रीवसख्यसमुद्रतीरगमनविभीषणसमागमान्तरामायणवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, अथ सर्वराक्षसराज्ये विभीषणाभिषेचनानन्तरं समुद्रतरणोपायचिन्तया चक्रतीर्थे सुग्रीवादिभिः सह दर्भशयने स्थित्वा मन्त्रकरणम्, ततस्त्रिरात्रपर्यन्तं समुद्र- तरणोपायं चिन्तयानेन रामेण समुद्रस्योपासनापूर्वकं प्रतीक्षणम्, अथ समुद्रस्य स्वं प्रत्यनागमनादिरूपमनादरं दृष्ट्वा श्रीरामेण समुद्रं शोषयितुं प्रतिज्ञाया कृतायां भयभीतेन समुद्रेण श्रीरामं प्रति शरणमागत्य श्रीरामस्य स्तुतिकरणम्, ततस्तत्स्तुतिप्रसन्नेन श्रीरामेण लङ्कागमनार्थं तरणार्थमुक्ते समुद्रेण स्वोपरि सेतु- बन्धनार्थं विज्ञप्तिकरणम्, ततः श्रीरामेण सर्ववानरसाहाय्येन विश्वकर्मसुतनल- वानरद्वारा समुद्रे सेतुबन्धनम् दर्भशयनस्य सेतुमूलत्ववर्णनम्, सेतौ स्थितानां चक्रतीर्थादिचतुर्विंशतितीर्थानां वर्णनम् 4 1
3.1.m: 2. In the context of the account of building the bridge: narration of the inner Rāmāyaṇa story including the journey of Śrī Rāmacandra to the Daṇḍaka forest by his father's command, the abduction of Sītā, friendship with Sugrīva, going to the ocean shore, and meeting with Vibhīṣaṇa; then, after consecrating Vibhīṣaṇa over the entire realm of the rākṣasas, taking counsel with Sugrīva and others on the bed of darbha grass at Cakratīrtha in contemplation of the means to cross the ocean; then Rāma, contemplating the means to cross the ocean for three nights, waiting while worshipping the ocean; then, seeing the ocean's disrespect by its not coming to him, etc., when Śrī Rāma makes a vow to dry up the ocean, the terrified ocean seeks refuge with Śrī Rāma and recites a hymn of praise to Śrī Rāma; then, pleased with that hymn, when Śrī Rāma tells him it is for crossing in order to reach Laṅkā, the ocean's petition to build a bridge over him; then Śrī Rāma's construction of a bridge across the ocean through the monkey Nala, son of Viśvakarman, with the aid of all the monkeys; description of the bed of darbha grass as the root of the bridge; description of the twenty-four sacred fords situated on the bridge, beginning with Cakratīrtha 4 1

3.1.s: 3 atha setumūlākhyacakratīrthaprasiddhivṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra dharmapuṣkariṇītīre gālavākhya-. maharṣitapastuṣṭena bhagavatā gālavāya varapradānapūrvakaṃ dharmasyārādhanasantoṣitahara- prasādalabdhaharavāhanavṛṣabhatvaprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, athaharibhaktiparāyaṇasya gālava- maharṣeḥ kenacidrākṣasena bhakṣaṇārthaṃ gṛhītasya stutyā bhagavatā preṣitena sudarśanacakreṇa rākṣasasya hananam sū tato nihataṃ rākṣasaṃ dṛṣṭvā gālavena puraḥsthitasya dedīpyamānasya sudarśanacakrasya stutikaraṇam, tataḥ sudarśanacakreṇa gālavamaharṣaye varapradānapūrvakaṃ dharmapuṣkariṇyāṃ sadā sannidhānakaraṇam , tata eva dharmapuṣkariṇyāścakratīrthatvena prasiddhiḥ, dharmatīrthāparaparyāyacakratīrthasya māhātmyavarṇanam...... . 6 2
3.1.d: 3 अथ सेतुमूलाख्यचक्रतीर्थप्रसिद्धिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र धर्मपुष्करिणीतीरे गालवाख्य-. महर्षितपस्तुष्टेन भगवता गालवाय वरप्रदानपूर्वकं धर्मस्याराधनसन्तोषितहर- प्रसादलब्धहरवाहनवृषभत्वप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, अथहरिभक्तिपरायणस्य गालव- महर्षेः केनचिद्राक्षसेन भक्षणार्थं गृहीतस्य स्तुत्या भगवता प्रेषितेन सुदर्शनचक्रेण राक्षसस्य हननम् सू ततो निहतं राक्षसं दृष्ट्वा गालवेन पुरःस्थितस्य देदीप्यमानस्य सुदर्शनचक्रस्य स्तुतिकरणम्, ततः सुदर्शनचक्रेण गालवमहर्षये वरप्रदानपूर्वकं धर्मपुष्करिण्यां सदा सन्निधानकरणम् , तत एव धर्मपुष्करिण्याश्चक्रतीर्थत्वेन प्रसिद्धिः, धर्मतीर्थापरपर्यायचक्रतीर्थस्य माहात्म्यवर्णनम्...... . 6 2
3.1.m: 3. Now begins the account of the fame of Cakratīrtha, also known as the Root of the Setu (Setumūla): There, on the bank of the Dharmapuṣkariṇī, the Lord, pleased by the tapas of the great seer named Gālava, granted a boon to Gālava, and the account of Dharma’s gaining the state of being Hara's vehicle, the bull, obtained through the grace of Hara who was pleased by his worship; then, when the great seer Gālava, who was devoted to the worship of Hari, was seized by a certain rākṣasa in order to devour him, the slaying of the rākṣasa by the Sudarśanacakra sent by the Lord upon his praise; then Gālava, seeing the rākṣasa slain, praised the blazing Sudarśanacakra standing before him; then the Sudarśanacakra granted a boon to the great seer Gālava and established its perpetual presence in the Dharmapuṣkariṇī; therefore the Dharmapuṣkariṇī became famous as Cakratīrtha; the description of the māhātmya of Cakratīrtha, another name for Dharmatīrtha...... 62

3.1.s: 4 gālavamaharṣitrāsadāyakarākṣasavṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra viśvāvasugandharvasutasya durdamākhya- sya salilāśaye vivastrasya vivastrābhiḥ strībhiḥ saha krīḍayā madāndhatāmavekṣya mādhyā- hnikavidhānārthe salilāśayaṃ pratyāgatena vasiṣṭhamaharṣiṇā śāpapradānam, vasiṣṭhaśā- pāddurdamasya rākṣasatvaprāptiḥ, tadbhāryābhiḥ prārthitena vasiṣṭhena durdamasya śāpāntāva- dhikaraṇam, tato durdamasya sudarśanacakrakṛtaśiraśchedānantaraṃ divyadehaprāptiḥ, durdamena sudarśanacakrastutikaraṇam , darbhaśayanamārabhya devīpattanaparyantaṃ cakratīrtha- syāyāmavistāravattve satyapi madhyemadhye vicchinnatākāraṇakathanānusāreṇa śakrakṛta- parvatapakṣacchedanavṛttāntavarṇanam......... .... 8 2
3.1.d: 4 गालवमहर्षित्रासदायकराक्षसवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र विश्वावसुगन्धर्वसुतस्य दुर्दमाख्य- स्य सलिलाशये विवस्त्रस्य विवस्त्राभिः स्त्रीभिः सह क्रीडया मदान्धतामवेक्ष्य माध्या- ह्निकविधानार्थे सलिलाशयं प्रत्यागतेन वसिष्ठमहर्षिणा शापप्रदानम्, वसिष्ठशा- पाद्दुर्दमस्य राक्षसत्वप्राप्तिः, तद्भार्याभिः प्रार्थितेन वसिष्ठेन दुर्दमस्य शापान्ताव- धिकरणम्, ततो दुर्दमस्य सुदर्शनचक्रकृतशिरश्छेदानन्तरं दिव्यदेहप्राप्तिः, दुर्दमेन सुदर्शनचक्रस्तुतिकरणम् , दर्भशयनमारभ्य देवीपत्तनपर्यन्तं चक्रतीर्थ- स्यायामविस्तारवत्त्वे सत्यपि मध्येमध्ये विच्छिन्नताकारणकथनानुसारेण शक्रकृत- पर्वतपक्षच्छेदनवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्......... .... 8 2
3.1.m: 4. The account of the rākṣasa who caused terror to the great seer Gālava: There, the great seer Vasiṣṭha, who had arrived at the reservoir of water to perform the midday rites, seeing the infatuation through lust of Durdama, the son of the gandharva Viśvāvasu, as he sported in the water without clothes together with naked women, uttered a curse; through Vasiṣṭha's curse Durdama attained the condition of a rākṣasa; Vasiṣṭha, implored by his wives, set a limit to the end of Durdama's curse; then, following the decapitation wrought by the Sudarśanacakra, Durdama attained a divine body; Durdama's praise of the Sudarśanacakra; although Cakratīrtha extends continuously from Darbhaśayana up to Devīpattana, the account of the cutting of the wings of the mountains by Śakra in explanation of why it is broken in between......... 82

3.1.s: 5 atha cakratīrthamāhātmyaprasaṃgena vidhūmākhyavasvalaṃbusāpsarovṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra brahma- loke nijasabhāyāṃ sāvitrīsanakaprabhṛtisamastasuramunisiddhavasugandharvaiḥ saha sthitasya brahmaṇaḥ purastādakhilāpsarasāṃ paryāyanṛtyasamāraṃbhe krameṇālaṃbusākhyāyā apsaraso nṛtyamānāyā līlayā vāyunābhyantaravastre samutkṣipte sati spaṣṭorumūlajaghanadarśanena kāmabāṇanipīḍitasya vidhūmanāmakasya vasornirlajjatāṃ nirīkṣya brahmaṇā tasmai manuṣyatvaprāptirūpaśāpapradānam, alaṃbusāyāśca mānuṣītvaprāptirūpaśāpapradānam, vidhūmaprārthanayā brahmaṇā tacchāpāntāvadhikaraṇam, atha bhūtale śatānīkamahī- paterbhāryāyāṃ vidhūmavasoḥ sahasrānīkanāmnā janma, tasya trayāṇāmanucarāṇāṃ ca tanmantrisenānīvayasyānāṃ gṛheṣu janma, alaṃbuṣākhyāyāḥ svarveśyāyā ayodhyā- dhipateḥ kṛtavarmaṇaḥ kanyātvam ,atha śatānīke nṛpe divi daityena saha yuddhe mṛte sati sahasrānīkasya rājyābhiṣekaḥ, anantaraṃ sanaṃdanamahotsave śakranimantraṇavaśāccha-krabhavanaṃ gatena sahasrānīkena śakravacanānnijaśāpāntavṛttāntamājñāya bhuvamāgatya mṛgāvatīpariṇayanam, mṛgāvatīpariṇayottaraṃ kauśāṃbīṃ nagarīṃ prati prasthitasya sahasrānīkasya madhyemārga śakravacanaṃ dhyātvā'nālokitayā tilottamākhyayā'psa- rasā caturdaśasamāparyaṃtaṃ bhāryayā saha te viyogo bhaviṣyatīti śāpapradānam, atha kālena garbhiṇyāṃ mṛgāvatyāṃ daurhṛdaparipūrtyai kausumbhakusumapūrṇavāpyāṃ nimajjane kriyamāṇe suparṇakulasaṃbhavena vikaṭapakṣiṇā haraṇapūrvakamudayācalaśikharopāre naya- nam, tatra jamadagninā śokākulāyā mṛgāvatyāḥ sāntvanapūrvakaṃ svāśrame sthāpanam, atha tatra prasūtāyā mṛgāvatyāḥ putrasya jamadagninodayanetināmakaraṇam, udayanena svamātṛdattakaṃkaṇaṃ pradāya śabaravyādhato mocitena sadyo manuṣyarūpadhṛtā kiṃnarākhya- nāgena saha pātālaṃ prati gatvā dhṛtarāṣṭranāgakanyayā kiṃnaranāgabhaginyā lalitā- khyayā saha vivāhakaraṇam, lalitāyāṃ tasmātputrotpattiḥ, atha lalitāyāḥ śāpato vimuktiḥ, udayanasya lalitāsakāśātputraṃ tāṃbūlīsrajaṃ ghoṣavatīṃ vīṇāṃ ca gṛhītvā svamātaraṃ prati jamadagnyāśrama āgamanam, śabaravyādhasamīpe sthitaṃ nijamudrāṃkita- kaṃkaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasrānīkena śabarātkaṃkaṇaprāptivṛttāṃtaṃ śrutvā mantribhiḥ saha jama dagnyāśramaṃ prati gamanam, jamadagnitaḥ svabhāryā mṛgāvatī svaputramudayanaṃ svapautraṃ ca prāpya svapurīṃ pratyāgamanam , tata udayanākhye svaputre rājyabhāraṃ nyasya svaśāpa- nivṛttaye mṛgāvatīpatnyā vasaṃtakarumaṇvadyaugandharāyaṇākhyairnijamantriputrādibhiśca saha dakṣiṇodadhitaṭasthacakratīrthaṃ gatvā tatra snānamātreṇa tasya śāpanivṛttipūrvaka rūpaprāptivarṇanam, tatasteṣāṃ caturṇāmapi pūrvasvarūpāvāptivarṇanam, cakratīrthamāhātmya- varṇanam..... .......... ... 10 1
3.1.d: 5 अथ चक्रतीर्थमाहात्म्यप्रसंगेन विधूमाख्यवस्वलंबुसाप्सरोवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र ब्रह्म- लोके निजसभायां सावित्रीसनकप्रभृतिसमस्तसुरमुनिसिद्धवसुगन्धर्वैः सह स्थितस्य ब्रह्मणः पुरस्तादखिलाप्सरसां पर्यायनृत्यसमारंभे क्रमेणालंबुसाख्याया अप्सरसो नृत्यमानाया लीलया वायुनाभ्यन्तरवस्त्रे समुत्क्षिप्ते सति स्पष्टोरुमूलजघनदर्शनेन कामबाणनिपीडितस्य विधूमनामकस्य वसोर्निर्लज्जतां निरीक्ष्य ब्रह्मणा तस्मै मनुष्यत्वप्राप्तिरूपशापप्रदानम्, अलंबुसायाश्च मानुषीत्वप्राप्तिरूपशापप्रदानम्, विधूमप्रार्थनया ब्रह्मणा तच्छापान्तावधिकरणम्, अथ भूतले शतानीकमही- पतेर्भार्यायां विधूमवसोः सहस्रानीकनाम्ना जन्म, तस्य त्रयाणामनुचराणां च तन्मन्त्रिसेनानीवयस्यानां गृहेषु जन्म, अलंबुषाख्यायाः स्वर्वेश्याया अयोध्या- धिपतेः कृतवर्मणः कन्यात्वम् ,अथ शतानीके नृपे दिवि दैत्येन सह युद्धे मृते सति सहस्रानीकस्य राज्याभिषेकः, अनन्तरं सनंदनमहोत्सवे शक्रनिमन्त्रणवशाच्छ-क्रभवनं गतेन सहस्रानीकेन शक्रवचनान्निजशापान्तवृत्तान्तमाज्ञाय भुवमागत्य मृगावतीपरिणयनम्, मृगावतीपरिणयोत्तरं कौशांबीं नगरीं प्रति प्रस्थितस्य सहस्रानीकस्य मध्येमार्ग शक्रवचनं ध्यात्वाऽनालोकितया तिलोत्तमाख्ययाऽप्स- रसा चतुर्दशसमापर्यंतं भार्यया सह ते वियोगो भविष्यतीति शापप्रदानम्, अथ कालेन गर्भिण्यां मृगावत्यां दौर्हृदपरिपूर्त्यै कौसुम्भकुसुमपूर्णवाप्यां निमज्जने क्रियमाणे सुपर्णकुलसंभवेन विकटपक्षिणा हरणपूर्वकमुदयाचलशिखरोपारे नय- नम्, तत्र जमदग्निना शोकाकुलाया मृगावत्याः सान्त्वनपूर्वकं स्वाश्रमे स्थापनम्, अथ तत्र प्रसूताया मृगावत्याः पुत्रस्य जमदग्निनोदयनेतिनामकरणम्, उदयनेन स्वमातृदत्तकंकणं प्रदाय शबरव्याधतो मोचितेन सद्यो मनुष्यरूपधृता किंनराख्य- नागेन सह पातालं प्रति गत्वा धृतराष्ट्रनागकन्यया किंनरनागभगिन्या ललिता- ख्यया सह विवाहकरणम्, ललितायां तस्मात्पुत्रोत्पत्तिः, अथ ललितायाः शापतो विमुक्तिः, उदयनस्य ललितासकाशात्पुत्रं तांबूलीस्रजं घोषवतीं वीणां च गृहीत्वा स्वमातरं प्रति जमदग्न्याश्रम आगमनम्, शबरव्याधसमीपे स्थितं निजमुद्रांकित- कंकणं दृष्ट्वा सहस्रानीकेन शबरात्कंकणप्राप्तिवृत्तांतं श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिभिः सह जम दग्न्याश्रमं प्रति गमनम्, जमदग्नितः स्वभार्या मृगावती स्वपुत्रमुदयनं स्वपौत्रं च प्राप्य स्वपुरीं प्रत्यागमनम् , तत उदयनाख्ये स्वपुत्रे राज्यभारं न्यस्य स्वशाप- निवृत्तये मृगावतीपत्न्या वसंतकरुमण्वद्यौगन्धरायणाख्यैर्निजमन्त्रिपुत्रादिभिश्च सह दक्षिणोदधितटस्थचक्रतीर्थं गत्वा तत्र स्नानमात्रेण तस्य शापनिवृत्तिपूर्वक रूपप्राप्तिवर्णनम्, ततस्तेषां चतुर्णामपि पूर्वस्वरूपावाप्तिवर्णनम्, चक्रतीर्थमाहात्म्य- वर्णनम्..... .......... ... 10 1
3.1.m: 5. Now, in connection with the māhātmya of Cakratīrtha, the account of the Vasu named Vidhūma and the apsaras Alaṃbusā: There, in the world of Brahmā, while Brahmā sat in his assembly together with Sāvitrī, Sanaka, and all the gods, munis, siddhas, Vasus, and gandharvas, and all the apsarases began dancing in turn before him, in due course the inner garment of the apsaras named Alaṃbusā as she danced was playfully tossed up by the wind; seeing the shamelessness of the Vasu named Vidhūma, who was tormented by the arrows of Kāma upon clearly seeing her thighs and hips, Brahmā pronounced a curse upon him to take birth as a mortal, and also a curse upon Alaṃbusā to become a human woman; through Vidhūma's plea, Brahmā set a limit for the termination of that curse; then, on the mortal earth, the Vasu Vidhūma was born to the wife of King Śatānīka by the name Sahasrānīka, and his three attendants took birth in the houses of his minister, army commander, and companion; the celestial courtesan named Alaṃbusā became the daughter of Kṛtavarman, the lord of Ayodhyā; then, when King Śatānīka died in heaven in battle with a Daitya, Sahasrānīka's coronation; thereafter, having gone to the abode of Śakra on the occasion of the joyful festival of Sanandana by invitation of Śakra, Sahasrānīka learned the details of the end of his curse from Śakra's words, returned to earth, and married Mṛgāvatī; after the wedding to Mṛgāvatī, as Sahasrānīka was setting out for the city of Kauśāmbī, he was cursed on the way by an apsaras named Tilottamā, whom he did not notice because he was meditating on the words of Śakra, that: 'For fourteen years there shall be separation between you and your wife'; then, in the course of time, when Mṛgāvatī was pregnant and immersed in a reservoir filled with safflower blossoms to satisfy her pregnancy craving, she was seized and carried away by a giant bird born of the family of Suparṇa to the summit of the Udayācala mountain; there Jamadagni consoled the grief-stricken Mṛgāvatī and settled her in his hermitage; then Jamadagni gave the name Udayana to the son born of Mṛgāvatī there; Udayana, having freed a nāga named Kinnara from a Śabara hunter by giving a bracelet given by his mother, which nāga immediately assumed human form, went with him to Pātāla and married the sister of the Kinnara nāga named Lalitā, the daughter of the nāga Dhṛtarāṣṭra; from him a son was born in Lalitā; then Lalitā's release from a curse; Udayana's return to his mother at the hermitage of Jamadagni, taking the son from Lalitā, a garland of betel leaves, and the vīṇā named Ghoṣavatī; Sahasrānīka, seeing his own signet bracelet in the possession of the Śabara hunter and hearing the account of obtaining the bracelet from the Śabara, went with his ministers to the hermitage of Jamadagni; after regaining his wife Mṛgāvatī, his son Udayana, and his grandson from Jamadagni, his return to his city; then, having placed the burden of the kingdom on his son named Udayana, in order to remove his curse he went with his wife Mṛgāvatī and his sons of ministers named Vasantaka, Rumaṇvat, Yaugandharāyaṇa, and others, to Cakratīrtha situated on the shore of the southern ocean; the account of the removal of his curse and regaining of his [divine] form by merely bathing there; then the account of all four of them regaining their original forms; the description of the māhātmya of Cakratīrtha..... 101

3.1.s: 6 atha navapāṣāṇasthānasthadevīpattanavṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra devairhataputrayā dityā nija- putrīṃ prati tapaścaraṇārthamājñākaraṇam, dityājñayā tatputryā mahiṣīrūpaṃ dhṛtvā tapo- vanaṃ gatvā paṃcāgnisādhanādighoratapaḥkaraṇama, tattapaḥkṣubdhena supārśvamuninā tāṃ prati devavijayimahiṣamukhanararūpaputraprāptimāśvāsya tāṃ gṛhītvā ca svasthānaṃ prati gama-nam, atha tasyā ditiputryāḥ sakāśānmahiṣāsurotpattiḥ, mahiṣāsureṇa sarvadaitya-rājyādhipatyaprāptyanaṃtaraṃ devaiḥ saha yuddhaṃ kṛtvā sarvadevānāṃ parājayakaraṇam , atha parājitāndevāngṛhītvā brahmaṇo nārāyaṇaśivasamīpaṃ prati gamanam, brahmaniveditamahiṣāsuropadrava vṛttāntamāśrutya kuddhayo rameśvaramaheśvarayormukhataḥ sumahatte-jaso niṣkramaṇam, tadanu sarvadevaśarīrebhyastejaso niṣkramaṇama , teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ tejasāmekatra samudāyena paramabhāsvarasarvāṅgasundaradurgānāmakanārīsamutpattiḥ, tataḥ sarvadevaistasyai durgādevyai nijāyudhebhya utpāditānāmāyudhānāṃ pradānam , sarvadevaiḥ stutayā devyā siṃhamāruhya mahiṣāsuravadhārthaṃ subhairavāṭṭahāsakaraṇam, atha mahiṣā-surasainyaiḥ saha devānāmatibhayaṃkarayuddham, tatra yuddhe devyā mahiṣāsurasainyavadhakaraṇa-varṇanam . 13 2
3.1.d: 6 अथ नवपाषाणस्थानस्थदेवीपत्तनवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र देवैर्हतपुत्रया दित्या निज- पुत्रीं प्रति तपश्चरणार्थमाज्ञाकरणम्, दित्याज्ञया तत्पुत्र्या महिषीरूपं धृत्वा तपो- वनं गत्वा पंचाग्निसाधनादिघोरतपःकरणम, तत्तपःक्षुब्धेन सुपार्श्वमुनिना तां प्रति देवविजयिमहिषमुखनररूपपुत्रप्राप्तिमाश्वास्य तां गृहीत्वा च स्वस्थानं प्रति गम-नम्, अथ तस्या दितिपुत्र्याः सकाशान्महिषासुरोत्पत्तिः, महिषासुरेण सर्वदैत्य-राज्याधिपत्यप्राप्त्यनंतरं देवैः सह युद्धं कृत्वा सर्वदेवानां पराजयकरणम् , अथ पराजितान्देवान्गृहीत्वा ब्रह्मणो नारायणशिवसमीपं प्रति गमनम्, ब्रह्मनिवेदितमहिषासुरोपद्रव वृत्तान्तमाश्रुत्य कुद्धयो रमेश्वरमहेश्वरयोर्मुखतः सुमहत्ते-जसो निष्क्रमणम्, तदनु सर्वदेवशरीरेभ्यस्तेजसो निष्क्रमणम , तेषां सर्वेषां तेजसामेकत्र समुदायेन परमभास्वरसर्वाङ्गसुन्दरदुर्गानामकनारीसमुत्पत्तिः, ततः सर्वदेवैस्तस्यै दुर्गादेव्यै निजायुधेभ्य उत्पादितानामायुधानां प्रदानम् , सर्वदेवैः स्तुतया देव्या सिंहमारुह्य महिषासुरवधार्थं सुभैरवाट्टहासकरणम्, अथ महिषा-सुरसैन्यैः सह देवानामतिभयंकरयुद्धम्, तत्र युद्धे देव्या महिषासुरसैन्यवधकरण-वर्णनम् . 13 2
3.1.m: 6. Now, the description of the account of Devīpattana situated at the place of the Nine Stones (Navapāṣāṇa): therein, the instruction given by Diti, whose sons had been slain by the gods, to her own daughter to perform austerities; the performing of terrible austerities such as practicing the five fires by her daughter, who assumed the form of a buffalo cow on Diti's order and went to a penance grove; the sage Supārśva, agitated by those austerities, reassuring her that she would obtain a son in the form of a man with a buffalo's head who would conquer the gods, taking her and returning to his own hermitage; then the birth of Mahiṣāsura from that daughter of Diti; after obtaining dominion over the entire Daitya kingdom, Mahiṣāsura waging war against the gods and defeating all the gods; then Brahmā taking the defeated gods and going to Nārāyaṇa and Śiva; upon hearing from Brahmā the account of Mahiṣāsura's harassment, the emergence of an immense splendour from the mouths of the enraged Rameśvara and Maheśvara; then the emergence of splendour from the bodies of all the gods; from the coming together of all those splendours into one mass, the manifestation of a woman named Durgā, exquisitely radiant and beautiful in all her limbs; then all the gods bestowing weapons created from their own weapons upon that Goddess Durgā; the Goddess, praised by all the gods, mounting a lion and uttering a terrible, loud roar of laughter for the purpose of slaying Mahiṣāsura; then the terribly fierce battle of the gods with the armies of Mahiṣāsura; and the description of the Goddess slaying Mahiṣāsura's army in that battle. 13 2

3.1.s: 7 atha devyā mahiṣāsuraprahitacaṇḍakopākhyāsurahananānantaraṃ yuddhārthaṃ svayamupasthitena mahiṣāsureṇa saha tumulayuddhakaraṇama, tato devyā mahiṣāsuravadhakaraṇam, mahiṣāsura-vadhena saṃtuṣṭairdevairdevyāḥ stutikaraṇam, tato deveṣu svasvādhikārasthāneṣu gateṣu satsu jaganmātrā devyā dakṣiṇodadhitīre dharmapuṣkariṇītīrthadevīpattanayornirmāṇapūrvakaṃ varapradānam , śrīrāmacandreṇa navagrahasvarūpanavapāṣāṇasthāpanapūrvakaṃ naladvārā setu-nirmāpaṇam, setvārambhasīmāsthānavarṇanam, setunāthaharimāhātmyam , cakratīrthapra-śaṃsā, darbhaśayanasthānamārabhya setuyātrārambhakathanam...... .... 15 1
3.1.d: 7 अथ देव्या महिषासुरप्रहितचण्डकोपाख्यासुरहननानन्तरं युद्धार्थं स्वयमुपस्थितेन महिषासुरेण सह तुमुलयुद्धकरणम, ततो देव्या महिषासुरवधकरणम्, महिषासुर-वधेन संतुष्टैर्देवैर्देव्याः स्तुतिकरणम्, ततो देवेषु स्वस्वाधिकारस्थानेषु गतेषु सत्सु जगन्मात्रा देव्या दक्षिणोदधितीरे धर्मपुष्करिणीतीर्थदेवीपत्तनयोर्निर्माणपूर्वकं वरप्रदानम् , श्रीरामचन्द्रेण नवग्रहस्वरूपनवपाषाणस्थापनपूर्वकं नलद्वारा सेतु-निर्मापणम्, सेत्वारम्भसीमास्थानवर्णनम्, सेतुनाथहरिमाहात्म्यम् , चक्रतीर्थप्र-शंसा, दर्भशयनस्थानमारभ्य सेतुयात्रारम्भकथनम्...... .... 15 1
3.1.m: 7. Now, after the Goddess slays the asura named Caṇḍakopa sent by Mahiṣāsura, a tumultuous battle fought with Mahiṣāsura himself, who arrived for combat; then the slaying of Mahiṣāsura by the Goddess; the gods, pleased by the slaying of Mahiṣāsura, praising the Goddess; then, when the gods returned to their respective stations of authority, the Goddess, Mother of the Universe, creating the Dharmapuṣkariṇī tīrtha and Devīpattana on the shore of the southern ocean and granting boons; the glorious Rāmacandra having the bridge constructed by Nala after installing the nine stones embodying the nine planets; the description of the boundary location where the bridge begins; the māhātmya of Hari, Lord of the Bridge; praise of Cakratīrtha; and the statement of the beginning of the pilgrimage to the bridge starting from the place of Darbhaśayana. 15 1

3.1.s: 8 atha vetālavaradatīrthavṛttāntavarṇanam , tatra gālavamaharṣikanyāyāḥ kāntimatīnāmnyāḥ sudarśanākhyena vidyādharakumāreṇa madanavihvalatayā keśeṣu grahaṇam, gālavena suda-rśanākhyavidyādharāya manuṣyatvaprāptipūrvakavetālatvaprāptiśāpapradānama, tadanumodaka-sya tatkaniṣṭhabandhoḥ sukarṇakākhyasya ca kevalamanuṣyatvaprāptirūpaśāpapradānam, tata-stayoḥ sudarśanasukarṇakayoryamunātīranivāsigovindasvāmino gṛhe vijayadattāśo-kadattanāmakatanayatvaprāptiḥ, atha svadeśe durbhikṣavaśādvārāṇasīṃ prati gatena goviṃ- dasvāminā kapālamālābharaṇākhyayatimukhādvijayadattanāmakaputrabhaviṣyadviyogaśra- vaṇam, vijayadattasyākasmātkapālasphoṭanāmakavetālatvaprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam 16 2
3.1.d: 8 अथ वेतालवरदतीर्थवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् , तत्र गालवमहर्षिकन्यायाः कान्तिमतीनाम्न्याः सुदर्शनाख्येन विद्याधरकुमारेण मदनविह्वलतया केशेषु ग्रहणम्, गालवेन सुद-र्शनाख्यविद्याधराय मनुष्यत्वप्राप्तिपूर्वकवेतालत्वप्राप्तिशापप्रदानम, तदनुमोदक-स्य तत्कनिष्ठबन्धोः सुकर्णकाख्यस्य च केवलमनुष्यत्वप्राप्तिरूपशापप्रदानम्, तत-स्तयोः सुदर्शनसुकर्णकयोर्यमुनातीरनिवासिगोविन्दस्वामिनो गृहे विजयदत्ताशो-कदत्तनामकतनयत्वप्राप्तिः, अथ स्वदेशे दुर्भिक्षवशाद्वाराणसीं प्रति गतेन गोविं- दस्वामिना कपालमालाभरणाख्ययतिमुखाद्विजयदत्तनामकपुत्रभविष्यद्वियोगश्र- वणम्, विजयदत्तस्याकस्मात्कपालस्फोटनामकवेतालत्वप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् 16 2
3.1.m: 8. Now, the description of the account of Vetālavarada-tīrtha: therein, the Vidyādhara youth named Sudarśana, overcome with passion, seizing by the hair the daughter of the great seer Gālava, named Kāntimatī; Gālava uttering a curse upon the Vidyādhara named Sudarśana that he would become a human and then a vetāla; and his uttering a curse merely of human birth upon his younger brother named Sukarṇaka, who approved of it; then the birth of those two, Sudarśana and Sukarṇaka, as sons named Vijayadatta and Aśokadatta in the house of Govindasvāmin, who lived on the banks of the Yamunā; then Govindasvāmin, having gone to Vārāṇasī due to a famine in his own land, hearing from the mouth of an ascetic named Kapālamālābharaṇa of his future separation from his son named Vijayadatta; and the description of the account of Vijayadatta suddenly becoming a vetāla named Kapālasphoṭa. 16 2

3.1.s: 9 atha putraśokavyākulasya goviṃdasvāminaḥ svagṛhaṃ pratyāgatya bhāryayā saha vilāpakara- ṇam, aśokadattanāmnā goviṃdasvāmidvitīyaputreṇa pratāpamukuṭākhyanarapateranujñayā dākṣiṇātyamahāmallasya nipātanapūrvakaṃ hananam, atha pratāpamukuṭanṛpaterāśrayeṇā- śokadattasya sthitiḥ, atha kadācidvijane'raṇye nṛpeṇa saha paribhramatā dhairyavatā'śo- kadattena smaśānaṃ gatvā māyikāyā vidyutkeśākhyāyā rākṣasyāḥ pādatalaṃ nigṛhyaikaṃ ratnanūpuraṃ gṛhītvā rājasamīpamāgatya rājñe ratnanūpurasamarpaṇam , tatastaddhairyasantuṣṭena pratāpamukuṭākhyena rājñā'śokadattāya vaivāhikena vidhinā madanalekhākhyanijasutāpradānam, tato nṛpecchāṃ vijñāya dvitīyanūpuraprāptaye'śoka dattasya mahāmāṃsaṃ gṛhītvā smaśāne gamanam, tatra mantrairbhūtānāmāmantraṇe kriya- māṇe rakṣaḥkanyāsamāvṛtāyā viyutkeśākhyarākṣasyāstatsamīpaṃ prati māṃsabhakṣaṇa- lālasayā''gamanam, tatastaddhairyasantuṣṭayā vidyutkeśākhyayā rākṣasyā'śokadattā- khyāya dvijasūnave svapādasthitadvitīyaratnanūpurapradānapūrvakaṃ vidyutprabhākhyanija- kanyāpradānam, tasmā eva ca jāmātre kanyāpradānaprābhṛtatvarūpeṇa suvarṇakamala- pradānam, tatsarvaṃ guhītvā'śokadattasya pratāpamukuṭākhyanṛpasamīpa āgamanam, pratāpamukuṭenāśokadattasya praśaṃsākaraṇam, atha kadācidekānte vidyutprabhāṃ prati tanmātṛdattasuvarṇapaṅkajotpattisthale pṛṣṭe tayā kapālavisphoṭakanāmakavetālabhūpati- divyasarovṛttāntavarṇanam ,atha tayā vidyatprabhayāsahāśokadattasyakapālavisphoṭaka- vetālarakṣitakāñcanakamalasaraḥ prati gamanam, tatra vighnakāriṇo vetālānhatvā kapālavisphoṭakākhyaṃ vetālaṃ hantukāmenāśokadattena vimānārūḍhavijñaptikautukanā- makavidyādharapatidarśanam, taddarśanamātreṇāśokadattasya gālavamaharṣidattamanuṣyatvarūpa-śāpānmuktipūrvakaṃsukarṇākhyasvasvarūpaprāptiḥ,atho vijñaptakautukavidyādharapativacanena vetālatvaṃ prāptasya nijabhrāturuddhārārthaṃ tena saha 3.1.d: 9 अथ पुत्रशोकव्याकुलस्य गोविंदस्वामिनः स्वगृहं प्रत्यागत्य भार्यया सह विलापकर- णम्, अशोकदत्तनाम्ना गोविंदस्वामिद्वितीयपुत्रेण प्रतापमुकुटाख्यनरपतेरनुज्ञया दाक्षिणात्यमहामल्लस्य निपातनपूर्वकं हननम्, अथ प्रतापमुकुटनृपतेराश्रयेणा- शोकदत्तस्य स्थितिः, अथ कदाचिद्विजनेऽरण्ये नृपेण सह परिभ्रमता धैर्यवताऽशो- कदत्तेन स्मशानं गत्वा मायिकाया विद्युत्केशाख्याया राक्षस्याः पादतलं निगृह्यैकं रत्ननूपुरं गृहीत्वा राजसमीपमागत्य राज्ञे रत्ननूपुरसमर्पणम् , ततस्तद्धैर्यसन्तुष्टेन प्रतापमुकुटाख्येन राज्ञाऽशोकदत्ताय वैवाहिकेन विधिना मदनलेखाख्यनिजसुताप्रदानम्, ततो नृपेच्छां विज्ञाय द्वितीयनूपुरप्राप्तयेऽशोक दत्तस्य महामांसं गृहीत्वा स्मशाने गमनम्, तत्र मन्त्रैर्भूतानामामन्त्रणे क्रिय- माणे रक्षःकन्यासमावृताया वियुत्केशाख्यराक्षस्यास्तत्समीपं प्रति मांसभक्षण- लालसया'ऽगमनम्, ततस्तद्धैर्यसन्तुष्टया विद्युत्केशाख्यया राक्षस्याऽशोकदत्ता- ख्याय द्विजसूनवे स्वपादस्थितद्वितीयरत्ननूपुरप्रदानपूर्वकं विद्युत्प्रभाख्यनिज- कन्याप्रदानम्, तस्मा एव च जामात्रे कन्याप्रदानप्राभृतत्वरूपेण सुवर्णकमल- प्रदानम्, तत्सर्वं गुहीत्वाऽशोकदत्तस्य प्रतापमुकुटाख्यनृपसमीप आगमनम्, प्रतापमुकुटेनाशोकदत्तस्य प्रशंसाकरणम्, अथ कदाचिदेकान्ते विद्युत्प्रभां प्रति तन्मातृदत्तसुवर्णपङ्कजोत्पत्तिस्थले पृष्टे तया कपालविस्फोटकनामकवेतालभूपति- दिव्यसरोवृत्तान्तवर्णनम् ,अथ तया विद्यत्प्रभयासहाशोकदत्तस्यकपालविस्फोटक- वेतालरक्षितकाञ्चनकमलसरः प्रति गमनम्, तत्र विघ्नकारिणो वेतालान्हत्वा कपालविस्फोटकाख्यं वेतालं हन्तुकामेनाशोकदत्तेन विमानारूढविज्ञप्तिकौतुकना- मकविद्याधरपतिदर्शनम्, तद्दर्शनमात्रेणाशोकदत्तस्य गालवमहर्षिदत्तमनुष्यत्वरूप-शापान्मुक्तिपूर्वकंसुकर्णाख्यस्वस्वरूपप्राप्तिः,अथो विज्ञप्तकौतुकविद्याधरपतिवचनेन वेतालत्वं प्राप्तस्य निजभ्रातुरुद्धारार्थं तेन सह दक्षिणोदधितीरस्थितचक्रतीर्थं गत्वा स्नानकरणम्, तत्तीर्थजलकणस्पर्शमात्रेण वेतालस्यवेतालत्वनिवृत्तिपूर्वकं पुनर्विज-यदत्ताख्यद्विजपुत्रत्वप्राप्तिः, तेन विजयदत्तेन पुनः संकल्पपूर्वकं स्नाने कृते सति ततस्तस्य मनुष्यत्वरूपशापनिवृत्तिपूर्वकं सुदर्शनाख्यविद्याधरत्वप्राप्तिवर्णनम्, वेतालत्वमोचकत्वेन तत्तीर्थस्य वेतालवरदनाम्ना प्रख्यातिवर्णनम् ..... 18 1
3.1.m: 9. Now, Govindasvāmin, distressed by grief for his son, returns to his house and laments with his wife; with the permission of King Pratāpamukuṭa, Govindasvāmin's second son named Aśokadatta throws down and slays a great champion of the Deccan; then Aśokadatta resides under the patronage of King Pratāpamukuṭa; then once, wandering in a solitary forest with the king, the resolute Aśokadatta goes to a cremation ground, seizes the sole of the foot of the illusory rākṣasī named Vidyutkeśā, takes one jeweled anklet, comes into the presence of the king, and offers the jeweled anklet to the king; then King Pratāpamukuṭa, pleased by that courage, bestows his own daughter named Madanalekhā upon Aśokadatta according to the marriage rite; then, knowing the king's desire, Aśokadatta takes human flesh and goes to the cremation ground to obtain the second anklet; there, while the spirits are being summoned with mantras, the rākṣasī named Vidyutkeśā, surrounded by rākṣasa maidens, approaches him eager to eat flesh; then the rākṣasī named Vidyutkeśā, pleased by his courage, gives the second jeweled anklet from her foot and also gives her own daughter named Vidyutprabhā to the brahmin's son named Aśokadatta; and to him, the son-in-law, she gives a golden lotus as a bridal gift; taking all that, Aśokadatta returns to King Pratāpamukuṭa; Pratāpamukuṭa praises Aśokadatta; then once in private, when Vidyutprabhā is asked about the place of origin of the golden lotus given by her mother, she narrates the account of the divine lake of the vetāla king named Kapālavisphoṭaka; then Aśokadatta goes with that Vidyutprabhā to the golden-lotus lake guarded by the vetāla Kapālavisphoṭaka; there, having slain the obstructive vetālas, Aśokadatta, wishing to slay the vetāla named Kapālavisphoṭaka, beholds the lord of the vidyādharas named Vijñaptikautuka mounted on an aerial chariot; upon merely beholding him, Aśokadatta is freed from the curse of human birth given by the great sage Gālava and attains his own true form named Sukarṇa; then, by the word of the vidyādhara lord Vijñaptikautuka, for the purpose of redeeming his own brother who had been turned into a vetāla, he goes with him to Cakratīrtha on the shore of the southern ocean and takes a ritual bath; upon merely touching a drop of water of that sacred ford, the vetāla's state of being a vetāla ceases and he regains the state of being the brahmin's son named Vijayadatta; when that Vijayadatta performs a ritual bath again with solemn resolve, he is freed from the curse of human birth and attains the state of the vidyādhara named Sudarśana; and the proclamation of that sacred ford under the name Vetālavarada, because of its freeing [one] from the state of a vetāla, is related. 18 1

10 atha dakṣiṇodadhisthagandhamādanaparvatamāhātsyavarṇanam, gandhamādanaparvatasthapāpavinā- . śanatīrthamāhātmyam, tatra dṛḍhamatyākhyaśūdravṛttāntavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena śūdradharma-varṇanam, yāgadīkṣānarhasya dṛḍhamatyākhyaśūdrasya devāyatanādidharmakṛtyakaraṇapūrvakaṃ tapaḥ kartuṃ munivṛttyā sthitasya sumatyākhyavipreṇa vaidikakarmopadeśakaraṇam, tenāyā-jyayājanadoṣeṇa sumatyākhyaviprasya narakādiprāptipūrvakavividhagardabhādiyoniprāpti-rūpadurgativarṇanam, atha katipayajanmānantaratasya brāhmaṇajanmaprāptau brahmarākṣasagraha-gṛhītatayā vaidikakarmaparibhraṣṭatvam , atha tatpitrā taṃ gṛhītvāgastyaṃ prati śaraṇagamanam
tato'gastyopadeśena dakṣiṇodadhitīrasthapāpavināśākhyatīrthe tatpitrā nītasya tasya saṃkalpapūrvakasnānamātreṇa brahmarākṣasagrahamuktiḥ, sakalabhogāvāptipūrvakamokṣāvāptiśca, tadupadiṣṭavaidikakarmācaraṇatatparasya dṛḍhamatyākhyaśūdrasya narakaprāptipūrvakānekatirya-gyonijanmaprāptiḥ, tataḥ krameṇa gṛdhrajanmaprāptau dakṣiṇodadhisthagandhamādanaparvatavarti-pāpavināśanākhyatīrthajalaprāśanātsvargalokāvāptiḥ, pāpavināśanatīrthaprabhāvavarṇanam 20 1
3.1.d:
10 अथ दक्षिणोदधिस्थगन्धमादनपर्वतमाहात्स्यवर्णनम्, गन्धमादनपर्वतस्थपापविना- . शनतीर्थमाहात्म्यम्, तत्र दृढमत्याख्यशूद्रवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन शूद्रधर्म-वर्णनम्, यागदीक्षानर्हस्य दृढमत्याख्यशूद्रस्य देवायतनादिधर्मकृत्यकरणपूर्वकं तपः कर्तुं मुनिवृत्त्या स्थितस्य सुमत्याख्यविप्रेण वैदिककर्मोपदेशकरणम्, तेनाया-ज्ययाजनदोषेण सुमत्याख्यविप्रस्य नरकादिप्राप्तिपूर्वकविविधगर्दभादियोनिप्राप्ति-रूपदुर्गतिवर्णनम्, अथ कतिपयजन्मानन्तरतस्य ब्राह्मणजन्मप्राप्तौ ब्रह्मराक्षसग्रह-गृहीततया वैदिककर्मपरिभ्रष्टत्वम् , अथ तत्पित्रा तं गृहीत्वागस्त्यं प्रति शरणगमनम्
ततोऽगस्त्योपदेशेन दक्षिणोदधितीरस्थपापविनाशाख्यतीर्थे तत्पित्रा नीतस्य तस्य संकल्पपूर्वकस्नानमात्रेण ब्रह्मराक्षसग्रहमुक्तिः, सकलभोगावाप्तिपूर्वकमोक्षावाप्तिश्च, तदुपदिष्टवैदिककर्माचरणतत्परस्य दृढमत्याख्यशूद्रस्य नरकप्राप्तिपूर्वकानेकतिर्य-ग्योनिजन्मप्राप्तिः, ततः क्रमेण गृध्रजन्मप्राप्तौ दक्षिणोदधिस्थगन्धमादनपर्वतवर्ति-पापविनाशनाख्यतीर्थजलप्राशनात्स्वर्गलोकावाप्तिः, पापविनाशनतीर्थप्रभाववर्णनम् 20 1
3.1.m: 10. Now, the glorification of Mount Gandhamādana situated on the southern ocean; the māhātmya of Pāpavināśanatīrtha situated on Mount Gandhamādana; therein, the account of a śūdra named Dṛḍhamati is related; in that connection, the duties of a śūdra are described; to the śūdra named Dṛḍhamati, who was ineligible for Vedic sacrifice initiation but was performing meritorious acts such as [building] temples and living by the lifestyle of a sage in order to practice austerity, a brahmin named Sumati gives instruction in Vedic rituals; through the sin of performing sacrifices for one unfit to sacrifice, that brahmin named Sumati undergoes downfall, going to hells and obtaining various wombs such as that of an ass; then after some births, when he obtains birth as a brahmin, he falls away from Vedic rites because of being possessed by a brahmarākṣasa; then his father takes him and seeks refuge with Agastya; then, upon Agastya's instruction, he is led by his father to the sacred ford named Pāpavināśana situated on the shore of the southern ocean, and upon merely taking a ritual bath with solemn resolve, he is freed from possession by the brahmarākṣasa, experiences all enjoyments, and attains liberation; and the śūdra named Dṛḍhamati, who was intent on performing the Vedic rites taught to him, goes to hell and takes birth in many animal wombs; then, in due course obtaining birth as a vulture, he attains the heavenly world from drinking the water of the sacred ford named Pāpavināśana situated on Mount Gandhamādana on the southern ocean; the power of Pāpavināśanatīrtha is described. 20 1

3.1.s: 11 atha sītāsarastīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam ,tatprasaṃgena puraṃdarabrahmahatyāvimukti vṛttānta varṇanam, tatra sasainyasya kapālābharaṇākhyarākṣasasya śakrādidevaiḥ saha yuddham, tasminyuddhe śakreṇa kapālābharaṇarākṣasavadhakaraṇam , tadvadhajanitayā brahmahatyayā śakrasyopadrava-ṇam , kapālābharaṇākhyarākṣasasyabrāhmaṇatvakāraṇavarṇanaprasaṃgena trivakrarākṣasabhāryāyāḥ suśīlānāmnyāḥ patyājñayā śucināmakabrāhmaṇasakāśātputrotpādanātkapālābharaṇasya brāhmaṇavīryotpannatvavṛttāntaḥ, atha brahmahatyayopadrutasya śakrasya brahmopadeśena dakṣiṇodadhisthagandhamādanaparvatavartisītākuṇḍe snānena yajñaiḥ sadāśivasaṃtoṣaṇena ca brahmahatyāto vimuktivarṇanam , sītāsaromāhātmyapraśaṃsāvarṇanam 22 1
3.1.d: 11 अथ सीतासरस्तीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् ,तत्प्रसंगेन पुरंदरब्रह्महत्याविमुक्ति वृत्तान्त वर्णनम्, तत्र ससैन्यस्य कपालाभरणाख्यराक्षसस्य शक्रादिदेवैः सह युद्धम्, तस्मिन्युद्धे शक्रेण कपालाभरणराक्षसवधकरणम् , तद्वधजनितया ब्रह्महत्यया शक्रस्योपद्रव-णम् , कपालाभरणाख्यराक्षसस्यब्राह्मणत्वकारणवर्णनप्रसंगेन त्रिवक्रराक्षसभार्यायाः सुशीलानाम्न्याः पत्याज्ञया शुचिनामकब्राह्मणसकाशात्पुत्रोत्पादनात्कपालाभरणस्य ब्राह्मणवीर्योत्पन्नत्ववृत्तान्तः, अथ ब्रह्महत्ययोपद्रुतस्य शक्रस्य ब्रह्मोपदेशेन दक्षिणोदधिस्थगन्धमादनपर्वतवर्तिसीताकुण्डे स्नानेन यज्ञैः सदाशिवसंतोषणेन च ब्रह्महत्यातो विमुक्तिवर्णनम् , सीतासरोमाहात्म्यप्रशंसावर्णनम् 22 1
3.1.m: 11. Now, the description of the māhātmya of the Sītāsaras sacred ford; in that connection, the account of Puraṃdara's release from the sin of killing a brahmin is described; therein, the battle of the rākṣasa named Kapālābharaṇa with his army against the gods headed by Śakra; in that battle, Śakra slays the rākṣasa Kapālābharaṇa; Śakra is tormented by the sin of killing a brahmin arising from slaying him; in the context of describing the reason for the brahminhood of the rākṣasa named Kapālābharaṇa, the account of Kapālābharaṇa being generated from a brahmin's semen is told, because the wife of the rākṣasa Trivakra, named Suśīlā, by her husband's order, produced a son from a brahmin named Śuci; then Śakra, afflicted by the sin of killing a brahmin, upon the instruction of Brahmā, is freed from the sin of killing a brahmin by bathing in Sītākuṇḍa situated on Mount Gandhamādana on the southern ocean, and by pleasing Sadāśiva with sacrifices; the praise of the māhātmya of Sītāsaras is described. 22 1

3.1.s: 12 atha maṅgalākhyatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam tatprasaṃgena manojavākhyarājavṛttāntavarṇanam, ahaṃkāravato manojavanṛpasya brāhmaṇebhyaḥ karagrahaṇajanyapāpena golabhākhyena taccha-trubhūpena rājyaharaṇapūrvakaṃ rājyānnirvāsanam , atha patnīputrābhyāṃ saha manojavasya vane gamanam , ttra putrasya kṣutparītatāṃ vilokya manojavasya duḥkhenātipaścāttāpaka-raṇapūrvakaṃ mūrchayā patanam, tatpatnyāḥ sumitrākhyāyā vilāpakaraṇam, putrasyāpi rodanam , atha tasminnavasare tatra teṣāṃ samīpe parāśaramaharṣerāgamanam, parāśa-reṇa rājopari maṃtrapūtajalasecanena tasya mūrchāpanayanam , tato rājñā vijñāpitena parāśaramuninā rājānaṃ prati śrīrāmasetusthamaṃgalākhyatīrthayātropāyakathanapūrvakamekā- kṣararāmamaṃtropadeśakaraṇam, munyājñayā bhāryāputrābhyāṃ saha maṃgalatīrthaṃ gatvā catvā-riṃśaddinaparyaṃrtaṃ maṃtropāsanānuṣṭhānaṃ kṛtavato manojavanṛpasya purato maṃgalākhyatī-rthāddhanurniṣaṅgakhaṅgacarmagadāmusalaśaṅkhavājiyuktasasārathisapatākarathakāṃcanamayakava- cādisarvarājālaṃkārādivastuprādurbhāvaḥ, tato manojavena parāśaramunaye teṣāṃ sarva- vastūnāṃ nivedanam, atha parāśareṇa muninā manojavabhūpasya mantrābhiṣekakaraṇam, brahmāstrādyastravidyāpradānapūrvakāśīḥpradānaṃ ca, atha manojavanṛpeṇa svapuraṃ pratyāga- tya brahmāstreṇa golabhanṛpaṃ vināśya nijarājyaṃ prāpya dharmeṇa vartanam, aṃte maṅga- latīrthamāsādya tanutyāgānantaraṃ manojavabhūpasya śivalokāvāptivarṇanam... 23 2
3.1.d: 12 अथ मङ्गलाख्यतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् तत्प्रसंगेन मनोजवाख्यराजवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, अहंकारवतो मनोजवनृपस्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यः करग्रहणजन्यपापेन गोलभाख्येन तच्छ-त्रुभूपेन राज्यहरणपूर्वकं राज्यान्निर्वासनम् , अथ पत्नीपुत्राभ्यां सह मनोजवस्य वने गमनम् , त्त्र पुत्रस्य क्षुत्परीततां विलोक्य मनोजवस्य दुःखेनातिपश्चात्तापक-रणपूर्वकं मूर्छया पतनम्, तत्पत्न्याः सुमित्राख्याया विलापकरणम्, पुत्रस्यापि रोदनम् , अथ तस्मिन्नवसरे तत्र तेषां समीपे पराशरमहर्षेरागमनम्, पराश-रेण राजोपरि मंत्रपूतजलसेचनेन तस्य मूर्छापनयनम् , ततो राज्ञा विज्ञापितेन पराशरमुनिना राजानं प्रति श्रीरामसेतुस्थमंगलाख्यतीर्थयात्रोपायकथनपूर्वकमेका- क्षरराममंत्रोपदेशकरणम्, मुन्याज्ञया भार्यापुत्राभ्यां सह मंगलतीर्थं गत्वा चत्वा-रिंशद्दिनपर्यंर्तं मंत्रोपासनानुष्ठानं कृतवतो मनोजवनृपस्य पुरतो मंगलाख्यती-र्थाद्धनुर्निषङ्गखङ्गचर्मगदामुसलशङ्खवाजियुक्तससारथिसपताकरथकांचनमयकव- चादिसर्वराजालंकारादिवस्तुप्रादुर्भावः, ततो मनोजवेन पराशरमुनये तेषां सर्व- वस्तूनां निवेदनम्, अथ पराशरेण मुनिना मनोजवभूपस्य मन्त्राभिषेककरणम्, ब्रह्मास्त्राद्यस्त्रविद्याप्रदानपूर्वकाशीःप्रदानं च, अथ मनोजवनृपेण स्वपुरं प्रत्याग- त्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण गोलभनृपं विनाश्य निजराज्यं प्राप्य धर्मेण वर्तनम्, अंते मङ्ग- लतीर्थमासाद्य तनुत्यागानन्तरं मनोजवभूपस्य शिवलोकावाप्तिवर्णनम्... 23 2
3.1.m: 12. Now, description of the māhātmya of the sacred ford named Maṅgala. In that connection, account of the king named Manojava: King Manojava's arrogance, and, through the sin arising from levying taxes upon brahmins, the seizure of his kingdom by his enemy-king named Golabha, followed by his banishment from the kingdom; then, Manojava's going to the forest together with his wife and son; there, seeing his son overcome with hunger, Manojava's falling in a faint after extreme repentance in sorrow; the lamentation of his wife named Sumitrā; the weeping also of the son; then, at that moment, the arrival of the great seer Parāśara near them; Parāśara's reviving him from the faint by sprinkling water sanctified by mantras over the king; then, upon being entreated by the king, the sage Parāśara's imparting to the king the one-syllable Rāma mantra along with explaining the means of undertaking a pilgrimage to the sacred ford named Maṅgala located at Śrī Rāmasetu; upon the sage's instruction, King Manojava's going to Maṅgala-tīrtha with his wife and son and performing the observance of worship with the mantra for forty days, before whom from the Maṅgala sacred ford there manifested a bow, quivers, sword, shield, mace, pestle, conch, a chariot equipped with horses, driver, and flags, golden armor, and all other royal ornaments and appurtenances; then Manojava's presenting all those items to the sage Parāśara; then the sage Parāśara's consecrating King Manojava with mantras and giving him blessings accompanied by the transmission of weapon-lore such as the Brahmāstra; then King Manojava's returning to his city, slaying King Golabha with the Brahmāstra, regaining his kingdom, and governing righteously; finally, after reaching Maṅgala-tīrtha and casting off his body, the description of King Manojava's attainment of Śiva's world... 23 2

3.1.s: 13 athaikāntarāmanāthākhyakṣetravarṇanam, tatrāmṛtavāpikātīrthamāhātmyam, tatprasaṃgenāga-styānujavṛttāntavarṇanam, himavatparvate'gastyānujena tapakaraṇam, tattapastuṣṭasya śaṃkarasya prādurbhāve'gastyānujena śivastutikaraṇam, tatastuṣṭasya śivasya vacanā-dagastyānujasya dakṣiṇodadhisthagandhamādanaparvatoparyekāntarāmanāthakṣetravartini tīrthe snānaṃ kṛtvā samādhiyogena muktiprāptyā'maratvāttasya tīrthasyāmṛtavāpītināmaprathā varṇanam, athaikāntarāmanāthakṣetraprathākāraṇakathanaprasaṅgena śrīrāmacandrasya lakṣmaṇena sahaikāntasthitipūrvakaṃ samudrataraṇopāyavicintanavṛttāntavarṇanam, ekāntarāghava-māhātmyam................. 26 1
3.1.d: 13 अथैकान्तरामनाथाख्यक्षेत्रवर्णनम्, तत्रामृतवापिकातीर्थमाहात्म्यम्, तत्प्रसंगेनाग-स्त्यानुजवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, हिमवत्पर्वतेऽगस्त्यानुजेन तपकरणम्, तत्तपस्तुष्टस्य शंकरस्य प्रादुर्भावेऽगस्त्यानुजेन शिवस्तुतिकरणम्, ततस्तुष्टस्य शिवस्य वचना-दगस्त्यानुजस्य दक्षिणोदधिस्थगन्धमादनपर्वतोपर्येकान्तरामनाथक्षेत्रवर्तिनि तीर्थे स्नानं कृत्वा समाधियोगेन मुक्तिप्राप्त्याऽमरत्वात्तस्य तीर्थस्यामृतवापीतिनामप्रथा वर्णनम्, अथैकान्तरामनाथक्षेत्रप्रथाकारणकथनप्रसङ्गेन श्रीरामचन्द्रस्य लक्ष्मणेन सहैकान्तस्थितिपूर्वकं समुद्रतरणोपायविचिन्तनवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, एकान्तराघव-माहात्म्यम्................. 26 1
3.1.m: 13. Now, description of the sacred field named Ekāntarāmanātha. Therein, the māhātmya of the Amṛtavāpikā sacred ford. In that connection, account of the younger brother of Agastya: the performance of austerity by Agastya's younger brother on Mount Himavat; upon the manifestation of Śaṃkara, who was pleased with that austerity, the singing of Śiva's praise by Agastya's younger brother; then, by the word of the gratified Śiva, Agastya's younger brother's taking a ritual ablution in the sacred ford situated in the Ekāntarāmanātha sacred field on Mount Gandhamādana by the southern ocean, and attaining liberation through the yoga of samādhi, whereby, due to [his] immortality, the renown of the name of that sacred ford as 'Amṛtavāpī' is described; then, in connection with explaining the origin of the renown of the Ekāntarāmanātha sacred field, the account of Śrī Rāmacandra's staying in solitude with Lakṣmaṇa and pondering the means of crossing the ocean; the māhātmya of Ekāntarāghava... 26 1

3.1.s: 14 atha dakṣiṇodadhisthagandhamādanavartibrahmakuṇḍamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgenabrahmakuṇḍastha-bhasmanā tripuṇḍradhāraṇasya māhātmyam, brahmakuṇḍotpattivṛttāntaḥ, tatra brahmaviṣṇvo-rmadhye śraiṣṭhayaviṣaye parasparaṃ vivāde samutpanne tayormadhye bhagavato'nādyantaliṅga- prādurbhāvaḥ, tadūrdhvādho'ntaparyantaśodhanārthaṃ brahmaviṣṇvorhaṃsavarāharūpadhāraṇapūrvakaṃ gamanam, liṅgasyādhaḥparyantamadṛṣṭvā svapūrvasthānaṃ pratyāgatena viṣṇunā satyavācā liṅgaparyantādarśanakathanam, brahmaṇordhvaparyantamadṛṣṭvā pratyāgatenāpi cchadmanā mithyā liṅgaparyantadarśanakathanam, atha tanmithyābhāṣaṇaprakupitena śaṃkareṇa liṅgamadhyā-tprādurbhūya brahmaṇe'pūjyatvaprāptirūpaśāpapradānam, tato brahmaṇā stutena śaṅkareṇa brahmaṇe mithyādoṣapraśāṃtyartha dakṣiṇodadhisthagandhamādanaparvate yāgārthamājñākaraṇam, śaṃkarājñayā brahmaṇo gandhamādanaparvate śivamuddiśya yāgakaraṇam, tatra prādurbhūtene-śvareṇa brahmaṇe śrautasmārtakarmapūjyatvarūpavarapradānapūrvaka brahmakuṇḍābhidhatīrthāya vara-pradānam , brahmakuṇḍamāhātmyam..... 27 1
3.1.d: 14 अथ दक्षिणोदधिस्थगन्धमादनवर्तिब्रह्मकुण्डमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेनब्रह्मकुण्डस्थ-भस्मना त्रिपुण्ड्रधारणस्य माहात्म्यम्, ब्रह्मकुण्डोत्पत्तिवृत्तान्तः, तत्र ब्रह्मविष्ण्वो-र्मध्ये श्रैष्ठयविषये परस्परं विवादे समुत्पन्ने तयोर्मध्ये भगवतोऽनाद्यन्तलिङ्ग- प्रादुर्भावः, तदूर्ध्वाधोऽन्तपर्यन्तशोधनार्थं ब्रह्मविष्ण्वोर्हंसवराहरूपधारणपूर्वकं गमनम्, लिङ्गस्याधःपर्यन्तमदृष्ट्वा स्वपूर्वस्थानं प्रत्यागतेन विष्णुना सत्यवाचा लिङ्गपर्यन्तादर्शनकथनम्, ब्रह्मणोर्ध्वपर्यन्तमदृष्ट्वा प्रत्यागतेनापि च्छद्मना मिथ्या लिङ्गपर्यन्तदर्शनकथनम्, अथ तन्मिथ्याभाषणप्रकुपितेन शंकरेण लिङ्गमध्या-त्प्रादुर्भूय ब्रह्मणेऽपूज्यत्वप्राप्तिरूपशापप्रदानम्, ततो ब्रह्मणा स्तुतेन शङ्करेण ब्रह्मणे मिथ्यादोषप्रशांत्यर्थ दक्षिणोदधिस्थगन्धमादनपर्वते यागार्थमाज्ञाकरणम्, शंकराज्ञया ब्रह्मणो गन्धमादनपर्वते शिवमुद्दिश्य यागकरणम्, तत्र प्रादुर्भूतेने-श्वरेण ब्रह्मणे श्रौतस्मार्तकर्मपूज्यत्वरूपवरप्रदानपूर्वक ब्रह्मकुण्डाभिधतीर्थाय वर-प्रदानम् , ब्रह्मकुण्डमाहात्म्यम्..... 27 1
3.1.m: 14. Now, description of the māhātmya of Brahmakuṇḍa situated on Gandhamādana by the southern ocean. In that connection, the māhātmya of bearing the tripuṇḍra mark with the ashes from Brahmakuṇḍa; the account of the origin of Brahmakuṇḍa: there, when a dispute arose between Brahmā and Viṣṇu concerning their superiority to each other, the manifestation between the two of the Lord's beginningless and endless liṅga; the going forth of Brahmā and Viṣṇu in the forms of a swan and a boar to explore the top and bottom extremities of it; Viṣṇu, returning to his former place without having seen the bottom extremity of the liṅga, speaking the truth that he did not see the end of the liṅga; Brahmā, though having returned without seeing the upper extremity, deceitfully and falsely claiming that he saw the end of the liṅga; then Śaṃkara, enraged by that falsehood, appearing from within the liṅga and pronouncing a curse upon Brahmā in the form of forfeiting eligibility for worship; then Śaṃkara, praised by Brahmā, instructing Brahmā to perform a sacrificial rite on Mount Gandhamādana situated by the southern ocean for the pacification of the sin of falsehood; by Śaṃkara's order, Brahmā's performing a sacrificial rite dedicated to Śiva on Mount Gandhamādana; Īśvara, manifesting there, granting Brahmā the boon of being worthy of worship in Vedic and Smārta rituals, and granting a boon to the sacred ford named Brahmakuṇḍa; the māhātmya of Brahmakuṇḍa... 27 1

3.1.s: 15 atha hanumatkuṃḍamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena dharmasakhākhyarājacaritavarṇanam, dharma-sakhanṛpatiputrasya sucandrasya vṛścikadaṃśavṛttāṃtaḥ, atha bahuputratvamākāṃkṣamāṇena dharmasakhākhyamahīpatinā nijartvigvacanato yajñasāmagrīṃ saṃpādya svapatnībhiḥ sarva-parijanairṛtvigbhiśca saha dakṣiṇodadhitīrastha gandhamādanaparvatavarti hanumatkuṇḍaṃ pratigamanam, tatra snātvā putrīyeṣṭiṃ ca kṛtvā hutocchiṣṭaṃ prāśya brāhmaṇebhyo grāmā-grahārādikaṃ dattvā bhāryāśatena sahāvabhṛthasnānaṃ kṛtvā svapurīṃ prati pratyā-gamanam, tatra hanumatkuṇḍaprabhāvāttasya dharmasakhasya śatabhāryāsu śataputraprāptiḥ, athāntakāle hanumatkuṇḍamabhyetya dharmasakhena rājñā tapaḥkaraṇam, tatastasya vaikuṇṭhalokāvāptiḥ, tatputreṇa sucandreṇa pituraurdhvadaihikakarmakaraṇam, sucandrādīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ putrāṇāṃ saubhrātrapūrvakaṃ rājyasukhabhogavarṇanam, hanūmatkuṇḍamāhātmyam... 28 2
3.1.d: 15 अथ हनुमत्कुंडमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन धर्मसखाख्यराजचरितवर्णनम्, धर्म-सखनृपतिपुत्रस्य सुचन्द्रस्य वृश्चिकदंशवृत्तांतः, अथ बहुपुत्रत्वमाकांक्षमाणेन धर्मसखाख्यमहीपतिना निजर्त्विग्वचनतो यज्ञसामग्रीं संपाद्य स्वपत्नीभिः सर्व-परिजनैरृत्विग्भिश्च सह दक्षिणोदधितीरस्थ गन्धमादनपर्वतवर्ति हनुमत्कुण्डं प्रतिगमनम्, तत्र स्नात्वा पुत्रीयेष्टिं च कृत्वा हुतोच्छिष्टं प्राश्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ग्रामा-ग्रहारादिकं दत्त्वा भार्याशतेन सहावभृथस्नानं कृत्वा स्वपुरीं प्रति प्रत्या-गमनम्, तत्र हनुमत्कुण्डप्रभावात्तस्य धर्मसखस्य शतभार्यासु शतपुत्रप्राप्तिः, अथान्तकाले हनुमत्कुण्डमभ्येत्य धर्मसखेन राज्ञा तपःकरणम्, ततस्तस्य वैकुण्ठलोकावाप्तिः, तत्पुत्रेण सुचन्द्रेण पितुरौर्ध्वदैहिककर्मकरणम्, सुचन्द्रादीनां सर्वेषां पुत्राणां सौभ्रात्रपूर्वकं राज्यसुखभोगवर्णनम्, हनूमत्कुण्डमाहात्म्यम्... 28 2
3.1.m: 15. Now, description of the māhātmya of Hanumatkuṇḍa. In that connection, description of the deeds of the king named Dharmasakha: the account of the scorpion sting of Sucandra, son of King Dharmasakha; then, the sovereign named Dharmasakha, desiring many sons, assembling sacrificial materials upon the counsel of his priests, and departing with his wives, all attendants, and priests to Hanumatkuṇḍa situated on Mount Gandhamādana on the shore of the southern ocean; there, having bathed, performed the rite for obtaining offspring, consumed the sacrificial remnants, granted villages, land endowments, and the like to brahmins, and performed the concluding ablution with his hundred wives, his returning to his capital city; there, through the power of Hanumatkuṇḍa, that Dharmasakha's obtaining a hundred sons through his hundred wives; then, at the end of his life, King Dharmasakha's coming to Hanumatkuṇḍa and performing austerity; then his attainment of the realm of Vaikuṇṭha; the performance of the father's funeral rites by his son Sucandra; description of all the sons, Sucandra and the rest, enjoying the happiness of kingship with fraternal affection; the māhātmya of Hanūmatkuṇḍa... 28 2

3.1.s: 16 athāgastitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tanmāhātmyaprasaṃgena dīrghatamomuniputrasya kakṣīvataśca-ritravarṇanam tatrodaṃkākhyasya gurorgṛhe kakṣīvatā ṣaṣṭivarṣaparyantaṃ vidyābhyāsaṃ kṛtvā gṛhaṃ pratyāgantuṃ guroḥ prārthanākaraṇam , tatastadguruṇā tasyodvāhāyopāyakathanam, gurvājñayā kakṣīvatā'gastyatīrthe snātvā tasmāttīrthādudgataṃ caturdantaṃ śubhraṃ gajendra-māruhya madhyemārgameva militena svanayākhyena rājñā saha tasya puraṃ prati gamanam, tataḥ svanayena rājñā kakṣīvate svakanyāyāḥ pradānāya tadvacanāttatpiturdīrghatamasaḥ sudarśanākhyapurodhodvārā''mantraṇaṃ kṛtvā satkārapūrvakaṃ svapuraṃ pratyānayanam, dīrgha-tamasaṃ pitaraṃ prati kakṣīvatā'bhivādanam, nijavidyādhyayanavṛttāntanivedanaṃ ca.... 30 1
3.1.d: 16 अथागस्तितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तन्माहात्म्यप्रसंगेन दीर्घतमोमुनिपुत्रस्य कक्षीवतश्च-रित्रवर्णनम् तत्रोदंकाख्यस्य गुरोर्गृहे कक्षीवता षष्टिवर्षपर्यन्तं विद्याभ्यासं कृत्वा गृहं प्रत्यागन्तुं गुरोः प्रार्थनाकरणम् , ततस्तद्गुरुणा तस्योद्वाहायोपायकथनम्, गुर्वाज्ञया कक्षीवताऽगस्त्यतीर्थे स्नात्वा तस्मात्तीर्थादुद्गतं चतुर्दन्तं शुभ्रं गजेन्द्र-मारुह्य मध्येमार्गमेव मिलितेन स्वनयाख्येन राज्ञा सह तस्य पुरं प्रति गमनम्, ततः स्वनयेन राज्ञा कक्षीवते स्वकन्यायाः प्रदानाय तद्वचनात्तत्पितुर्दीर्घतमसः सुदर्शनाख्यपुरोधोद्वारा'ऽमन्त्रणं कृत्वा सत्कारपूर्वकं स्वपुरं प्रत्यानयनम्, दीर्घ-तमसं पितरं प्रति कक्षीवताऽभिवादनम्, निजविद्याध्ययनवृत्तान्तनिवेदनं च.... 30 1
3.1.m: 16. Now follows the description of the māhātmya of Agastitīrtha. In connection with that māhātmya, the account of Kakṣīvat, son of the sage Dīrghatamas, is described: there Kakṣīvat, having pursued the study of sacred lore for sixty years in the home of his guru named Udaṅka, requested the guru to return home; then the guru told him the means for his marriage; Kakṣīvat, by order of his guru, having taken a ritual ablution at Agastitīrtha, mounted a white lord of elephants with four tusks that emerged from that sacred ford, and met King Svanaya along the way, going with him to his city; then King Svanaya, wishing to give his daughter to Kakṣīvat, upon his word invited Kakṣīvat's father Dīrghatamas through the priest named Sudarśana and brought him with honor to his city; Kakṣīvat saluted his father Dīrghatamas and reported the account of his own study of sacred lore. ... [Chapters] 30–31.

3.1.s: 17 atha tasminnagastitīrthe svanayena rājñā dīrghatamāmuneḥ satkārakaraṇam atrāṃtara eva tatrāgastitīrthe snātuṃ saśiṣyasamūhasyodaṅkamaharṣerāgamanam , udaṅkadīrghatamasoḥ samā-gamaḥ, athedaṅkadarśanārthaṃ svanayena rājñā''gatya nijoddeśanivedanam, athodaṅkena saha dīrghatamaso svanayasya rājñā kakṣīvate nijakanyāpradānasyānumodanam, tataḥ svanayena rājñā madhurāpurītaḥ svaparicārakaiḥ kanyāmānīya vivāhavidhinā kakṣīvate kanyādānakaraṇam, tataḥ svarṇagodāsīgrāmādivipulavaivāhikaprābhṛtapradānam, atha dīrghatamaso munestatsarvamādāya putreṇa snuṣayā ca saha vedāraṇyasthita svāśramaṃ pratyāgamanam, svanayena rājñā'ntaḥpuraiḥ sahāgastitīrthe snātvā svapuraṃ prati gamanam, agastitīrthamāhātmyam........... 32 1
3.1.d: 17 अथ तस्मिन्नगस्तितीर्थे स्वनयेन राज्ञा दीर्घतमामुनेः सत्कारकरणम् अत्रांतर एव तत्रागस्तितीर्थे स्नातुं सशिष्यसमूहस्योदङ्कमहर्षेरागमनम् , उदङ्कदीर्घतमसोः समा-गमः, अथेदङ्कदर्शनार्थं स्वनयेन राज्ञा'ऽगत्य निजोद्देशनिवेदनम्, अथोदङ्केन सह दीर्घतमसो स्वनयस्य राज्ञा कक्षीवते निजकन्याप्रदानस्यानुमोदनम्, ततः स्वनयेन राज्ञा मधुरापुरीतः स्वपरिचारकैः कन्यामानीय विवाहविधिना कक्षीवते कन्यादानकरणम्, ततः स्वर्णगोदासीग्रामादिविपुलवैवाहिकप्राभृतप्रदानम्, अथ दीर्घतमसो मुनेस्तत्सर्वमादाय पुत्रेण स्नुषया च सह वेदारण्यस्थित स्वाश्रमं प्रत्यागमनम्, स्वनयेन राज्ञाऽन्तःपुरैः सहागस्तितीर्थे स्नात्वा स्वपुरं प्रति गमनम्, अगस्तितीर्थमाहात्म्यम्........... 32 1
3.1.m: 17. Now follows the honoring of the sage Dīrghatamas by King Svanaya at that Agastitīrtha; right then the arrival at Agastitīrtha of the great seer Udaṅka with the assembly of his disciples to bathe; the meeting of Udaṅka and Dīrghatamas; then King Svanaya's coming to see Udaṅka and stating his intention; then Dīrghatamas's consent, together with Udaṅka, to King Svanaya's giving his daughter to Kakṣīvat; then King Svanaya, having brought the maiden from the city of Mathurā by his attendants, bestowed his daughter upon Kakṣīvat according to the marriage rite; then the gifting of vast bridal dowries of gold, cows, female slaves, villages, and the like; then the sage Dīrghatamas, taking all that, returned with his son and daughter-in-law to his own hermitage situated in Vedāraṇya; King Svanaya, having bathed at Agastitīrtha together with his harem, went to his own city. The māhātmya of Agastitīrtha. ... [Chapter] 32.

3.1.s: 18 atha rāmakuṇḍākhyatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgenāgastyaśiṣyasutīkṣṇamunītihāsa-varṇanam, rāmacandrasarastīrthe tapastapatā sutīkṣṇena śrīrāmacandrastutikaraṇam, evaṃ tapastapataḥ sutīkṣṇasyālaukikatapaḥsiddhivarṇanaprasaṃgena rāmakuṇḍamāhātmyavarṇanam, rāmakuṇḍatīre rāmasthāpitaśrīśivaliṅgamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena dharmaputrasya yudhiṣṭhirasyāsatyabhāṣaṇadoṣanivṛttivṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra bhāratayuddhe droṇaṃ jetuṃ keśavena bhīmadvārā 'aśvatthāmā yuddhe hataḥ iti mṛṣā pravādaprasaraṇam, taṃ pravāda-mākarṇya droṇena yudhiṣṭhirādapi tathaiveti śrutvā satyaṃ matvā yogena svatanutyāga-karaṇam, tasminkāle sadaiva satyabhāṣiṇo yudhiṣṭhirasya mṛṣāpravādajanitapātaka-prāptiḥ, tasya ca yuddhasamāptyanantaraṃ rājyābhiṣekasamaye nabhovāṇyā cchadmanā'-satyabhāṣaṇajanitapātakena rājyābhiṣekānarhatākathanam, yudhiṣṭhireṇa paścāttāpakara-ṇam, tasminnavasare samāgatena vyāsamaharṣiṇā yudhiṣṭhiraṃ prati dakṣiṇodadhitīrastha-rāmatīrthe snānārthamupadeśakaraṇam, tato yudhiṣṭhireṇa nijakaniṣṭhabandhuṃ sahadevaṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpya dhaumyenopādhyāyena bhīmādibhirnijānujaiśca saha rāmasetuṃ samuddiśya vāhanārohaṇaṃ vinā yātrāvidhinā rāmatīrtha samāsādya purohitoktamārgeṇa snāna- karaṇam, tena rāmatīrthasnānadānaśrāddhamāsopavāsādiprabhāveṇa nabhovāṇyā yudhi-ṣṭhirasyāsatyabhāṣaṇajanita pātakanivṛttipūrvaka rājyārohaṇayogyatāvarṇanam rāmaku-ṇḍākhyatīrthamāhātmyam . 33 1
3.1.d: 18 अथ रामकुण्डाख्यतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेनागस्त्यशिष्यसुतीक्ष्णमुनीतिहास-वर्णनम्, रामचन्द्रसरस्तीर्थे तपस्तपता सुतीक्ष्णेन श्रीरामचन्द्रस्तुतिकरणम्, एवं तपस्तपतः सुतीक्ष्णस्यालौकिकतपःसिद्धिवर्णनप्रसंगेन रामकुण्डमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, रामकुण्डतीरे रामस्थापितश्रीशिवलिङ्गमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन धर्मपुत्रस्य युधिष्ठिरस्यासत्यभाषणदोषनिवृत्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र भारतयुद्धे द्रोणं जेतुं केशवेन भीमद्वारा ऽअश्वत्थामा युद्धे हतः इति मृषा प्रवादप्रसरणम्, तं प्रवाद-माकर्ण्य द्रोणेन युधिष्ठिरादपि तथैवेति श्रुत्वा सत्यं मत्वा योगेन स्वतनुत्याग-करणम्, तस्मिन्काले सदैव सत्यभाषिणो युधिष्ठिरस्य मृषाप्रवादजनितपातक-प्राप्तिः, तस्य च युद्धसमाप्त्यनन्तरं राज्याभिषेकसमये नभोवाण्या च्छद्मना'-सत्यभाषणजनितपातकेन राज्याभिषेकानर्हताकथनम्, युधिष्ठिरेण पश्चात्तापकर-णम्, तस्मिन्नवसरे समागतेन व्यासमहर्षिणा युधिष्ठिरं प्रति दक्षिणोदधितीरस्थ-रामतीर्थे स्नानार्थमुपदेशकरणम्, ततो युधिष्ठिरेण निजकनिष्ठबन्धुं सहदेवं राज्ये प्रतिष्ठाप्य धौम्येनोपाध्यायेन भीमादिभिर्निजानुजैश्च सह रामसेतुं समुद्दिश्य वाहनारोहणं विना यात्राविधिना रामतीर्थ समासाद्य पुरोहितोक्तमार्गेण स्नान- करणम्, तेन रामतीर्थस्नानदानश्राद्धमासोपवासादिप्रभावेण नभोवाण्या युधि-ष्ठिरस्यासत्यभाषणजनित पातकनिवृत्तिपूर्वक राज्यारोहणयोग्यतावर्णनम् रामकु-ण्डाख्यतीर्थमाहात्म्यम् . 33 1
3.1.m: 18. Now follows the description of the māhātmya of the sacred ford named Rāmakuṇḍa. In connection with that, the description of the legend of the sage Sutīkṣṇa, a disciple of Agastya: the hymn of praise to the venerable Rāmacandra by Sutīkṣṇa as he performed austerity at the sacred ford of Rāmacandrasaras; in connection with describing such extraordinary perfection in austerity of Sutīkṣṇa as he performed austerity, the description of the māhātmya of Rāmakuṇḍa; the description of the māhātmya of the venerable Śivaliṅga established by Rāma on the bank of Rāmakuṇḍa; in connection with that, the description of the account of the removal of the fault of telling an untruth by Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma: there, in the Bhārata war, in order to defeat Droṇa, a false rumor was spread by Keśava through Bhīma that 'Aśvatthāman has been slain in battle'; hearing that rumor, Droṇa, hearing likewise even from Yudhiṣṭhira, believed it to be true and relinquished his own body through yoga; at that time, sin generated from a false statement attached to Yudhiṣṭhira, who was always a speaker of truth; and after the conclusion of the war, at the time of his royal consecration, a voice from the sky declared his unfitness for royal consecration due to the sin arising from speaking an untruth deceitfully; Yudhiṣṭhira felt remorse; on that occasion the great seer Vyāsa arrived and instructed Yudhiṣṭhira to bathe in the Rāmatīrtha situated on the shore of the southern ocean; then Yudhiṣṭhira, having established his youngest brother Sahadeva on the throne, set out for Rāmasetu without mounting a chariot or mount, accompanied by his preceptor Dhaumya and his younger brothers headed by Bhīma, following the prescribed rules of pilgrimage; having reached Rāmatīrtha, he performed his ritual ablution according to the path instructed by the family priest; thereby, through the power of the ritual ablution, gifts, ancestral rites, month-long fasts, and other acts at Rāmatīrtha, a voice from the sky described the removal of Yudhiṣṭhira's sin born of untruthful speech and his eligibility to ascend the throne. The māhātmya of the sacred ford named Rāmakuṇḍa. ... [Chapters] 33–34.

3.1.s: 19 atha lakṣmaṇatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena balabhadra brahmahatyā vimuktivṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra kauravapāṃḍavavadhaṃ draṣṭumanicchato balabhadrasya tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena naimiṣā-raṇye maharṣisamāje gamanam, tatra balabhadreṇa purāṇakathanāyoccabrahmāsane sthitasya sūtasyāvicārya nijahastotsṛṣṭakuśāgreṇa hananādbrahmahatyāprāptiḥ, atha munīnāṃ vaca-nena lokasaṃgrahāya prāyaścittacikīrṣayā munīnprati prārthanam, munibhirbalabhadrāya balvalākhyarākṣasavadhaṃ kṛtvā varṣaparyantaṃ tīrthayātrākaraṇarūpaprāyaścittakathanam, atha balabhadreṇa balvalanāmakarākṣasahananam, tato varṣaparyantaṃ bhūtalasya sarvatīrtheṣu snāna-pūrvakaṃ yātrākaraṇama, kṛtāyāmapi tīrthayātrāyāṃ brahmahatyāyā nivṛttimadṛṣṭvā muni-vākyena dakṣiṇodadhistha gandhamādanavarti lakṣmaṇatīrthe gatvā snānamātreṇa lakṣmaṇe-śvaraliṃgadarśanena ca brahmahatyāto vimuktivarṇanam , lakṣmaṇatīrthamāhātmyama.... 35 2
3.1.d: 19 अथ लक्ष्मणतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन बलभद्र ब्रह्महत्या विमुक्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र कौरवपांडववधं द्रष्टुमनिच्छतो बलभद्रस्य तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगेन नैमिषा-रण्ये महर्षिसमाजे गमनम्, तत्र बलभद्रेण पुराणकथनायोच्चब्रह्मासने स्थितस्य सूतस्याविचार्य निजहस्तोत्सृष्टकुशाग्रेण हननाद्ब्रह्महत्याप्राप्तिः, अथ मुनीनां वच-नेन लोकसंग्रहाय प्रायश्चित्तचिकीर्षया मुनीन्प्रति प्रार्थनम्, मुनिभिर्बलभद्राय बल्वलाख्यराक्षसवधं कृत्वा वर्षपर्यन्तं तीर्थयात्राकरणरूपप्रायश्चित्तकथनम्, अथ बलभद्रेण बल्वलनामकराक्षसहननम्, ततो वर्षपर्यन्तं भूतलस्य सर्वतीर्थेषु स्नान-पूर्वकं यात्राकरणम, कृतायामपि तीर्थयात्रायां ब्रह्महत्याया निवृत्तिमदृष्ट्वा मुनि-वाक्येन दक्षिणोदधिस्थ गन्धमादनवर्ति लक्ष्मणतीर्थे गत्वा स्नानमात्रेण लक्ष्मणे-श्वरलिंगदर्शनेन च ब्रह्महत्यातो विमुक्तिवर्णनम् , लक्ष्मणतीर्थमाहात्म्यम.... 35 2
3.1.m: 19. Now follows the description of the māhātmya of Lakṣmaṇatīrtha. In connection with that, the description of the account of Balabhadra's release from the sin of killing a brahmin: there Balabhadra, not wishing to see the slaughter of the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas, went on a pilgrimage to sacred fords and came to the assembly of great seers in Naimiṣāraṇya; there, through the killing of Sūta, who was seated on the high seat of Brahmā to narrate the Purāṇas, by the tip of a kuśa grass blade hurled from his hand without reflection, Balabhadra incurred the sin of killing a brahmin; then, according to the word of the sages and desiring to perform an expiation for the welfare of the world, he entreated the sages; the sages prescribed for Balabhadra an expiation consisting of slaying the rākṣasa named Balvala and undertaking a pilgrimage to sacred fords for a whole year; then Balabhadra slew the rākṣasa named Balvala; thereafter, for a whole year, he went on a pilgrimage, taking ritual ablutions in all sacred fords throughout the earth; even though the pilgrimage to sacred fords was completed, not seeing the cessation of the sin of killing a brahmin, he went by the sages' instruction to Lakṣmaṇatīrtha situated on Mount Gandhamādana in the southern ocean; through mere ritual ablution and the darśana of the Lakṣmaṇeśvaraliṅga, his deliverance from the sin of killing a brahmin is described. The māhātmya of Lakṣmaṇatīrtha. ... [Chapters] 35–36.

3.1.s: 20 atha jaṭātīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṅgena śukācāryacaritravarṇanam, tatra śukena vyāsaṃ prati cittaśuddhyarthamupāye pṛṣṭe sati vyāsena bhṛguvaruṇetihāsakathanapūrvakaṃ rāmasetustha jaṭātīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam tataḥ śukasya vyāsopadeśaṃ śrutvā jaṭātīrthaṃ gatvā snānamātreṇa manaḥśuddhivarṇanam, jaṭātīrthamāhātmyam .. 37 1
3.1.d: 20 अथ जटातीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसङ्गेन शुकाचार्यचरित्रवर्णनम्, तत्र शुकेन व्यासं प्रति चित्तशुद्ध्यर्थमुपाये पृष्टे सति व्यासेन भृगुवरुणेतिहासकथनपूर्वकं रामसेतुस्थ जटातीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् ततः शुकस्य व्यासोपदेशं श्रुत्वा जटातीर्थं गत्वा स्नानमात्रेण मनःशुद्धिवर्णनम्, जटातीर्थमाहात्म्यम् .. 37 1
3.1.m: 20. Now follows the description of the māhātmya of Jaṭātīrtha. In connection with that, the description of the life of the teacher Śuka: there, when Śuka inquired of Vyāsa about the means for purifying the mind, Vyāsa described the māhātmya of Jaṭātīrtha situated on Rāmasetu, recounting first the legend of Bhṛgu and Varuṇa; then, having heard the instruction of Vyāsa, Śuka went to Jaṭātīrtha, and the purification of his mind by a mere ritual ablution is described. The māhātmya of Jaṭātīrtha. ... [Chapter] 37.
Jaṭātīrtha Temple

3.1.s: 21 atha lakṣmītīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṅgena yudhiṣṭhiravṛttāntavarṇanam, tatrendraprasthe sthitena yudhiṣṭhireṇa śrīkṛṣṇaṃ prati mahaiśvaryaprāpakadharmaviṣayakapṛcchāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ śrīkṛṣṇena yudhiṣṭhirāyāneketihāsapūrvakaṃ gandhamādanasthalakṣmītīrthamāhātmyakathanam, tato yudhiṣṭhireṇa lakṣmītīrthaṃ gatvā māsaparyantaṃ niyamapūrvakaṃ snānaṃ vidhāya svapuraṃ pratyāgatya tatastatprabhāveṇa saṃprāpta niratiśaya saṃpadaiśvaryavaśānmahatā samārambheṇa śrīkṛṣṇasāhāyyena rājasūyayajñakaraṇam lakṣmītīrthamāhātmyam... .. 38 1
3.1.d: 21 अथ लक्ष्मीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसङ्गेन युधिष्ठिरवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्रेन्द्रप्रस्थे स्थितेन युधिष्ठिरेण श्रीकृष्णं प्रति महैश्वर्यप्रापकधर्मविषयकपृच्छायां कृतायां श्रीकृष्णेन युधिष्ठिरायानेकेतिहासपूर्वकं गन्धमादनस्थलक्ष्मीतीर्थमाहात्म्यकथनम्, ततो युधिष्ठिरेण लक्ष्मीतीर्थं गत्वा मासपर्यन्तं नियमपूर्वकं स्नानं विधाय स्वपुरं प्रत्यागत्य ततस्तत्प्रभावेण संप्राप्त निरतिशय संपदैश्वर्यवशान्महता समारम्भेण श्रीकृष्णसाहाय्येन राजसूययज्ञकरणम् लक्ष्मीतीर्थमाहात्म्यम्... .. 38 1
3.1.m: 21. Now begins the description of the māhātmya of Lakṣmītīrtha. In connection with that, the narrative of Yudhiṣṭhira is described: there, when Yudhiṣṭhira, residing in Indraprastha, questioned Śrī Kṛṣṇa concerning the dharma that brings about supreme sovereignty, Śrī Kṛṣṇa recounted to Yudhiṣṭhira, along with various ancient narratives, the māhātmya of Lakṣmītīrtha situated on Mount Gandhamādana; then, after Yudhiṣṭhira went to Lakṣmītīrtha and performed ritual ablutions according to the prescribed rules for a whole month, he returned to his own city, and by the power thereof, possessing unsurpassable wealth and sovereignty, he performed the Rājasūya sacrifice with great preparations and through the assistance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. [Thus ends] the māhātmya of Lakṣmītīrtha. 38. 1.

3.1.s: 22 athāgnitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena sītāśuddhivṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra rāmaca-ndreṇa laṃkāyāṃ rāvaṇaṃ hatvā śakrādibhiḥ saha setumārgeṇa gandhamādanaṃ pratyāgatya lakṣmītīrthataṭe sthitvā jānakīśodhanāyāgnerāhvānakaraṇam, tato'gninā tatra same-tya rāmasyāgre sītāyāḥ śuddhatākathanam, agnivacanādrāmacandreṇa jānakyāḥ svīka-raṇam, agnervinirgamasthānasyāgnitīrthābhidhayā prasiddhiḥ, agnitīrthamāhātmyaprasaṃge-na paśumannāmadheyasya vaṇigvarasya caritravaṇarnam, tatra tasya paśumato'ṣṭaputreṣu madhye'-ṣṭamaputrasya duṣpaṇyākhyasya nagarasthabālakamāraṇarūpātiduṣkarmaparasya rājñā tatpituḥ sacchīlaṃ nirīkṣya deśānnirvāsanam , tato vanaṃ prayātenāpi tenograśravomuniputre jale nimajjya mārite satyugraśravasā muninā duṣpaṇyāya jalanimajjanataste mṛtyurbha-viṣyatīti śāpapradānam, atha varṣākāle'tivṛṣṭau satyāṃ duṣpaṇyena mṛtapatita-gajaśarīramadhye praveśe kṛte tasya gajaśarīrasya mahatā payapūrapravāheṇa samudraṃ prati praveśe sati tadantaḥsthitasya duṣpaṇyasya mṛtyuḥ, tadanaṃtaraṃ tasya piśācatvaprāptiḥ, tataḥ piśācarūpiṇā tenāgastyāśramasamīpaṃ pratyabhyetyoccaiḥ svamuktaye maharṣīṇāṃ prārthanākaraṇam, atha tasya vimuktaye'gastyamaharṣiṇā sutīkṣṇākhyaṃ svaśiṣyaṃ prati taduddeśenāgnitīrthe snānārthamājñākaraṇam, sutīkṣṇena piśācasya vimuktyuddeśenā-gnitīrthe snāne kṛte sati duṣpaṇyasya piśācatvavimuktipūrvakaṃ divyaṃ vimānamāruhya maharṣīṃnnamaskṛtya divyalokaṃ prati gamanam , agnitīrthamāhātmyam..... 39 2
3.1.d: 22 अथाग्नितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेन सीताशुद्धिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र रामच-न्द्रेण लंकायां रावणं हत्वा शक्रादिभिः सह सेतुमार्गेण गन्धमादनं प्रत्यागत्य लक्ष्मीतीर्थतटे स्थित्वा जानकीशोधनायाग्नेराह्वानकरणम्, ततोऽग्निना तत्र समे-त्य रामस्याग्रे सीतायाः शुद्धताकथनम्, अग्निवचनाद्रामचन्द्रेण जानक्याः स्वीक-रणम्, अग्नेर्विनिर्गमस्थानस्याग्नितीर्थाभिधया प्रसिद्धिः, अग्नितीर्थमाहात्म्यप्रसंगे-न पशुमन्नामधेयस्य वणिग्वरस्य चरित्रवणर्नम्, तत्र तस्य पशुमतोऽष्टपुत्रेषु मध्ये'-ष्टमपुत्रस्य दुष्पण्याख्यस्य नगरस्थबालकमारणरूपातिदुष्कर्मपरस्य राज्ञा तत्पितुः सच्छीलं निरीक्ष्य देशान्निर्वासनम् , ततो वनं प्रयातेनापि तेनोग्रश्रवोमुनिपुत्रे जले निमज्ज्य मारिते सत्युग्रश्रवसा मुनिना दुष्पण्याय जलनिमज्जनतस्ते मृत्युर्भ-विष्यतीति शापप्रदानम्, अथ वर्षाकालेऽतिवृष्टौ सत्यां दुष्पण्येन मृतपतित-गजशरीरमध्ये प्रवेशे कृते तस्य गजशरीरस्य महता पयपूरप्रवाहेण समुद्रं प्रति प्रवेशे सति तदन्तःस्थितस्य दुष्पण्यस्य मृत्युः, तदनंतरं तस्य पिशाचत्वप्राप्तिः, ततः पिशाचरूपिणा तेनागस्त्याश्रमसमीपं प्रत्यभ्येत्योच्चैः स्वमुक्तये महर्षीणां प्रार्थनाकरणम्, अथ तस्य विमुक्तयेऽगस्त्यमहर्षिणा सुतीक्ष्णाख्यं स्वशिष्यं प्रति तदुद्देशेनाग्नितीर्थे स्नानार्थमाज्ञाकरणम्, सुतीक्ष्णेन पिशाचस्य विमुक्त्युद्देशेना-ग्नितीर्थे स्नाने कृते सति दुष्पण्यस्य पिशाचत्वविमुक्तिपूर्वकं दिव्यं विमानमारुह्य महर्षींन्नमस्कृत्य दिव्यलोकं प्रति गमनम् , अग्नितीर्थमाहात्म्यम्..... 39 2
3.1.m: 22. Now begins the description of the māhātmya of Agnitīrtha. In connection with that, the narrative of Sītā's purification is described: there, after Rāmacandra slew Rāvaṇa in Laṅkā and returned to Gandhamādana via the bridge with Indra and the other [gods], he stood on the bank of Lakṣmītīrtha and summoned Agni to examine Jānakī; then, Agni arrived there and proclaimed Sītā's purity before Rāma; upon Agni's words, Rāmacandra accepted Jānakī; the place from which Agni emerged became famous by the name of Agnitīrtha. In connection with the māhātmya of Agnitīrtha, the story of the excellent merchant named Paśumant is described: there, among the eight sons of that Paśumant, the eighth son named Duṣpaṇya, intent upon extreme evil deeds such as killing boys residing in the city, was exiled from the realm by the king in consideration of his father's virtuous character; then, though he had gone to the forest, he submerged and killed the son of the sage Ugraśravas in the water, whereupon the sage Ugraśravas cursed Duṣpaṇya, saying, 'Your death shall occur through drowning in water'; then, during the rainy season when excessive rain fell, Duṣpaṇya entered inside the body of a fallen, dead elephant; when that elephant's body was carried into the ocean by a great flood of water, Duṣpaṇya within it died; thereafter, he attained the state of a piśāca; then, in the form of a piśāca, he approached the hermitage of Agastya and loudly prayed to the great seers for his liberation; then, for his release, the great seer Agastya instructed his own pupil named Sutīkṣṇa to perform a ritual ablution in Agnitīrtha on his behalf; when Sutīkṣṇa performed the ritual ablution in Agnitīrtha for the sake of the piśāca's liberation, Duṣpaṇya was freed from the state of a piśāca, mounted a celestial aerial chariot, bowed to the great seers, and departed to the celestial realm. [Thus ends] the māhātmya of Agnitīrtha. 39. 2.

3.1.s: 23 atha cakratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgenāhirbudhnyākhyabrāhmaṇakṛta sudarśanopāsanāva-rṇanam , sudarśanacakreṇa tasya brāhmaṇasya tapovighnakāriṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ nāśanam , sudarśanacakrasaṃnidhānāttīrthasya cakratīrthatvena prasiddhiḥ, brahmadevājñayā rākṣasatrastai-ssarvadevaiścakratīrthasaṃnidhau māheśvarayajñakaraṇam, tasminyajñe prāśitrapātrasparśamātrā-cchinnapāṇeḥ saviturdevasyāṣṭāvakramunivacanāccakratīrthe snānamātreṇa hiraṇmayapāṇya-vāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, cakratīrthamāhātmyam ....... . 42 1
3.1.d: 23 अथ चक्रतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेनाहिर्बुध्न्याख्यब्राह्मणकृत सुदर्शनोपासनाव-र्णनम् , सुदर्शनचक्रेण तस्य ब्राह्मणस्य तपोविघ्नकारिणां राक्षसानां नाशनम् , सुदर्शनचक्रसंनिधानात्तीर्थस्य चक्रतीर्थत्वेन प्रसिद्धिः, ब्रह्मदेवाज्ञया राक्षसत्रस्तै-स्सर्वदेवैश्चक्रतीर्थसंनिधौ माहेश्वरयज्ञकरणम्, तस्मिन्यज्ञे प्राशित्रपात्रस्पर्शमात्रा-च्छिन्नपाणेः सवितुर्देवस्याष्टावक्रमुनिवचनाच्चक्रतीर्थे स्नानमात्रेण हिरण्मयपाण्य-वाप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, चक्रतीर्थमाहात्म्यम् ....... . 42 1
3.1.m: 23. Now begins the description of the māhātmya of Cakratīrtha. In connection with that, the worship of Sudarśana performed by the brahmin named Ahirbudhnya is described; the destruction, by the Sudarśana discus, of the rākṣasas who caused obstacles to that brahmin's austerity; the fame of the sacred ford as Cakratīrtha because of the presence of the Sudarśana discus; the performance of a sacrifice to Maheśvara near Cakratīrtha by all the gods who were terrified of the rākṣasas, by command of Lord Brahmā; and the narrative of the god Savitṛ—whose hand was severed at that sacrifice merely upon touching the prāśitra vessel—obtaining a golden hand merely by performing ritual ablutions in Cakratīrtha, in accordance with the words of the sage Aṣṭāvakra. [Thus ends] the māhātmya of Cakratīrtha. 42. 1.

3.1.s: 24 atha śivatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena kālabhairavavṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra brahma-viṣṇvoḥ parasparaṃ śraiṣṭhayaviṣaye vivāde samutpanne praṇavena śivasya śraiṣṭhye varṇite'pi durāgrahavaśādbrahmaviṣṇubhyāṃ śivaśraiṣṭhye'nādṛte sati śivena tejomayasvasvarūpa-prakaṭanam, maheśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmaṇā taṃ pratyapyanādarapūrvakaṃ garvoktisaṃbhāṣaṇam, atha maheśvareṇa brahmāṇaṃ prati kālabhairavākhyapuruṣapreṣaṇam, brahmaṇā saha kālabhairavasya yuddhe kālabhairaveṇa brahmaṇaḥ pañcamaśiraśchedapūrvakaṃ vadhakaraṇam , tato bhagavatā maheśvareṇa brahmaṇaḥ saṃjīvanam, brahmadevena bhagavataḥ śaṅkarasya stutikaraṇam, śaṃkareṇa brahmaṇe'bhayapradānam, atha śivājñayā kālabhairavasya brahmahatyādoṣaviśuddhaye brahma-śiraḥ kare saṃdhārya varṣaparyataṃ samastatīrthayātrākaraṇapūrvakaṃ dakṣiṇāṃbhodhisthagandha-mādanavartiśivatīrthasnānakaraṇādbrahmahatyānivṛttiḥ, tatraiva kālabhairaveṇa kapālasthā-panāttasya śivatīrthasya kapālatīrthatvenābhidhānam, śivatīrthamāhātmyam... 43 1
